Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

Hai la rugiada della tua giovinezza. Salmo 110:3

Ci sono molti aspetti della giovinezza che non sono virtuosi. Molti giovani del nostro tempo attraversano precocemente una stagione di insensibilità, spensieratezza e sventura. Spesso le decisioni prese negli anni della giovinezza gettano le fondamenta per il resto della vita. Fu il fratello minore del prodigo a chiedere di ricevere in anticipo la sua parte di eredità, e poi ad andare a sperperarla vivendo dissolutamente. Fu una giovane Dina ad allontanarsi dalla casa di suo padre e …uscì per vedere le figlie del paese –Genesi 34:1. Là fu esposta ai giovani pagani del paese e provocò un massacro sanguinoso, lasciando Giacobbe come un fetore nel paese. Molti giovani stolti hanno seminato vento e ne hanno raccolto le devastazioni. Coloro che sono privi di solidi principi e dell’autorità dei genitori corrono un alto rischio di naufragio spirituale.

Ci sono particolari concupiscenze che affliggono i giovani più degli anziani, e i giovani sono esortati a fuggirle. (–vedi 2 Timoteo 2:22) Salomone guardò dalla finestra a grata, e vidi tra gli inesperti, scorsi fra i giovani, un giovane privo di senno -Proverbi 7:6-7. Il giovane era alla ricerca appassionata di ciò che appariva bello… [Finché] una freccia gli trapassò il fegato; come un uccello che si precipita nella rete senza sapere che è in gioco la sua vita –Proverbi 7:23. Potremmo esaminare i vizi della giovinezza di Roboamo, Amnon, Nadab e Abiu, e di innumerevoli altri. Non mancano neppure intorno a noi esempi moderni, pieni di follia, messi in atto da giovani frivoli.

Ma i giovani non devono essere disprezzati. Nessuno disprezzi la tua giovane età; ma sii d’esempio ai credenti, nel parlare, nella condotta, nell’amore, nello spirito, nella fede, nella purezza –1 Timoteo 4:12. In effetti, in genere Dio sceglie i giovani come strumenti per la diffusione del suo messaggio. Giuseppe, uomo di carattere integerrimo, fu mandato da Dio in Egitto all’età di 17 anni per conservare la vita (–vedi Genesi 45:5). Miriam, all’età di dodici anni, vegliò sul futuro liberatore dell’intera nazione ebraica e fece in modo che sua madre, Iochebed, fosse la nutrice del piccolo Mosè. Davide, da giovane, fu mandato a incoraggiare i suoi fratelli nell’esercito. I suoi fratelli lo disprezzarono: …Conosco la tua superbia e la malizia del tuo cuore… –1 Samuele 17:28. Saul lo respinse: …Tu non puoi andare a combattere contro questo Filisteo, perché sei ancora un ragazzo… –1 Samuele 17:33. Golia lo schernì: …Sono forse un cane, che tu vieni contro di me con dei bastoni… –1 Samuele 17:43. Ma il loro disprezzo fu del tutto vano quando Dio lo scelse come re su tutto Israele.

Queste nobili aspirazioni giovanili furono seguite da Giosia, Isaia, Geremia, Daniele, Maria e dai discepoli del Signore, tutti decisi a ricordarsi del loro Creatore nei giorni della giovinezza. Ma non erano esempi ingenui, intenti a garantirsi un posto nella vita: erano esempi eloquenti di giovani che cercavano di imitare l’immagine del loro Signore.

Non dobbiamo scrutare a lungo il carattere di Cristo prima di trovare…

...Hai la rugiada della tua giovinezza

Il Salmo 110 è forse il passo più citato dell’Antico Testamento. Questo ritratto retorico del Messia rivela una virtù vivida da contemplare. Cristo, quale Antico di giorni, viene descritto nell’Apocalisse con il capo e i capelli… bianchi come lana, bianchi come neve… –Apocalisse 1:14; eppure qui è raffigurato eternamente giovane, mentre siede alla destra di Dio (–vedi Salmo 110:1). Là non può entrare alcuna stanchezza dovuta all’età, perché Cristo è la Stella mattutina. Intorno al trono di Dio è sempre mattino. Anche i santi che seguono con ardore la sua somiglianza rifletteranno questa virtù, perché la luce di Gesù è la luce della giovinezza.

Descrivendo il Messia, il salmista attinge alla bellezza naturale della rugiada del mattino (–vedi Salmo 110:3). Il pensiero della rugiada ci richiama giù dai cieli e ci svela un ritratto di questa terra in cui viviamo. In cielo non c’è notte, non c’è variazione di caldo e freddo, non c’è bisogno del sole per illuminare il giorno e, di conseguenza… non c’è rugiada. La rugiada appartiene alla natura terrestre, dove chiunque si chini a osservarla vedrà un reggimento uniforme d’erba scintillare come se fosse incastonato di miriadi di diamanti. Dopo una lunga notte buia, le gocce di rugiada, come lacrime, brillano negli occhi dei fiori mentre piangono di gioia all’arrivo del primo raggio del sole mattutino. Chi cammina tra la bassa vegetazione si vedrà lavare i piedi da mille mani carezzevoli, opera di Dio. Cristo non è raffigurato come la rugiada del mattino, ma come la rugiada della giovinezza, e l’immagine si sviluppa ulteriormente.

La giovinezza è una stagione di energia esuberante. Alcuni non riescono a stare fermi. In genere sono creature socievoli che amano le attività in compagnia. Questo non è né una virtù né un vizio; è piuttosto una caratteristica naturale. Con il progredire degli anni, una tendenza graduale doma e tempera l’anima. Man mano che la vita procede, la visione si fa più chiara e il pensiero più stabile, e ci eleviamo verso cose migliori. Ma quando si è superata la vetta della mezza età e i piedi scendono lungo il pendio, quell’impeto tumultuoso di energia fisica che travolgeva ogni cosa si custodisce nei ricordi del passato. Per molti, è la consolazione più vicina che si possa trovare ai giorni ormai trascorsi della propria forza.

Ma Cristo non ci ha chiamati a coltivare la nostalgia del passato, né un desiderio malinconico del «fare» della nostra giovinezza. Oggi tanti si lamentano tristemente che il loro slancio sia ormai svanito. Non hanno alcuna visione di cose più elevate e sono più energizzati da una lattina di Mountain Dew che dalla rugiada della giovinezza. Li ispira di più un viaggio nei ricordi e il ripensare agli eventi del passato che la speranza che sta davanti a loro.

L’età non è un ostacolo per ottenere la rugiada della giovinezza. L’Antico di giorni cavalca ancora fra i candelabri d’oro. Giovanni vide i suoi capelli… bianchi come lana, bianchi come neve… –Apocalisse 1:14; eppure Salomone dichiara: …i suoi riccioli sono folti e neri come il corvo –Cantico dei Cantici 5:11. Anche se l’età può rubarci la forza e l’udito, …la mano del Signore non è troppo corta per salvare, né il suo orecchio troppo duro per udire –Isaia 59:1. Egli ha assicurato la rugiada della giovinezza e ci invita a parteciparvi. Il problema non si trova nel nostro corpo che si deteriora, ma in una mente che declina spiritualmente. Il flagello della vecchiaia si instaura soprattutto quando la mente segue il corpo.

Non è che la vita diventi più povera con il passare degli anni o cessi di essere nobile quando svanisce il fascino della giovinezza. Se fossimo stati messi qui soltanto per provare gioia, lo spegnersi del romanticismo giovanile sarebbe terribile. Dio aveva per i suoi figli uno scopo molto più grande che renderli semplicemente «attivi e pieni di vitalità». Siamo stati mandati qui per imparare. Gli anni che ci sono assegnati sulla terra devono essere tutti un periodo di formazione, e non è nel luminoso romanticismo della giovinezza che impariamo le lezioni migliori e più durature. Le impariamo nell’adempimento ostinato del nostro dovere, nell’accettazione tranquilla dei nostri limiti, nel portare con pazienza il peso quotidiano e nel tendere una mano d’aiuto al nostro fratello. Queste sono le vere occasioni per la formazione cristiana e le radici della nobiltà morale. Cristo lavorò …non per il cibo che perisce, ma per il cibo che dura in vita eterna… –Giovanni 6:27 e portò a termine il suo compito terreno in 33 anni. Ma la rugiada della giovinezza non si dissipò quando si sedette alla destra del Padre.

Concludiamo dunque che questa giovinezza non si ottiene con la forza, ma con…

...La speranza

Ma egli, dopo aver offerto un unico sacrificio per i peccati per sempre, si è seduto alla destra di Dio; da allora aspetta che i suoi nemici siano posti come sgabello dei suoi piedi. –Ebrei 10:12-13.

Come dobbiamo immaginare Cristo ora? Adagiato su una poltrona, completamente sfinito dalla sua esperienza con il popolo ostinato di questa terra? È intento a mettere insieme un album di ricordi preziosi? Questa è troppo spesso la condizione degli anziani, e così la loro mente muore insieme al corpo.

Ma non solo: ci gloriamo anche nelle tribolazioni, sapendo che la tribolazione produce pazienza, la pazienza esperienza e l’esperienza speranza –Romani 5:3-4. A volte ci chiediamo se questo passo possa essere vero. Chiunque abbia qualche anno sulle spalle può testimoniare di aver fatto brutte esperienze e di aver poi provato disperazione. Come persone, tutti abbiamo vissuto esperienze deludenti con un coniuge, un figlio o una comunità di chiesa, dopo le quali si posa una persistente nube di disperazione. Al di fuori di Cristo, un’esperienza amara conduce sempre al pessimismo. Così era nel mondo quando venne Gesù. Così è ancora oggi.

Ma la rugiada della giovinezza è irrimediabilmente piena di speranza. Nella giovinezza nasce naturalmente, e in modo meraviglioso, un’attesa effervescente che si conserva in Cristo. In ogni inverno, quando i campi sono spogli e la fredda raffica fischia tra gli alberi, rimane la speranza che i fiori sbocceranno di nuovo. In ogni primavera c’è la speranza dell’estate. In ogni estate c’è la speranza del raccolto. È viva nella natura ed è viva nella giovinezza. Chi non la vede raccoglierà, nel migliore dei casi, un’esistenza monotona e grigia. Vivere è la cosa più rara al mondo. La maggior parte delle persone esiste, e basta. –Oscar Wilde.

Gli altri saranno invece illuminati dalla speranza che…

…Guarisce le nostre infermità

I nostri corpi sono destinati alla tomba e non hanno speranza di rinnovamento in questa vita. Sono le nostre menti a portare le infermità più grandi. L’uomo infermo da 38 anni a Betesda poté soltanto esprimere un lamento senza speranza quando Cristo gli chiese: …Vuoi guarire? –Giovanni 5:6. All’alba della sua nuova vita gli fu offerto un nuovo rimedio: …Ecco, tu sei guarito; non peccare più, affinché non ti accada di peggio –Giovanni 5:14. Che cosa potrebbe essere peggio dell’essere storpio per anni? Una mente assillata da un cupo indulgere nei dolori di questo mondo. La vecchiaia si instaura quando abbiamo più ricordi del passato che speranze per il domani. È deludente quando le persone invecchiano senza avere una visione del domani, ma è disastroso vedere giovani afflitti dai suoi effetti paralizzanti. Molti brancolano senza meta attraverso le varie prove della vita, intorpiditi dalla mancanza di beatitudine. Il sole di mezzogiorno ha fatto evaporare la rugiada della loro giovinezza, e l’unica lode che riescono a esprimere è il risultato di una manciata di piacevoli ricordi di ieri. La rugiada di un nuovo mattino deve far nascere un atteggiamento nuovo.

…Ridimensiona le nostre ambizioni

In verità, in verità ti dico: quand’eri più giovane, ti cingevi da solo e andavi dove volevi; ma quando sarai vecchio, stenderai le mani, e un altro ti cingerà e ti porterà dove non vuoi. –Giovanni 21:18. Da giovani possiamo vincere grazie alla forza della giovinezza. Quando l’età fa il suo corso, troveremo un’altra strada: la vittoria attraverso la resa.

…Vi ho scritto, giovani, perché siete forti, e la parola di Dio dimora in voi, e avete vinto il maligno. –1 Giovanni 2:14. Il mondo ci induce a vivere egoisticamente. I giovani sono spesso sottoposti a percorsi di studio che insegnano loro a «essere tutto ciò che possono essere». Si dà grande importanza al miglioramento personale e alla preparazione per il futuro. Questo può prepararli a un mondo in cui sopravvive il più forte, ma li lascerà privi di risorse quando la forza e il vigore della giovinezza saranno svaniti.

Poiché tutto ciò che è nel mondo, la concupiscenza della carne, la concupiscenza degli occhi e la superbia della vita, non viene dal Padre, ma dal mondo. E il mondo passa con la sua concupiscenza; ma chi fa la volontà di Dio rimane in eterno. –1 Giovanni 2:16-17. Vincere il male con il bene è l’antidoto biblico per incanalare le energie giovanili. Che si tratti della concupiscenza interiore o del desiderio rivolto all’esterno, la speranza nasce piantando un seme di gentilezza nella vita di un’altra persona. La ricerca del piacere e la scelta dell’ozio deluderanno sempre chi le persegue e lo lasceranno in una valle di disperazione più profonda di quella da cui era partito. È bene per l’uomo portare il giogo nella sua giovinezza… Ponga la bocca nella polvere: forse c’è ancora speranza. –Lamentazioni 3:27-29. Siamo stati creati per lavorare nella vigna di Dio, e quanti ne hanno il desiderio raccoglieranno con la speranza della sua ricompensa giovanile.

…Santifica le nostre prove

Poiché siamo stati salvati in speranza; ora, una speranza di ciò che si vede non è speranza... –Romani 8:24. Quanto spesso riusciamo a identificarci con Giobbe nel suo dolore. Ma prima che il suo dolore ricevesse anche solo un briciolo di ricompensa, i flussi di guarigione cominciarono a scorrere quando Giobbe rese riverenza al suo Creatore. Quando riconosciamo che Dio è perfetto in tutte le prove che permette, impariamo allora ad adorare nel tempio non fatto da mani d’uomo e a non tener conto delle fragilità del corpo. Sedersi ai piedi di Cristo accende una scintilla giovanile che irradia lo spirito interiore e fa nascere la speranza. La rugiada della giovinezza diventa così la nostra parte, poiché Cristo ci impartisce vita eterna ed eterna giovinezza. Dall’ora della tomba e per tutta l’eternità saremo giovani e sfideremo la stanchezza e la morte, se viviamo nella luce mattutina di Gesù Cristo. Il cielo è un luogo di eterna giovinezza e, proprio come la luce del sole si riflette sulla luna, così la luce di Cristo si riflette sulla sua sposa. Ella è pura e giovane, …una chiesa gloriosa, senza macchia, senza ruga o altri simili difetti… –Efesini 5:27. Beato il santo venerabile che giunge alle porte del cielo in tale condizione.

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

তুমি কি ভালো জীবন যাপন করতে চাও? সত্যিই জীবন উপভোগ করার জন্য তোমার কী অভিজ্ঞতা অর্জন করা বা কী সম্পন্ন করা দরকার বলে মনে হয়? অনেকের জীবনের প্রধান লক্ষ্য হলো আনন্দ খোঁজা এবং মজা করা। তা অর্জন করতে প্রচুর সময় ও অর্থ ব্যয় করা হয়। কিন্তু আমরা কি তা অর্জন করতে পারি? আমাদের স্বাভাবিক চিন্তায় মনে হয়, আমাদের খুশি করার জন্য পরিস্থিতি ঠিকঠাক হওয়া দরকার। কিন্তু আমরা সবাই জানি, পরিস্থিতি সব সময় আদর্শ থাকে না। তাই আমাদের সুখের জন্য সেগুলোর ওপর নির্ভর করা যায় না। আমাদের এর চেয়ে বড় কিছু দরকার। অথবা কারও।

নিশ্চয়ই, আমরা জানি যে একমাত্র ঈশ্বরই কখনো পরিবর্তন হন না এবং সর্বদা বিশ্বস্ত। ঈশ্বরের আরেকটি বিষয় হলো, তিনি সার্বভৌম। অন্য কথায়, তিনিই কর্তৃত্বে আছেন। কিন্তু আমরা স্বাধীনতা পছন্দ করি; আমরা চাই, সবকিছু এমনভাবে ঘটুক যা আমাদের ভালো লাগে। জীবন যখন সেভাবে চলে না, তখন আমাদের একটি সিদ্ধান্ত নিতে হয়। আমরা কি ঈশ্বরের সম্পূর্ণ স্বরূপ—তাঁর অপরিবর্তনীয়তা ও সার্বভৌমত্ব, উভয়ই—মেনে নেব, নাকি ভালো জীবন পাওয়ার চেষ্টায় নিজেদের ইচ্ছামতো চলার জন্য লড়াই করব?

আনন্দের মূল উৎস স্বয়ং ঈশ্বর। কারণ তিনি আমাদের নিজের জন্য সৃষ্টি করেছেন। তিনি আমাদের সৃষ্টি করেছেন যেন আমরা তাঁকে আনন্দ দিই, কিন্তু আমাদের মনে হয়, নিজেদের আনন্দ দেওয়া দরকার। এর শুরু হয়েছিল এদন উদ্যানে, যখন সর্প হবাকে বুঝিয়েছিল যে ঈশ্বরকে সন্তুষ্ট করার চেয়ে নিজেকে সন্তুষ্ট করা বেশি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। সেই থেকে মানুষ নিজেদের হৃদয়ের ভেতরে এবং বাইরে, অন্যদের সঙ্গে, যুদ্ধে লিপ্ত। নিজেদের জন্য আনন্দ খুঁজে পাওয়ার চেষ্টায় তারা তা পায় না, কারণ তাদের সৃষ্টি করা হয়েছে ঈশ্বরকে সন্তুষ্ট করার জন্য।

এই যুদ্ধের সমাধান যাকোব ৪ অধ্যায়ে পাওয়া যায়। বিষয়টি সহজ: ঈশ্বরের বশীভূত হও। তাঁর সামনে নিজেদের নত করো। তিনি আমাদের কাছে অতিরিক্ত কিছু চাইছেন না, কারণ তিনি সার্বভৌম। তিনি আমাদের সৃষ্টি করেছেন, তাই আমরা কীভাবে জীবনযাপন করব, সে বিষয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত দেওয়ার অধিকার তাঁরই। যদি আমরা সত্যিই জীবনে আনন্দ খুঁজে পাই, তবে তা হবে নিজেদের জীবন ও আকাঙ্ক্ষাকে ক্রুশে তুলে ঈশ্বর এবং আমাদের জন্য তাঁর আদি উদ্দেশ্যের সঙ্গে একাত্ম হওয়ার মাধ্যমে। এটি আমাদের সীমাবদ্ধ না করে বরং সুযোগ ও সম্ভাবনার এক জগৎ খুলে দেয়। এর অর্থ এই নয় যে ঈশ্বর চান বলে আমাদের কাজগুলো করতে হবে। ঈশ্বরের সঙ্গে একাত্ম হওয়ার অর্থ, তিনি আমাদের যা করতে চান, আমরাও তা-ই করতে চাই।

উপাসনা ও কৃতজ্ঞতা

যখন আমরা ঈশ্বরের সঙ্গে একাত্ম হই, তখন আমাদের দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি পুরোপুরি বদলে যায়। যা কিছু আদর্শ নয়, তা নিয়ে আক্ষেপ করার বদলে আমরা দেখতে শুরু করি, কত কিছু সত্যিই আশীর্বাদ। আমরা যে সব ভালো বিষয় উপভোগ করি, সেগুলোর জন্য উপাসনা ও কৃতজ্ঞতায় পূর্ণ হৃদয় রাখতে পারি। আমরা বুঝতে পারি, আমরা আসলে কতটা অযোগ্য। কোনো ভালো কিছুরই আমরা যোগ্য ছিলাম না, তবু ঈশ্বর আমাদের উপভোগ করার জন্য কত কিছু দিয়েছেন!

বর্তমানে বেঁচে থাকা

তরুণী হিসেবে আমাদের কল্পনায় ডুবে থাকতে, আদর্শ ও মনোরম এক ভবিষ্যতে বেঁচে থাকতে প্রবণতা আছে। বর্তমানের অপূর্ণ বাস্তবতায় বেঁচে থাকা এবং তাতেই আনন্দ খুঁজে পাওয়া কখনো কখনো আমাদের জন্য কঠিন হয়। কিন্তু ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছা যখন আমাদের ইচ্ছা হয়ে ওঠে, তখন সত্যিকারের আনন্দ আসে, কারণ আমরা তাঁর উদ্দেশ্য পূরণ করছি।

যেকোনো পরিস্থিতিতে, এমনকি একঘেয়ে জীবনেও, আমরা আনন্দ অনুভব করতে শিখতে পারি। আমরা একঘেয়ে জীবন কাটাতে ভয় পাই। আমরা চাই জীবন রোমাঞ্চকর হোক। কিন্তু ঈশ্বর চান আমরা তাঁকে সন্তুষ্ট করি, আর তা করলে পরিস্থিতি যা-ই হোক, আমরা আনন্দ অনুভব করি। তবে তখন তাঁর রাজ্যের সেবায় আমাদের ব্যবহার করার জন্যও আমরা প্রস্তুত থাকি, আর তিনি হয়তো আমাদের রোমাঞ্চকর সুযোগের দিকে ডাকবেন। কিন্তু প্রতিদিনের জীবনে তাঁর ইচ্ছার বশীভূত হতে না শিখলে, রোমাঞ্চকর অভিযানে আমরা কার্যকর হতে পারব না।

সম্পর্ক

বর্তমানে ঈশ্বর আমাদের যেখানে রেখেছেন, সেখানেই যখন আমরা আনন্দ ও সন্তুষ্টি খুঁজে পাই, তখন আমাদের জীবনে এখন যারা আছেন, তাঁদের সঙ্গে দৃঢ় ও গঠনমূলক সম্পর্ক গড়ে তোলায় মনোযোগ দিতে পারি। ঈশ্বর আমাদের সামাজিক জীব হিসেবে সৃষ্টি করেছেন, আর ভালো সম্পর্ক আমাদের সত্যিকারের আনন্দ দেবে। অন্যদের কাছে পৌঁছাতেও ঈশ্বর আমাদের ব্যবহার করতে পারেন। আমরা যখন তাঁর সঙ্গে একাত্ম হই, তখন আমাদের মনোযোগ আর নিজেদের ওপর থাকে না, বরং অন্যদের ওপর থাকে। ঈশ্বরের জীবন আমাদের মধ্য দিয়ে প্রবাহিত হতে পারে, আর এর মাধ্যমে আমরা অন্যদের তাঁকে পাওয়ার পথ দেখাতে পারি এবং তা করতে গিয়ে আনন্দ ও পরিতৃপ্তিও লাভ করতে পারি।

আবেগ

আমাদের আরেকটি প্রবণতা হলো, আবেগকে আমাদের নিয়ন্ত্রণ করতে দেওয়া। আর আনন্দ পাওয়ার জন্য আমরা যদি পরিস্থিতির দিকে তাকিয়ে থাকি, তাহলে আবেগ লাগামছাড়া হয়ে যাবে। তখন মুহূর্তে যা ঘটছে, তার দ্বারা পরিচালিত অনুভূতির এক রোলার কোস্টারে আমরা ওঠানামা করতে থাকব। এরপর আমরা স্বপ্নের জগতে পালিয়ে যাই, যা বাস্তবতা সম্পর্কে আমাদের দৃষ্টিভঙ্গিকে আরও বিকৃত করে। কিন্তু ঈশ্বর অবিচল, আর আমরা যখন তাঁর সঙ্গে একাত্ম হই, তখন তিনি আমাদের স্থিরতা ও বিশ্রাম দেন। ফলে চিরপরিবর্তনশীল পরিস্থিতিতেও আমরা সর্বদা বিদ্যমান আনন্দ অনুভব করতে পারি।

আসুন, আমরা তাঁর সঙ্গে ক্রমেই আরও একাত্ম হতে থাকি। আর তিনি আমাদের সমগ্র যাত্রাপথে স্বর্গীয় সূর্যালোক দেবেন—পৃথিবীর পরিস্থিতিতে যা বদলায় না, আর তাঁকে মুখোমুখি দেখলে যা পূর্ণরূপে উপলব্ধ হবে। …তোমার উপস্থিতিতে আনন্দের পূর্ণতা; তোমার দক্ষিণ হস্তে অনন্তকাল আনন্দ। –গীতসংহিতা ১৬:১১।

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19

هل سبق أن حاولت تغيير العالم؟ أنا فعلت ذلك. حين كنت مراهقة، حلمت بالمغامرات الجريئة التي سأخوضها من أجل الله. وبينما كنت أرتب المائدة في بيت والديّ، كنت أنتظر اليوم الذي أتمكن فيه من القيام بأمور أعظم—أمور مثل إقامة بيت في أفريقيا، والتحدث بلغات غريبة، وقيادة الناس إلى يسوع. وكان التفكير في العيش في كوخ من الطين ومراوغة الثعابين السامة يبدو مثيرًا.

ثم تحقق بعض أحلامي! تركت كل ما عرفته من قبل، ووصلت إلى بلد أفريقي في رحلة حافلة بالأدرينالين. حاولت أن أغير العالم الصغير الذي كنت فيه—تلك القرية التي بدت وكأن الله قد هجرها، والمليئة بالسكر والزيجات المحطمة والشجارات والأطفال المهملين. كنت أشعر يوميًا بالضيق من انشغالي الشديد بمهام أرضية «تافهة»، وأتساءل كيف يمكنني أن أحدث فرقًا. ثم انتهت أعمالنا فجأة وبلا مقدمات بسبب الإنهاك وموجة من شكوك الحكومة. لم يكن أي من هذا ضمن أحلامي.

ما زلت أطرح السؤال نفسه: «يا الله، كيف يمكنني أن أحدث فرقًا؟» يطرق الجار الباب. وتحتاج عاملة الغسيل إلى أجرها. ويجب أن يكون الغداء على المائدة بعد 15 دقيقة. ويحتاج طفلنا في الصف الخامس إلى مساعدة في ضرب الكسور. وتمتلئ السماء بالغيوم الداكنة، وحبل الغسيل مكتظ بالملابس. أمسح أنف طفلتي للمرة الألف بينما تجلس فوق المائدة وتبعثر كتب أخيها وأوراقه. أخبز الخبز، وأصنع اللبن، وأخضّ الزبدة، وأعد 21 وجبة في الأسبوع. أطوي جبالًا من الغسيل، ثم أفعل كل ذلك من جديد في الأسبوع التالي. أكنس الأرض التي تراكم عليها مقدار مذهل من الأوساخ في ساعتين فقط. ومن نواحٍ كثيرة، أصبحت الحياة أكثر رتابة مما كانت عليه من قبل.

لم أكن أملك القدرة على تغيير العالم حين كنت مراهقة حالمة، ولا أملكها الآن. الله لا يطلب مني ذلك. إنه لا يطلب مني سوى أن أسير معه وأطيع صوته. وأتعلم ببطء أن الروحي والجسدي لا ينفصلان—فحتى يسوع علّم إنجيل الملكوت في أوقات الراحة والنوم والأكل. يمكن أن يكون فرك الأرض وتقطيع الخبز عملَي عبادة لخالقي إن اعتبرتهما كذلك. فهو الذي صمم أن تتم مسيرتي الروحية وانتشارها بينما تلامس يداي الأمور الأرضية. هكذا تُنقّى روحي. وهذه هي الطريقة الوحيدة التي أستطيع بها أن أعبّر عن إيماني بوصفه إيمانًا حيًا. وهي الطريقة الوحيدة التي أستطيع بها أن ألمس قلوب أطفالي وأن أعيش أمامهم إنجيلًا عمليًا يقتدون به. وهكذا يثبت إيماني للمؤمنين أن إيماني حقيقي، إذ يرونني أواجه الصعوبات نفسها التي يواجهونها، ويرون أيضًا ردود أفعالي الناتجة عنها.

أتعلم ببطء أن خدمة الله لا تتعلق بالعزيمة أو بتغيير العالم، بل بالسماح لروح الله أن يسكن فيّ ويرشدني ويكلمني. وأتعلم أن الله يهتم أكثر بالشخص الذي أصبح عليه، لا بكل ما أريد أن أفعله من أجله. ولعلني في النهاية لست سوى فتيلة مدخنة، لا الشخص الذي سيغير العالم. أظن أن بولس استطاع أن يتفهم هذا الشعور حين كتب: «لكن الله اختار جهال العالم ليخزي الحكماء، واختار الله ضعفاء العالم ليخزي الأقوياء؛ واختار الله أدنياء العالم والمزدرى بهم، وغير الموجود، ليبطل الموجود، لكي لا يفتخر كل ذي جسد أمامه» –1 كورنثوس 1:27-29.

قالت إليزابيث إليوت: «أحيانًا يرتفع النور ببطء مؤلم. إن ملكوت الله مثل الخميرة والبذار، أشياء تعمل بصمت وخفاء وبطء، لكنها تحمل في داخلها قوة تحويل لا تُقدّر. ففي التربة العادية، بل وفي العجين الباهت، تكمن إمكانية التحول.»1

إن جعل الإنجازات والنجاح محور قلبي طريقة أنانية للعيش. عندما أُخذت منا تلك القرية وأولئك الناس وسط دوامة من مشكلات الحكومة وسوء الفهم، شعرت أن الله لا يمكن أن يستخدم هذا لخير أحد. ألم يكن لا يزال بحاجة إلينا هناك؟ والحقيقة أنه لم يعد بحاجة إلينا هناك. لم نكن لا غنى عنا. ولعل الله سمح بكل ذلك لكي أتعلم أن قبوله لي لا يستند إلى إنجازاتي.

«لأنه من ازدرى بيوم الأمور الصغيرة…» –زكريا 4:10.

من أكون حتى أحكم إن كان عمل ما صغيرًا أم لا؟ هل أشعر بالضجر من واجباتي، وأعتقد أن الله سيكون أكثر رضًا لو قمت، بحسب تصوري، بواجبات «عظيمة» تبدو دائمًا بعيدة المنال؟ هل أنسى أن خدمة المسيح لا تتعلق بي وبشعوري بالرضا، بل بالله والعمل الذي يريد أن يقوم به من خلالي؟! قالت إيمي كارمايكل: «ليس المكان الذي نوجد فيه، ولا العمل الذي نقوم به أو لا نستطيع القيام به، هو المهم؛ بل هناك أمر آخر. إنه النار التي تتقد وتضيء في داخلنا، أيًّا كانت ظروفنا.»2

النار التي تتقد وتضيء في داخلنا هي سرنا. يمكن لتلك النار أن تتقد بينما نفرك الأرضيات ونعد وجبات لا تنتهي ونعلم أطفالنا في المنزل. وستلمس عاملة الغسيل، ومساعدة المنزل، والفتاة التي تكابد الصعوبات في الكنيسة، والجيران. أحيانًا يحدث ذلك دون وعي منا، وأحيانًا يحدث حين نقرر أن نمد يد العون بدلًا من أخذ قيلولة أو القيام بشيء ممتع آخر؛ لكنه يتطلب دائمًا أن ننسى أنفسنا، ونحب الآخرين، وننتبه إلى الفرص الصغيرة.

لكن احذروا… لا يجوز أن نخلط بين تقبلنا لصِغر ما في حياتنا والخمول. فكثير من المسيحيين لا يتوقعون أن يستخدمهم الله، لذا يستقرون في حالة روحية خاملة. ينبغي أن نتوقع أن يعمل الله بطرق مدهشة. قد يستخدمنا الله لإنجاز تلك الأمور، لكن ذلك يحدث غالبًا بطرق لا تخطر ببالنا أو لا نتوقعها.

وافقت أرملة صرفة أن تعطي غريبًا آخر حفنة من الدقيق وآخر قطرات الزيت المتبقية لديها. كان بإمكانها أن تعارض النبي وتطالبه بأن يغادر فورًا، فهي كانت مسؤولة عن ابنها، ولم يكن لديها من الدقيق ما تعطيه له سوى تلك الكمية القليلة. لكنها لم تفعل؛ بل اختارت أن تعطيه كله. وبارك الله طاعتها المستعدة بأن جعل دقيقها وزيتها يتجددان بمعجزة ما دامت تحتاج إليهما.3

ظل الله يقلّص جيش جدعون حتى خاض المعركة وانتصر فيها في النهاية ببضع مئات من الرجال فقط. كان جدعون معتادًا في العادة على جيوش قوامها آلاف. والآن كان الله يطلب منه أن يخوض معركة عظيمة ببضع مئات فحسب. وفي النهاية، أصبح هذا الأمر المستحيل بشريًا فرصةً أظهر الله من خلالها قوته.4

في بداية خدمته، اختار يسوع اثني عشر رجلًا فقط ليدربهم، بدلًا من الجموع. وفي النهاية، هجرته فرقته الصغيرة من الرجال. وتعرض للسخرية والقتل. وبدا لمن شاهدوا أن ما تبقى من عمل يسوع قد مات معه، ومع ذلك كانت خطة الفداء الكونية توضع موضع التنفيذ—فقد قلب أولئك الصيادون البسطاء العالم رأسًا على عقب بالإنجيل.5

نرى من هذه الأمثلة أن الله لا يبحث عن الأكبر أو الأقوى أو الأفضل. وهو لا يستخدم أصحاب المهارات المتخصصة أو المواهب المبهرة وحدهم. فكثيرًا ما تشبه قوتنا ومواردنا بضع مئات من الجنود في جيش جدعون—أي إنها ببساطة لا تكفي لتلبية الحاجة. لكن حين نقدم ما لدينا بقلب مستعد، يضاعف الله جهودنا الصغيرة ويجعل منها عرضًا لنعمه—عرضًا مخصصًا له، وغالبًا لا يراه الآخرون. إن فعل إعداد المائدة البسيط هو فعل إيمان وعطاء وخدمة، أينما كنا. وقد اختار الله هذه الأمور الضعيفة لتكون ذات شأن في ملكوته.

سر الحياة الناجحة هو يسوع فينا، لا أفكارنا المسبقة عن النجاح. وحين يعمل فينا ومن خلالنا، ستتقد قوته في بيوتنا وأحيائنا. وحين يكون هو سبب عيشنا، يمكننا أن نثق به في ما ستؤول إليه الأمور. وبالإصغاء إلى صوت يسوع، يمكننا أن نحدث فرقًا—شخصًا واحدًا، ولقاءً واحدًا، وشيئًا صغيرًا واحدًا في كل مرة.

  1. إليزابيث إليوت، The Savage My Kinsman (الطبعة المنقحة، منشورات سيرفنت، 1981)، الخاتمة، ص 147
  2. إيمي كارمايكل، Edges of His Ways، ص 218
  3. 1 ملوك 17: 11-16
  4. قضاة 7
  5. لوقا 6:13-16، يوحنا 19

After living in Haiti for several months, I finally had the opportunity to go visit the local witch doctor. As I walked up his long drive, I passed many statues and satanic symbols. It was eerie for sure. As I approached the voodoo temple that was connected to his house, I saw him standing there watching me approach. My heart began to race; I knew he was a powerful man. Then he began to laugh. The closer I got, the louder he laughed. I was a bit puzzled until I realized that many people from the village were following me up the lane. They were very interested in what was about to transpire. I approached the man, not knowing what would happen next.

“Are you a pastor?” he asked.

“Yes, I am,” was my reply. Again, he began to laugh loudly.

“You pastors are all the same,” he proclaimed. “You want everyone to come to your churches, but your churches have no power! When one of your people gets sick, they come to me. No power, you Christians!”

A heavy burden overtook me, and I explained to him how I agreed with him, but that the real church of Jesus Christ would always have power. The Bible actually says that the very gates of Hell shall not prevail against it.

This was the beginning of a very interesting relationship, but I will never forget those words—most certainly from the devil himself—“You Christians have no power!”

I have since traveled to hundreds of churches and need to agree with that voodoo priest. The Christian churches are lacking power. But why? We know that God is power. We have many things figured out, we look good and sound good, but do we still have the power of God in our churches?

In the Old Testament we have many examples of power and the lack of power. We can also learn how we receive power, and why we lose it.

In Joshua, chapter 6, we have the familiar account of the children of Israel and the city of Jericho. God tells Joshua and all the men of war to compass the city, and walk around it once every day, for six days. Then on the seventh day they were to march around the city not just once, but seven times. After they had completed the seven trips around the city, the priests were to blow their trumpets.

We know what happened when Joshua obeyed each command—those thick, impenetrable walls came tumbling down. God also gave Joshua a strict command about what the men should and should not do. They were to keep themselves from everything that God had pronounced was accursed; all the silver, gold, and vessels were to be consecrated into the treasury of the Lord; no man was to take any of the spoil.

However, Achan saw some nice things that he desired. He slipped them into his armor, then later hid them under his tent, and no one saw a thing.

After this great victory, Joshua sent spies to the next city, Ai, to discover how well the city was fortified. The men returned and told Joshua not to send all the men to Ai, for there were only a few defenders protecting the city.

However, the men of Ai smote the children of Israel and chased them away. Moreover, Joshua rent his clothes and cried out to God. Then God replied that there was sin in the camp of Israel.

In the Old Testament, the children of Israel are normally representative of the church of Jesus Christ today. Can we not glean much from this account? When there was no sin in the camp (or in the church) God’s people had complete victory; they lost not one. They did many wonderful things, they destroyed all their enemies around them, and they lived in COMPLETE victory. However, as soon as sin entered into their midst, even a small sin done by one man, they lost their power. They no longer had victory over their enemies.

What follows is a graphic description of how the children of Israel dealt with the sin that had entered the camp. It was totally destroyed.

And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor … And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire… –Joshua 7:24-26.

In this account it is clear why God’s people had lost their power—they had sin in the camp. It is also clear what it took for them to regain that power which they had lost—get rid of the sin.

In chapter 8 we read of the power being restored to Israel instantly after the sin was dealt with. Again, they lived in victory!

Another passage in the Old Testament that speaks of this topic is in Leviticus chapters 13 and 14. Leprosy was a strange disease. If one were to get leprosy, it was easily spread. Thus, there needed to be some strict guidelines regarding how to deal with the disease. The priest was to examine very closely to see if the person in question indeed had leprosy or not. If the priest was unsure, he would shut the person up in a room for seven days then examine him again. If it was determined that the person had leprosy, then they were sent outside of the city.

As Paul addresses the church in Corinth, he tells them that he has heard there is sin in the church. He seems surprised that the church is taking it so casually, …Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump? Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened… –1 Corinthians 5:6-7. Later he tells the church …Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person –1 Corinthians 5:13.

Let’s say that you heard the news that leprosy was again a problem in your village. This flesh-destroying disease had made a comeback and many from your village were now infected. Then you’re sitting in church on Sunday morning, when the doors open, and a man enters with skin and flesh hanging from his extremities. He is badly infected, but he does not seem to know it. What would you do? What if he wanted to come sit by you? What if he wanted to talk to your children? I think we all know what we would do; we would not allow him into our midst. We love our people, our families too much for that.

What about sin? Do we allow sin to come and join us? Do we take it seriously? What is worse, being infected with a flesh-destroying disease, or being infected by a soul-destroying sin? Remember, the wages of sin is death—spiritual death; eternal death. If we would treat sin in the same way as we would the disease (and we should) then our churches would once again have Holy Spirit power.

The Bible says …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

We have already seen how sin separates us from the power of God, and we have also seen how God wants to give us power. He wants us to have victory over the enemy—the devil, the world, and flesh. However, something seems to be happening in our churches—we are allowing sin to enter. It is common to hear a preacher say, “No one is perfect.” Or, “We all sin.” Oh, that we would realize the damage these statements can make. Jesus came to save us from ALL sin; ALL unrighteousness. If we are left to continue in our sin, what has Jesus done for us?

I hear about churches drifting into the world. They gradually let go of convictions and allow some new fashion and pomp of the world to enter. Something that I hear little of is churches falling apart because of gross sin, such as fornication or drunkenness. The enemy of our souls, desires for us to become lukewarm. He wants the church to lose its power, to start living like everyone else. Here in Haiti, there are churches everywhere. On Sunday mornings starting at five o’clock in the morning, I start hearing the churches singing and worshipping. However, where are all those people on Monday morning? They are mixing right back into the world from whence they have come.

I was recently talking to a very wealthy Haitian man who owned resorts and properties all over Haiti. I asked him if he was a Christian. (I wanted to start a conversation.) I could tell that he wanted to say yes; instead, he became frustrated and said no. I asked him why not. He said exactly what I thought he would say. “I have desired to become a Christian, I’ve gone to all the churches around here, but I don’t feel they have anything to offer me. I have money; I have physical blessings; but that seems to be all that they are seeking for.”

If our churches today would refuse to settle for anything less than the infilling, empowering, and leading of the Holy Spirit, a full dose of heavenly power, then we would be able to offer something that would appeal to the lost around us. I believe this is exactly what the world is looking for; they are seeking for something better, something supernatural. What if we would settle for nothing less? What if we would stay on our knees until the power of God came back? What if we would again weep for our souls, and the souls of others?

I was working closely with a vicious gang leader who lived in the neighboring village. He was hard, but God had led him to me. For seven long months we met and communicated, I wanted him to catch a glimpse of the power of God; I wanted God to save him. He would often get drunk and threaten to kill me; I would continue to point him to the Savior. He and his gang came over one day to stop a work project, saying that they now owned the land. They brandished their guns and threatened all that were there. I explained to him that God owned the land. He said, “That is fine; tell God to come down here, and I’ll cut off His head.” I was troubled by this remark and asked him if he understood the power of the God he just threatened. One afternoon I drove to his house, and we sat outside and talked. God led me to preach a bold message to him that day. “You need to give up this gang life. God wants to save you, and change your heart!” He seemed very sober as I continued, “You never know when someone will come here and kill you! You can’t control that, but my friend you can control where you go after you are dead!” I then reminded him of the terrible thing he had said days before.

While we were still talking, two men from a neighboring gang approached on motorbikes. They were heavily armed; they had come at that very moment to kill him, but they saw me talking to him and waited for me to leave. “You have a wife and children, are you not tired of this life? God has something so much better for you!” I was pleading, pleading for his soul. It was his very last opportunity, death waited at the door. As I left I told him that I would be back.

After the shooting I rushed back, but it was over… all over.

When we live in the power of the resurrection, the power of the Almighty God, it is then that He works! I feel there is so much work to be done before the Lord returns, but God’s people are too busy, we do not have time.

Do we fear talking about the power of God and the Holy Ghost simply because the Pentecostal movement has twisted what the Bible teaches? God help us.

When we call out to God for salvation, we are doing so because we know we need to be saved; converted. We also know that we cannot save ourselves, so we ask God to help us. Then when God helps us, we are able to do things that we could not do before! Angry people are angry no more. People that could not control their lust now have control. Selfish people begin to put others first. Shy people begin to preach with boldness. Greedy people begin to give to others. God does a work that counselors and doctors cannot do, He changes the very core of a person, and then all things become new. We now live for something far better than what this world has to give; we rise above by the power of God and show this sin-sick world there is a better way!

All through the Bible, God’s people did supernatural things; they did not settle for just a nice life. They sought something bigger, something better. There is power in the blood of Jesus, but it took the cross to make that a possibility. It also takes a cross for us to find that power. And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24. Yes, it seems foolish to those that perish, but to those that believe, it is the Power of God.

아이티에서 몇 달을 지낸 뒤, 마침내 그 지역의 부두교 주술사를 찾아갈 기회가 생겼습니다. 그의 긴 진입로를 따라 걸어가면서 여러 조각상과 사탄의 상징물을 지나쳤습니다. 분명 섬뜩한 광경이었습니다. 그의 집에 딸린 부두교 사원에 다가가자, 그가 서서 제가 오는 것을 지켜보고 있었습니다. 심장이 뛰기 시작했습니다. 그는 힘 있는 사람이라는 것을 알고 있었습니다. 그러더니 그가 웃기 시작했습니다. 제가 가까이 갈수록 그는 더 크게 웃었습니다. 처음에는 조금 어리둥절했지만, 마을 사람들이 여럿 길을 따라 저를 뒤따라오고 있다는 것을 깨달았습니다. 그들은 무슨 일이 벌어질지 몹시 궁금해했습니다. 저는 다음에 무슨 일이 일어날지 모른 채 그에게 다가갔습니다.

“목사님이십니까?” 그가 물었습니다.

“예, 그렇습니다.” 제가 대답했습니다. 그는 또다시 큰 소리로 웃기 시작했습니다.

“목사들은 다 똑같아.” 그가 단언했습니다. “모두가 자기네 교회에 오길 바라지만, 자기네 교회에는 아무 힘도 없어! 너희 교인 중 하나가 아프면 나한테 오지. 힘이 없다니까, 너희 그리스도인들!”

저는 깊은 부담을 느꼈고, 그의 말에 동의한다고 설명했습니다. 하지만 예수 그리스도의 참된 교회에는 언제나 능력이 있을 것이라고 말했습니다. 성경은 실제로 음부의 문들이 교회를 이기지 못할 것이라고 말씀합니다.

이 일은 매우 흥미로운 관계의 시작이었지만, 저는 그 말들을 결코 잊지 못할 것입니다. 틀림없이 마귀 자신에게서 나온 말이었습니다. “너희 그리스도인들에게는 아무 힘도 없어!”

그 후 저는 수백 곳의 교회를 다녔고, 그 부두교 사제의 말에 동의할 수밖에 없습니다. 기독교 교회에는 능력이 부족합니다. 하지만 왜 그럴까요? 하나님이 능력이시라는 것을 우리는 압니다. 우리는 많은 것을 갖추었고, 보기에도 좋고 말도 그럴듯하지만, 우리 교회에 여전히 하나님의 능력이 있습니까?

구약에는 능력과 능력의 결핍을 보여 주는 사례가 많이 나옵니다. 우리는 또한 어떻게 능력을 받는지, 그리고 왜 그것을 잃는지도 배울 수 있습니다.

여호수아 6장에는 이스라엘 자손과 여리고 성에 관한 익숙한 이야기가 나옵니다. 하나님께서는 여호수아와 모든 전사에게 성을 에워싸고 엿새 동안 매일 한 번씩 그 주위를 돌라고 하셨습니다. 그리고 일곱째 날에는 성 주위를 한 번이 아니라 일곱 번 돌라고 하셨습니다. 성 주위를 일곱 번 다 돈 뒤에는 제사장들이 나팔을 불어야 했습니다.

여호수아가 명령 하나하나에 순종했을 때 무슨 일이 일어났는지 우리는 압니다. 두껍고 난공불락이던 성벽들이 무너져 내렸습니다. 하나님께서는 또한 여호수아에게 사람들이 해야 할 일과 하지 말아야 할 일에 관해 엄중한 명령을 내리셨습니다. 하나님께서 저주받았다고 선포하신 모든 것에서 스스로를 지켜야 했고, 은과 금과 모든 기구는 주님의 곳간에 바쳐야 했으며, 아무도 전리품을 가져가서는 안 되었습니다.

그러나 아간은 탐나는 물건 몇 가지를 보았습니다. 그는 그것들을 갑옷 속에 슬쩍 넣었다가 나중에 자기 장막 밑에 숨겼고, 아무도 눈치채지 못했습니다.

이 큰 승리 뒤에 여호수아는 다음 성읍 아이가 얼마나 잘 요새화되어 있는지 알아보려고 정탐꾼들을 보냈습니다. 그들은 돌아와 아이를 치러 모든 사람을 보낼 필요는 없다고 여호수아에게 말했습니다. 성을 지키는 자가 얼마 되지 않았기 때문입니다.

그러나 아이 사람들이 이스라엘 자손을 쳐서 쫓아냈습니다. 여호수아는 옷을 찢고 하나님께 부르짖었습니다. 그러자 하나님께서는 이스라엘 진영에 죄가 있다고 답하셨습니다.

구약에서 이스라엘 자손은 대개 오늘날 예수 그리스도의 교회를 나타냅니다. 이 이야기에서 많은 것을 배울 수 있지 않습니까? 진영에(또는 교회에) 죄가 없었을 때 하나님의 백성은 완전한 승리를 거두어 한 사람도 잃지 않았습니다. 그들은 놀라운 일을 많이 했고, 사방의 모든 원수를 무찔렀으며, 완전한 승리 가운데 살았습니다. 그러나 죄가 그들 가운데 들어오자마자, 한 사람이 지은 작은 죄였는데도 그들은 능력을 잃었습니다. 더는 원수들을 이기지 못했습니다.

이어지는 대목은 이스라엘 자손이 진영에 들어온 죄를 어떻게 처리했는지 생생하게 묘사합니다. 그 죄는 완전히 제거되었습니다.

여호수아와 온 이스라엘이 세라의 아들 아간과 은과 겉옷과 금덩이와 그의 아들들과 딸들과 소들과 나귀들과 양들과 장막과 그가 가진 모든 것을 취하여 아골 골짜기로 데리고 갔으며 … 온 이스라엘이 그를 돌로 쳐 죽이고 그들을 불살랐더라… –여호수아 7:24-26.

이 이야기에서 하나님의 백성이 왜 능력을 잃었는지는 분명합니다. 진영에 죄가 있었기 때문입니다. 그들이 잃은 능력을 되찾으려면 무엇을 해야 했는지도 분명합니다. 죄를 제거하는 것이었습니다.

8장에서는 죄를 처리한 뒤 이스라엘의 능력이 즉시 회복되는 것을 읽습니다. 그들은 다시 승리 가운데 살았습니다!

이 주제를 다루는 또 다른 구약의 본문은 레위기 13장과 14장에 있습니다. 나병은 기이한 질병이었습니다. 누군가 나병에 걸리면 쉽게 퍼졌습니다. 따라서 이 질병을 다루는 데에는 엄격한 지침이 필요했습니다. 제사장은 해당 사람이 실제로 나병에 걸렸는지 면밀히 살펴야 했습니다. 확신이 서지 않으면 그 사람을 방에 가두어 두었다가 이레 뒤에 다시 살펴보았습니다. 나병에 걸린 것으로 판정되면 성 밖으로 내보냈습니다.

바울은 고린도 교회에 말하면서 교회 안에 죄가 있다는 소식을 들었다고 합니다. 교회가 그 일을 그토록 대수롭지 않게 여기는 데 놀란 듯합니다. …적은 누룩이 온 덩이에 퍼진다는 것을 알지 못하느냐? 그러므로 묵은 누룩을 내버리라. 그리하여 너희가 누룩 없는 자들이니 새 덩이가 되게 하라… –고린도전서 5:6-7. 뒤이어 그는 교회에 이렇게 말합니다. …그 악한 자를 너희 가운데서 내쫓으라 –고린도전서 5:13.

여러분이 사는 마을에 나병이 다시 퍼지고 있다는 소식을 들었다고 해 봅시다. 살을 파괴하는 이 질병이 다시 나타나 마을 사람 여럿이 감염되었습니다. 그러던 어느 일요일 아침, 교회에 앉아 있는데 문이 열리고 한 남자가 들어옵니다. 사지 끝에서 피부와 살이 늘어져 있습니다. 심하게 감염되었지만, 그는 그 사실을 모르는 듯합니다. 여러분은 어떻게 하시겠습니까? 그가 여러분 옆에 앉으려 한다면요? 여러분의 자녀들과 이야기하려 한다면요? 우리가 어떻게 할지 다들 알고 있으리라 생각합니다. 그를 우리 가운데 들어오게 두지 않을 것입니다. 우리는 우리 마을 사람들과 가족을 너무나 사랑하니까요.

죄는 어떻습니까? 죄가 들어와 우리와 함께하도록 허용합니까? 죄를 심각하게 받아들입니까? 살을 파괴하는 질병에 감염되는 것과 영혼을 파괴하는 죄에 감염되는 것 중 어느 쪽이 더 심각합니까? 죄의 삯은 사망, 곧 영적인 죽음이며 영원한 죽음이라는 것을 기억하십시오. 우리가 질병을 다루듯 죄를 다룬다면(그리고 마땅히 그래야 합니다), 우리 교회에는 다시 성령의 능력이 임할 것입니다.

성경은 말씀합니다. …성령이 너희에게 임하시면 너희가 능력을 받고, 예루살렘과 온 유대와 사마리아와 땅끝까지 이르러 내 증인이 되리라 –사도행전 1:8.

우리는 이미 죄가 어떻게 우리를 하나님의 능력에서 떼어 놓는지 보았고, 하나님께서 우리에게 능력을 주시고자 하신다는 것도 보았습니다. 하나님께서는 원수, 곧 마귀와 세상과 육신을 이기게 해 주시기를 원하십니다. 그러나 우리 교회들에서 무언가 일어나고 있는 듯합니다. 죄가 들어오도록 허용하고 있습니다. 설교자가 “완벽한 사람은 아무도 없습니다”라고 말하는 것을 흔히 듣습니다. 또는 “우리 모두 죄를 짓습니다”라고 합니다. 이런 말들이 얼마나 큰 해를 끼칠 수 있는지 깨닫게 되기를 바랍니다. 예수님은 우리를 모든 죄와 모든 불의에서 구원하시려고 오셨습니다. 우리가 계속 죄 가운데 살도록 내버려 둔다면, 예수님께서 우리를 위해 하신 일은 무엇입니까?

교회들이 세상에 물들어 가는 이야기를 듣습니다. 조금씩 신념을 버리고 세상의 새로운 유행과 화려함을 받아들입니다. 간음이나 술 취함 같은 심각한 죄 때문에 교회가 무너진다는 이야기는 거의 듣지 못합니다. 우리 영혼의 원수는 우리가 미지근해지기를 바랍니다. 교회가 능력을 잃고 다른 모든 사람처럼 살기 시작하기를 원합니다. 이곳 아이티에는 어디에나 교회가 있습니다. 일요일 아침 다섯 시부터 교회들이 노래하고 예배드리는 소리가 들립니다. 그러나 월요일 아침에는 그 사람들이 다 어디에 있습니까? 그들은 자신들이 떠나온 세상으로 다시 섞여 들어갑니다.

얼마 전 아이티 곳곳에 휴양지와 부동산을 소유한 매우 부유한 아이티 남성과 이야기를 나누었습니다. 그가 그리스도인인지 물었습니다. (대화를 시작하고 싶었습니다.) 그는 그렇다고 말하고 싶어 하는 듯했지만, 대신 답답한 기색을 보이며 아니라고 했습니다. 왜 그러냐고 물었습니다. 예상했던 바로 그 말을 했습니다. “그리스도인이 되고 싶어서 이 근처 교회를 다 가 봤지만, 교회들이 내게 줄 것이 아무것도 없는 것 같아. 나는 돈도 있고 육신의 복도 누리고 있어. 하지만 교회들이 구하는 건 그것뿐인 것 같아.”

오늘날 우리 교회들이 성령으로 충만해지고, 성령께서 능력을 주시고 인도하시는 것, 곧 하늘의 능력을 온전히 받는 것보다 못한 것에 만족하기를 거부한다면, 우리는 주변의 잃어버린 사람들의 마음을 끌 만한 것을 내어 줄 수 있을 것입니다. 세상이 바로 이것을 찾고 있다고 믿습니다. 그들은 더 나은 것, 초자연적인 것을 찾고 있습니다. 우리가 그보다 못한 것에는 만족하지 않는다면 어떻겠습니까? 하나님의 능력이 돌아올 때까지 무릎 꿇고 기도한다면 어떻겠습니까? 우리 자신의 영혼과 다른 사람들의 영혼을 위해 다시 눈물을 흘린다면 어떻겠습니까?

저는 이웃 마을에 사는 잔혹한 갱단 두목과 긴밀히 함께 일하고 있었습니다. 그는 마음이 완고했지만 하나님께서 그를 제게 이끄셨습니다. 긴 일곱 달 동안 우리는 만나고 연락을 주고받았습니다. 저는 그가 하나님의 능력을 조금이라도 보게 되기를 바랐고, 하나님께서 그를 구원하시기를 바랐습니다. 그는 자주 술에 취해 저를 죽이겠다고 위협했지만, 저는 계속 구주를 가리켜 보였습니다. 어느 날 그와 갱단원들이 공사 일을 막으러 와서 이제 그 땅은 자기들 소유라고 말했습니다. 그들은 총을 휘두르며 그곳에 있던 모든 사람을 위협했습니다. 저는 그 땅은 하나님의 소유라고 설명했습니다. 그는 말했습니다. “좋아. 하나님더러 여기 내려오시라고 해. 내가 그분 목을 베어 버릴 테니까.” 저는 그 말이 마음에 걸려, 방금 위협한 하나님께 얼마나 큰 능력이 있는지 알고 있느냐고 물었습니다. 어느 날 오후 그의 집으로 차를 몰고 가서, 밖에 앉아 이야기를 나누었습니다. 그날 하나님께서는 담대하게 그에게 말씀을 전하도록 이끄셨습니다. “이 갱단 생활을 그만두셔야 합니다. 하나님께서는 당신을 구원하고 마음을 바꾸시기를 원하십니다!” 제가 말을 이어 가는 동안 그는 매우 진지해 보였습니다. “누가 여기 와서 당신을 죽일지 언제 알 수 있겠습니까! 그건 당신이 통제할 수 없지만, 친구여, 죽은 뒤 어디로 갈지는 당신이 선택할 수 있습니다!” 그러고 나서 며칠 전 그가 했던 끔찍한 말을 다시 일깨워 주었습니다.

우리가 아직 이야기를 나누고 있을 때, 이웃 갱단의 남자 두 명이 오토바이를 타고 다가왔습니다. 그들은 중무장하고 있었습니다. 바로 그 순간 그를 죽이러 왔지만, 저와 그가 이야기하는 것을 보고 제가 떠날 때까지 기다렸습니다. “아내와 아이들이 있잖습니까. 이런 삶에 지치지 않으셨습니까? 하나님께서는 당신을 위해 훨씬 더 나은 것을 마련해 두셨습니다!” 저는 그의 영혼을 위해 애원하고 또 애원했습니다. 그에게는 정말 마지막 기회였습니다. 죽음이 문 앞에서 기다리고 있었습니다. 제가 떠나면서 다시 오겠다고 말했습니다.

총격이 있은 뒤 저는 서둘러 돌아갔지만, 모든 것이 끝나 있었습니다… 완전히 끝났습니다.

부활의 능력, 전능하신 하나님의 능력 가운데 살 때 비로소 그분께서 일하십니다! 주님께서 다시 오시기 전에 해야 할 일이 참으로 많다고 느끼지만, 하나님의 백성은 너무 바빠 시간이 없습니다.

오순절 운동이 성경의 가르침을 왜곡했다는 이유만으로 하나님의 능력과 성령에 관해 말하기를 두려워합니까? 하나님, 도와주소서.

구원을 위해 하나님께 부르짖을 때, 우리는 구원받아야 한다는 것, 곧 회심해야 한다는 것을 알기 때문에 그렇게 합니다. 또한 우리 스스로는 자신을 구원할 수 없다는 것을 알기에 하나님께 도와 달라고 구합니다. 하나님께서 도우시면, 전에는 할 수 없었던 일들을 할 수 있게 됩니다! 화를 잘 내던 사람이 더는 화를 내지 않습니다. 정욕을 제어하지 못하던 사람이 이제는 정욕을 제어합니다. 이기적인 사람은 다른 사람을 먼저 생각하기 시작합니다. 수줍음이 많던 사람은 담대하게 설교하기 시작합니다. 욕심 많은 사람은 다른 사람에게 베풀기 시작합니다. 하나님께서는 상담사나 의사가 할 수 없는 일을 하십니다. 사람의 가장 깊은 곳을 바꾸시고, 그러면 모든 것이 새로워집니다. 이제 우리는 이 세상이 줄 수 있는 것보다 훨씬 더 나은 것을 위해 삽니다. 하나님의 능력으로 우뚝 서서 죄로 병든 세상에 더 나은 길이 있음을 보여 줍니다!

성경 곳곳에서 하나님의 백성은 초자연적인 일을 했습니다. 그들은 그저 안락한 삶에 만족하지 않았습니다. 더 크고 더 나은 것을 추구했습니다. 예수님의 피에는 능력이 있지만, 그것이 가능해지려면 십자가가 필요했습니다. 우리도 그 능력을 찾으려면 십자가를 져야 합니다. 또 모든 사람에게 이르시되, 누구든지 나를 따라오려거든 자기를 부인하고 날마다 자기 십자가를 지고 나를 따를 것이니라. 누구든지 자기 생명을 구원하고자 하면 잃을 것이요, 누구든지 나를 위하여 자기 생명을 잃으면 구원하리라 –누가복음 9:23-24. 그렇습니다. 멸망하는 자들에게는 어리석어 보이지만, 믿는 우리에게는 하나님의 능력입니다.

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19
