Har du noen gang prøvd å forandre verden? Det har jeg. Som tenåring drømte jeg om de dristige bedriftene jeg skulle utføre for Gud. Mens jeg dekket bordet hjemme hos foreldrene mine, ventet jeg på dagen da jeg skulle kunne gjøre større ting – ting som å slå meg ned i Afrika, snakke fremmede språk og lede mennesker til Jesus. Tanken på å bo i en leirhytte og unngå giftige slanger virket spennende.

Og så gikk noen av drømmene mine i oppfyllelse! Jeg forlot alt jeg noen gang hadde kjent, og landet full av adrenalin i et afrikansk land. Jeg prøvde å forandre den lille verdenen jeg befant meg i – den gudsforlatte landsbyen, full av fyll, ødelagte ekteskap, slagsmål og forsømte barn. Hver dag kjente jeg på fortvilelsen over å være så opptatt med «ubetydelige», jordiske oppgaver, og jeg lurte på hvordan jeg kunne utgjøre en forskjell. Så ble arbeidet vårt plutselig brått avsluttet på grunn av utbrenthet og en rekke mistanker fra myndighetene. Ingenting av dette fantes i drømmene mine.

Jeg stiller fortsatt det samme spørsmålet: «Gud, hvordan kan jeg utgjøre en forskjell?» Naboen ringer på døren. Kvinnen som vasker klærne våre, skal ha lønnen sin. Lunsjen må stå på bordet om 15 minutter. Femteklassingen vår trenger hjelp med å multiplisere brøker. Himmelen fylles av mørke skyer, og klessnoren er full av klesvask. Jeg tørker babyen på nesen for tusende gang mens hun sitter oppå bordet og roter i brorens bøker og papirer. Jeg baker brød, lager yoghurt og kjerner smør, og lager 21 måltider i uken. Jeg bretter fjell av klesvask, og uken etter gjør jeg alt sammen om igjen. Jeg feier gulvet, som på bare to timer har samlet en forbløffende mengde skitt. På mange måter er livet mer hverdagslig enn det noen gang har vært før.

Jeg hadde ingen evne til å forandre verden som en drømmende tenåring, og det har jeg heller ikke nå. Gud ber meg ikke om det. Han ber meg bare om å vandre med ham og adlyde hans stemme. Sakte lærer jeg at det åndelige og det fysiske ikke kan skilles fra hverandre – selv Jesus forkynte evangeliet om riket mens han hvilte, sov og spiste. Å skrubbe et gulv og skjære brød kan være tilbedelseshandlinger for Skaperen min, hvis jeg velger å se på dem slik. Det er han som har bestemt at min åndelige vandring og utbredelsen av den skjer når hendene mine berører det jordiske. Slik blir ånden min foredlet. Det er den eneste måten jeg kan uttrykke troen min som en levende tro på. Det er den eneste måten jeg kan nå hjertene til barna mine og leve ut et praktisk evangelium som de kan etterligne. Slik viser troen min seg å være ekte for den som ikke tror, når de ser at jeg strever med de samme tingene som de gjør, og ser hvordan jeg reagerer på dem.

Sakte lærer jeg at det å tjene Gud ikke handler om besluttsomhet eller om å forandre verden. Det handler om å la Guds Ånd bo i meg, lede meg og tale til meg. Jeg lærer at Gud er mer opptatt av den personen jeg er i ferd med å bli, enn av alt jeg ønsker å gjøre for ham. Kanskje er jeg tross alt bare en rykende veke, og ikke den som skal forandre verden. Jeg tror Paulus kunne kjenne seg igjen i den følelsen da han skrev: Men Gud har utvalgt det som er tåpelig i verden, for å gjøre de vise til skamme. Gud har utvalgt det som er svakt i verden, for å gjøre det sterke til skamme. Det som er lavt i verden, det som blir foraktet, ja, det som ikke er noe, har Gud utvalgt for å gjøre til intet det som er noe, for at ingen mennesker skal rose seg overfor Gud –1. Korinter 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot sa: «Noen ganger stiger lyset opp uutholdelig langsomt. Guds rike er som surdeig og frø, ting som virker stille, i det skjulte og langsomt, men som rommer en uoverskuelig forvandlende kraft. Selv i den enkle jorden, selv i den tunge deigen, ligger muligheten for forvandling.»1

Å være opptatt av prestasjoner og suksess er en egoistisk måte å leve på. Da den landsbyen og menneskene der ble tatt fra oss i en virvelvind av saker med myndighetene og misforståelser, følte jeg at Gud umulig kunne bruke dette til beste for noen. Han trengte oss vel fortsatt der? Sannheten er at han ikke trengte oss der lenger. Vi var ikke uunnværlige. Kanskje lot Gud alt dette skje for at jeg skulle lære at hans aksept av meg ikke er basert på prestasjonene mine.

For hvem har foraktet den dagen da det begynte i det små … –Sakarja 4:10.

Hvem er jeg som skal avgjøre om en bestemt oppgave er liten eller ikke? Er jeg rastløs med pliktene mine fordi jeg tror Gud ville vært mer fornøyd hvis jeg utførte oppgaver jeg oppfatter som «store», som tilsynelatende alltid er utenfor rekkevidde? Glemmer jeg at det å tjene Kristus ikke handler om meg og min følelse av å være tilfreds, men om Gud og det arbeidet han vil gjøre gjennom meg?! Amy Carmichael sa: «Det er ikke stedet vi er på, eller arbeidet vi gjør eller ikke kan gjøre, som betyr noe; det er noe annet. Det er ilden på innsiden som brenner og skinner, uansett hvilke omstendigheter vi befinner oss i.»2

Ilden som brenner og skinner på innsiden, er hemmeligheten vår. Den ilden kan brenne mens vi skrubber gulv, lager utallige måltider og underviser barna våre hjemme. Den vil berøre kvinnen som vasker klærne, hushjelpen, jenta i menigheten som strever, og naboene. Noen ganger skjer det ubevisst, andre ganger skjer det når vi bestemmer oss for å rekke ut en hånd i stedet for å ta en lur eller gjøre noe annet vi liker, men alltid krever det at vi glemmer oss selv, elsker andre og legger merke til de små mulighetene.

Men pass på … vi må ikke forveksle det å godta at livet vårt er preget av små ting, med sløvhet. Altfor mange kristne forventer ikke at Gud skal bruke dem, og slår seg derfor til ro i en åndelig sløvhet. Vi bør forvente at Gud virker på fantastiske måter. Gud kan bruke oss til å utrette slike ting, men det skjer ofte på måter vi minst tenker på eller venter oss.

Enken i Sarepta gikk med på å gi den siste håndfullen mel og de siste dråpene med olje hun hadde, til en fremmed. Hun kunne ha satt seg opp mot profeten og krevd at han straks skulle gå, for hun hadde tross alt ansvaret for sønnen sin, og den lille mengden mel var alt hun hadde å gi ham. Men nei, hun valgte å gi alt. Gud velsignet hennes villige lydighet ved på mirakuløst vis å fylle opp melkrukken og oljekruset så lenge hun trengte det.3

Gud fortsatte å redusere Gideons hær helt til han til slutt kjempet og vant slaget med bare noen få hundre menn. Vanligvis var Gideon vant til hærer på flere tusen. og nå ba Gud ham kjempe et avgjørende slag med bare noen få hundre. Til slutt ble det som var umulig for mennesker, en anledning for Gud til å vise sin makt.4

Da Jesus begynte sin tjeneste, valgte han bare tolv menn som disipler, i stedet for folkemengdene. Til slutt forlot den lille gruppen menn ham. Han ble hånet og drept. For alle som så på, virket det som om resten av Jesu verk døde med ham, men den kosmiske frelsesplanen var i ferd med å bli satt ut i livet – disse enkle fiskerne snudde verden på hodet med evangeliet.5

Av disse eksemplene ser vi at Gud ikke leter etter de største, sterkeste eller beste. Han bruker ikke bare mennesker med spesialiserte ferdigheter eller imponerende gaver. Styrken og ressursene våre er ofte som de få hundre soldatene i Gideons hær – rett og slett ikke nok til å dekke behovet. Men når vi gir det vi har med et villig hjerte, mangfoldiggjør Gud de små anstrengelsene våre og gjør dem til et utstillingsvindu for sin nåde – et utstillingsvindu som er ment for ham, og som ofte ikke er synlig for andre. Den enkle handlingen å dekke et bord er en handling i tro, en handling der vi gir og tjener, uansett hvor vi er. Gud har valgt disse svake tingene til å ha betydning i riket sitt.

Hemmeligheten bak et vellykket liv er Jesus i oss, ikke våre forutinntatte forestillinger om suksess. Når han virker i og gjennom oss, vil hans kraft brenne i hjemmene og nabolagene våre. Når han er grunnen til at vi lever, kan vi stole på ham med utfallet. Når vi lytter til Jesu stemme, kan vi utgjøre en forskjell – én person, ett møte, én liten ting om gangen.

  1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (revidert utgave, Servant Publications 1981), etterord, s. 147
  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, s. 218
  3. 1. Kongebok 17: 11-16
  4. Dommerne 7
  5. «Lukas 6:13-16, Johannes 19»

I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.

Jeg snudde meg i sengen og lyttet til lyden av personsøkeren som pep. Det kunne ikke ha gått mer enn 15 minutter siden jeg hadde lagt meg etter den forrige innleggelsen. Jeg så på nummeret på personsøkeren. Ja, det var akuttmottaket igjen.

Jeg prøvde å gni søvnen ut av øynene og få den søvnige hjernen min til å våkne. Jeg tok opp telefonen og ringte akuttmottaket. «Hei», sa legen der. «Jeg har to pasienter som skal legges inn hos deg.»

«Å», sa jeg søvnig.

«Du høres trøtt ut», sa han spøkefullt.

Jeg var trøtt. Etter medisinstudiet gjennomgår leger en intensiv opplæringsperiode som kalles spesialisering. De to første årene av denne opplæringen innebar nattevakter på sykehuset. Det var ikke uvanlig å tilbringe hundre timer på sykehuset i løpet av en uke.

Selv når vi ikke hadde vakt, startet dagene tidlig og sluttet sent. Jeg kjempet ofte mot søvnen mens jeg kjørte hjem fra sykehuset. Jeg lærte selvfølgelig mye i løpet av denne tiden, men jeg er også glad for at de dagene er bak meg.

Tretthet er en del av det å være menneske. Alle har opplevd perioder da de har strevd med tretthet. Kanskje skyldtes det en jobb som måtte gjøres, en lang reise eller søvnløse netter fordi familien hadde fått en ny baby – uansett hva som var vanskelig, presset vi oss målbevisst videre for å komme oss gjennom disse krevende periodene.

Fra vi er barn, lærer vi at arbeid er viktig. Vi må ta ansvar og utføre oppgavene vi blir satt til.

Arbeidet er innstiftet av Gud. I Første Mosebok, kapittel 2, ga Gud Adam i oppgave å ta vare på Edens hage. Senere, i 5. Mosebok 5:13, ble israelittene befalt å utføre alt arbeidet sitt på seks dager og så hvile på den sjuende dagen.

Det nye testamentet gir et par andre grunner til å arbeide. Vi skal arbeide for å kunne forsørge familiene våre (se 2. Tessaloniker 3:10). Dessuten skal vi arbeide for å kunne gi til andre som trenger det (se Efeserne 4:28).

Gud forventer at vi arbeider, og at vi gjør det på en måte som ærer ham. Men vi trenger også hvile, og Gud har sørget for det.

Gud viste hvile gjennom skapelsen

På den sjuende dagen fullførte Gud det arbeidet han hadde gjort, og på den sjuende dagen hvilte han fra alt arbeidet han hadde gjort. Gud velsignet den sjuende dagen og helliget den, for på den dagen hvilte han fra alt arbeidet han hadde gjort da han skapte – 1. Mosebok 2:2-3.

Da Gud skapte universet, inkludert jorden og alt den rommer, tok det ham bare seks dager. Siden Gud er Gud, kan vi være sikre på at han ikke var trøtt da arbeidet var ferdig. Likevel tok han en dag til å hvile og satte den til side. Han gjorde det som et eksempel for oss.

Selv om sabbatsloven ikke skulle bli innført før minst to tusen år senere, ble mønsteret lagt ved skapelsen … Hvil én dag i uken.

Gud påla hvile i loven

Kanskje tenker vi først på sabbatsbudene som ble gitt i 2. Mosebok 20:8-11. Det ble uttrykkelig befalt at folket ikke skulle arbeide på sabbaten. Dessuten skulle de heller ikke få andre til å arbeide.

En annen lov som tydelig dreide seg om behovet for hvile, var jubelåret. I 3. Mosebok 25 påla denne loven at jorden skulle ligge brakk hele året hvert sjuende år, at slavene skulle settes fri, at jorden skulle gå tilbake til den opprinnelige familiens eiendom, og at gjeld skulle ettergis.

I jubelårsbudene lå det visse løfter. Det var et løfte om frihet – uansett hvor ille ting hadde vært de foregående seks årene, skulle man få en ny start. Det var et løfte om arv – det som var gått tapt og solgt, skulle tas tilbake. Det var et løfte om overflod – Hvis dere spør: «Hva skal vi spise i det sjuende året? Vi skal jo ikke så og heller ikke samle inn avlingen vår», da vil jeg sende min velsignelse over dere i det sjette året, så det gir avling nok for tre år – 3. Mosebok 25:20-21. Framfor alt var det et løfte om hvile fra arbeidet – for folket og jorden.

Disse budene ble ikke gitt folket for å plage dem. Gud ga dem tvert imot fordi han visste at folket hans ellers ikke ville hvile nok eller bruke nok tid på å rette oppmerksomheten mot ham, sin skaper.

Alle trenger vi perioder med hvile, men vi må forstå at det å holde sabbaten ikke bare handler om å avstå fra arbeid. Når vi prøver å holde sabbaten, må vi både hvile og tilbe, og vi må legge vekt på å ha Gud nærværende i livet vårt, uten forstyrrelser.

Det nye testamentet endret ikke behovet for hvile

Et av versene jeg kommer til å tenke på når jeg tenker på hvile, er et løfte Jesus ga. Kom til meg, alle dere som strever og bærer tunge byrder, og jeg vil gi dere hvile. Ta mitt åk på dere og lær av meg, for jeg er mild og ydmyk av hjertet, og dere skal finne hvile for sjelen. For mitt åk er godt og min byrde lett – Matteus 11:28-30.

Hebreerbrevet i Bibelen taler også om hvor viktig hvile er, og om at vi skal gå inn til Guds hvile. Altså er det fremdeles en sabbatshvile i vente for Guds folk. Den som er kommet inn til hans hvile, har også fått hvile fra sine gjerninger, slik Gud hvilte fra sine. La oss derfor gjøre alt vi kan for å komme inn til denne hvilen, så ingen faller fra på grunn av samme slags ulydighet – Hebreerne 4:9-11.

Det er viktig å se at Det nye testamentets forståelse av hvile handler om mer enn bare fri fra arbeidet. Ekte bibelsk fred er uløselig forbundet med forestillingen om fred, også midt i en kaotisk verden. Fred etterlater jeg dere. Min fred gir jeg dere, ikke den fred som verden gir. La ikke hjertet bli grepet av angst og motløshet – Johannes 14:27. Jesus ga disiplene sine en fred som gjorde at de kunne hvile, selv når de sto i svært stressende situasjoner.

Dette er en velsignelse, for det er ikke nok bare å ta fri fra det vanlige arbeidet vårt. Vi trenger den freden og roen som forbindelsen med Jesus gir. Uten … Guds fred, som overgår all forstand … – Filipperne 4:7, vil fritiden vår være like urolig som arbeidstiden.

Det er tydelig at Gud vil at vi skal hvile. Han vet at vi trenger det, ikke bare av åndelige grunner, men også for vår fysiske helse.

******************************

De som sto bak den franske revolusjonen, forsøkte å avskaffe alle fortidens institusjoner. Det var et særlig gudløst prosjekt, og blant annet besluttet den nye regjeringen å «reformere» kalenderen.

I 1793 innførte de en arbeidsuke på ti dager. Hver måned skulle ha tre uker, med én hviledag i hver av disse ukene på ti dager. Blant annet ønsket de å avskaffe alle religiøse høytidsdager og feiringen av søndagen som hviledag. De trodde at man ville få gjort mer arbeid hvis det var færre hviledager hver måned.

Dette skapte store problemer for urmakerne. De måtte på en eller annen måte lage klokker som fulgte detaljene i disse nye bestemmelsene – hvert døgn skulle ha ti timer, hver time skulle ha hundre minutter, og hvert minutt skulle være på 100 sekunder.

Det viste seg å bli en katastrofe. Folk mislikte endringene, og produktiviteten falt betraktelig i hele Frankrike. Til slutt avskaffet Napoleon dette i 1806 og gikk tilbake til den gamle kalenderen og ordningen med søndagen som hviledag. Dette vitenskapelige «eksperimentet» var over. Det viser seg at mennesker trenger perioder med hvile og påfyll, og at en uke på sju dager med én fridag til hvile ikke bare er et kristent begrep, men noe som er nødvendig for helse og velvære.

Sovjetunionen under Josef Stalin forsøkte også et lignende eksperiment for å avskaffe søndagshvilen, med lignende resultater.

******************************

Uken slik Gud skapte den (med én hviledag av sju) er nødvendig for at vi skal kunne opprettholde produktiviteten.

Hvile demper betennelse

Noe av problemet moderne mennesker står overfor, er at de har høye nivåer av stresshormoner som adrenalin og kortisol. Disse hormonene øker blodtrykket og pulsen. De øker også betennelsesnivået i kroppen.

Kronisk betennelse er ikke sunt, men heldigvis ser hvile ut til å bidra mye til å senke hormonnivåene. En god natts søvn er avgjørende for tilheling, nettopp fordi den demper disse hormonene og lar overbelastede nerver og vev heles.

Autoimmune sykdommer og smertenivåer bedres når folk får nok søvn. Blodtrykket og hjertet har også godt av at man får tilstrekkelig med søvn som gir kroppen ny kraft.

Hvile gir rom for tilheling

Trening er bra. Leger anbefaler regelmessig kondisjonstrening fordi det er sunt for hjertet, sinnet og den generelle helsen vår.

Det er ikke klokt å trene hver dag. Trening øker også nivåene av stresshormoner og gir ikke kroppen tilstrekkelig tid til å heles. De som trener for ofte og for hardt, har langt større sannsynlighet for å ende opp med plagsomme skader, ledd- og muskelsmerter og utmattelse. En studie fant at det tar 72 timer etter styrketrening før musklene er helt restituert.

De som trener, trenger ideelt sett én til to fridager i uken for å la kroppen hente seg inn etter aktiviteten. Jo hardere du trener, desto mer trenger du slike hvileperioder. Selv den som trener intensivt til noe som et maraton, må ta jevnlige dager uten løping, ellers skader vedkommende seg.

Hvile reduserer smerte

Det er gjort mange studier der man har undersøkt folks søvnrapporter og sett på ting som kroniske smerter og spenningshodepine. Minst 50 prosent av dem som lider av søvnløshet, har også kroniske smerter. Det kan selvfølgelig ganske enkelt være at personer med kroniske smerter ikke sover like godt som personer som ikke har slike smerter.

Flere studier har undersøkt smertetoleransen hos folk etter søvnmangel. De fant at selv én eneste natt uten søvn var nok til at folk opplevde smerte sterkere.

Hvile styrker immunforsvaret

Flere studier har undersøkt funksjonen til ulike deler av immunforsvaret vårt og funnet at de fungerer bedre når deltakerne får nok søvn. Trolig øker den høyere betennelsen vi får når vi ikke hviler, risikoen for infeksjon.

Når vi presser oss for hardt uten å hvile, belaster det immunforsvaret. På den annen side er den beste måten å hente seg inn på å sørge for at vi får nok hvile.

Hvile har også mange andre virkninger. Den bidrar til bedre humør. Den kan hjelpe med skoleprestasjoner og hukommelsesoppgaver.

Som med alt annet er måtehold viktig. Den som ikke gjør annet enn å hvile og sove, vil ikke fungere bedre enn den som sover godt i sju timer om natten, og vil heller ikke være særlig produktiv.

Det finnes noen grunnleggende regler som kan hjelpe oss med å få hvileperioder.

Hvil regelmessig

Sabbatens budskap er at vi trenger å sette av korte, regelmessige perioder til hvile. Jubelårene forteller oss at vi også trenger lengre perioder med påfyll, men sjeldnere. Det krever innsats og planlegging å sørge for at disse periodene virkelig gir hvile.

Kanskje er det litt som med en bil. Du kan bare kjøre så langt på én tank bensin. Hvis du alltid venter med å fylle tanken til varsellampen lyser, vil det før eller siden skje at du er for langt fra en bensinstasjon til å fylle før tanken går tom. Det passer aldri å gå tom for bensin. På samme måte må vi med jevne mellomrom lade opp de åndelige, følelsesmessige og fysiske batteriene våre. Det er ingen grunn til å vente til varselsignalene viser at vi virkelig trenger en pause.

Hvile krever forberedelser

Fortellingen om mannaens gave i 2. Mosebok 16 viser oss at manna kom hver dag. Folket kunne ikke spare den til neste dag, for da ble den dårlig. Men på fredager skulle de samle ekstra, siden den neste dagen var en hviledag og det ikke kom manna på sabbaten. De som ikke hadde samlet ekstra dagen før, gikk sultne.

På samme måte krever slike perioder forberedelser. Det blir ikke lett, men det er viktig.

Gjør sunne ting når du hviler

Når folk er stresset, har de lett for å spise usunt. Når folk er utslitte, har de vanligvis ikke lyst til å trene eller gå tur. Dette er nettopp den typen ting som virkelig kan hjelpe oss med å lade opp igjen, både fysisk og følelsesmessig.

Også dette krever en innsats, men det er viktig for helsen og velværet vårt å velge sunne alternativer.

Vend oppmerksomheten mot Gud

Jeg har latt dette vente til slutt, men det er det viktigste ved hvilen. Ekte hvile kommer ikke av medisiner eller selv av flere ferier, men av et hjerte fylt av fred. Freden som overgår forstanden, kommer fra et hjerte som er vendt mot Gud.

Bønnestundene og bibellesingen vår bør være perioder med hvile. Hvis vi kan fjerne forstyrrelser og utfordringene fra arbeids- og hjemmelivet og rette blikket mot ham som betyr mest, vil vi få en virkelig velsignelse og det påfyllet ånden vår trenger.

Jeg er redd for at mange strever med å finne hvile fordi de ikke virkelig har fred. La oss derfor gjøre alt vi kan for å komme inn til denne hvilen, så ingen faller fra på grunn av samme slags ulydighet – Hebreerne 4:11. Hvilen det er snakk om her, er lovet dem som holder ut og tar imot Guds fred.

Avslutning

Livet handler om balanse. Noen ganger må vi arbeide, og andre ganger bør vi hvile. Å finne denne balansen er utfordringen hver enkelt av oss står overfor. Én ting er sikkert: Hver dag på 24 timer vil være helt full når vi kommer til slutten av den.

Gud ser oss og våre begrensninger, og han ønsker at vi skal finne balanse mellom arbeidet og hvileperiodene våre. Hvis vi bare kan rette oppmerksomheten mot ham, vil vi få veiledning til å finne denne balansen.

Framfor alt vil vi få en fred som er uvurderlig, og som gjør at vi kan finne hvile – selv midt i en storm.

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

तेरे युवाकाल की ओस तेरे साथ है। भजन संहिता 110:3

युवावस्था के अनेक पहलू सद्गुणपूर्ण नहीं होते। हमारे समय के बहुत-से युवा आरंभिक उम्र में ही कठोर लापरवाही और विनाश के दौर का अनुभव करते हैं। अक्सर युवावस्था में लिए गए निर्णय उनके शेष जीवन की नींव रख देते हैं। वह छोटा उड़ाऊ भाई ही था जिसने अपनी विरासत में से हिस्सा पहले ही माँगा और फिर जाकर उसे ऐयाशी में उड़ा दिया। वह युवा दीना ही थी जो अपने पिता के घर से निकलकर …देश की लड़कियों को देखने गई—उत्पत्ति 34:1। वहाँ वह उस देश के विधर्मी जवानों के संपर्क में आई और एक खूनी नरसंहार का कारण बनी, जिससे याकूब उस देश में दुर्गंध के समान हो गया। बहुत-से मूर्ख जवानों ने हवा बोई है और उसके विनाशकारी परिणाम काटे हैं। जिनमें दृढ़ सिद्धांतों और माता-पिता के अधिकार का अभाव है, उनके लिए आत्मिक जहाज़-भंग का जोखिम बहुत अधिक है।

कुछ विशेष अभिलाषाएँ ऐसी हैं जो वृद्धों की अपेक्षा युवाओं को अधिक सताती हैं, और युवाओं को उनसे भागने की सीख दी गई है। (—देखें 2 तीमुथियुस 2:22) सुलैमान ने अपनी खिड़की से बाहर देखा, और भोले लोगों में मैंने देखा, युवाओं में मैंने एक ऐसे जवान को पहचाना जिसमें समझ का अभाव था—नीतिवचन 7:6-7। उस जवान का मन उस चीज़ को पाने में लगा था जो मनोहर दिखाई देती थी… [जब तक] एक तीर उसके कलेजे को भेद न गया; जैसे पक्षी फंदे की ओर दौड़ता है और नहीं जानता कि यह उसके प्राणों के लिए है—नीतिवचन 7:23। हम रहूबियाम, अम्नोन, नादाब और अबीहू तथा अनगिनत अन्य लोगों के युवाकाल के दुर्गुणों की पड़ताल कर सकते हैं। हमारे चारों ओर आज भी हल्के-फुल्के युवाओं द्वारा किए गए मूर्खतापूर्ण कामों के आधुनिक उदाहरणों की कोई कमी नहीं है।

लेकिन युवाओं को तुच्छ नहीं समझना चाहिए। कोई तेरी जवानी को तुच्छ न समझे; पर तू विश्वास करनेवालों के लिये वचन, चालचलन, प्रेम, आत्मा, विश्वास और पवित्रता में आदर्श बन—1 तीमुथियुस 4:12। वास्तव में, परमेश्वर सामान्यतः अपने संदेश के प्रसार के साधन के रूप में युवाओं को चुनता है। उत्तम चरित्र वाले यूसुफ को परमेश्वर ने सत्रह वर्ष की आयु में जीवन बचाने के लिए मिस्र भेजा (—देखें उत्पत्ति 45:5)। बारह वर्ष की मरियम ने पूरे यहूदी राष्ट्र के भावी उद्धारकर्ता की रखवाली की और अपने ही माता-पिता, योकेबेद, को बालक मूसा की धाय बनने की व्यवस्था की। दाऊद को, युवावस्था में, सेना में अपने भाइयों का हौसला बढ़ाने भेजा गया। उसके भाइयों ने उसे तुच्छ समझा: …मैं तेरे अभिमान और तेरे मन की बुरी बातों को जानता हूँ…—1 शमूएल 17:28। शाऊल ने उसे ठुकराया: …तू इस पलिश्ती से युद्ध करने को उसके विरुद्ध नहीं जा सकता; क्योंकि तू तो लड़का ही है…—1 शमूएल 17:33। गोलियत ने उसका उपहास किया: …क्या मैं कुत्ता हूँ कि तू लाठियाँ लेकर मेरे पास आता है…—1 शमूएल 17:43। परन्तु जब परमेश्वर ने उसे समस्त इस्राएल पर राजा होने के लिए चुना, तब उनका तिरस्कार व्यर्थ सिद्ध हुआ।

युवावस्था की इन उदात्त आकांक्षाओं के बाद योशिय्याह, यशायाह, यिर्मयाह, दानिय्येल, मरियम और प्रभु के चेले आए—इन सबने अपनी जवानी के दिनों में अपने सृष्टिकर्ता को स्मरण रखना चुना। परन्तु ये भोले-भाले लोग नहीं थे जो जीवन में अपना स्थान सुरक्षित करना चाहते थे; ये उन युवाओं के सजीव उदाहरण थे जो अपने प्रभु के स्वरूप का अनुकरण करना चाहते थे।

मसीह के चरित्र में अधिक देर तक निहारने की आवश्यकता नहीं कि हम पाएँ…

...तेरे युवाकाल की ओस

भजन संहिता 110 शायद पुराने नियम में सबसे अधिक उद्धृत धर्मशास्त्र-वचन है। मसीहा का यह अलंकारपूर्ण चित्र हमारे सामने निहारने के लिए एक स्पष्ट सद्गुण प्रकट करता है। मसीह, जो सनातन परमेश्वर हैं, प्रकाशितवाक्य में ऐसे वर्णित हैं कि उनका सिर और बाल… ऊन के समान श्वेत, वरन् हिम के समान उज्ज्वल थे…—प्रकाशितवाक्य 1:14, फिर भी यहाँ उन्हें अनन्तकाल तक युवा दर्शाया गया है, जब वे परमेश्वर के दाहिने हाथ बैठते हैं (—देखें भजन संहिता 110:1)। वहाँ आयु की कोई थकान प्रवेश नहीं कर सकती, क्योंकि मसीह भोर के तारे हैं। परमेश्वर के सिंहासन के चारों ओर निरंतर भोर रहती है। जो संत उनकी समानता पाने के लिए पूरे मन से लगे रहते हैं, वे भी इस सद्गुण को प्रतिबिम्बित करेंगे, क्योंकि यीशु का प्रकाश ही युवावस्था का प्रकाश है।

मसीहा का वर्णन करते हुए भजनकार सुबह की ओस की प्राकृतिक सुंदरता का सहारा लेता है (—देखें भजन संहिता 110:3)। ओस का विचार हमें स्वर्ग से लौटाकर उस पृथ्वी का चित्र दिखाता है जिस पर हम रहते हैं। स्वर्ग में न रात है, न गर्मी-सर्दी का बदलाव, न दिन को प्रकाशमान करने के लिए सूर्य की आवश्यकता और इसलिए… वहाँ ओस भी नहीं। ओस का स्वभाव पृथ्वी का है, जहाँ जो कोई झुककर उसे देखने का प्रयास करे, उसे घास का एक समान पंक्तिबद्ध दल दिखाई देगा, जो मानो असंख्य हीरों से जड़ा हुआ चमक रहा हो। अँधेरी रात के लंबे समय के बाद, फूलों की आँखों में ओस की बूँदें आँसुओं की तरह ठहर जाती हैं, मानो वे सूर्य की पहली किरण के आगमन पर आनंद से रो रहे हों। जो लोग नीची वनस्पतियों के बीच से चलते हैं, उनके पैरों को परमेश्वर की रचना के हजारों स्नेहिल हाथ धो देते हैं। मसीह को सुबह की ओस नहीं, बल्कि युवावस्था की ओस कहा गया है, और यह चित्रण आगे और विस्तृत होता है।

युवावस्था प्रचुर ऊर्जा का समय है। कुछ लोग स्थिर बैठ ही नहीं सकते। वे आम तौर पर मिलनसार होते हैं और सामाजिक गतिविधियों से प्रेम करते हैं। यह न सद्गुण है, न दुर्गुण; यह तो बस सामान्य स्वभाव है। बढ़ती उम्र के साथ एक क्रमिक तनाव आता है जो आत्मा को संयमित और संतुलित करता है। जीवन आगे बढ़ने पर दृष्टि अधिक स्पष्ट और विचार अधिक स्थिर होता जाता है, और हम बेहतर बातों की ओर बढ़ते हैं। लेकिन जब मध्यजीवन का शिखर पार हो जाता है और पैर ढलान पर नीचे की ओर चलने लगते हैं, तब शरीर की ऊर्जा का वह उथल-पुथल भरा वेग, जो हर बाधा को चीरता हुआ आगे बढ़ता था, अतीत की स्मृतियों में बस जाता है। बहुतों को अपनी बीती हुई शक्ति के दिनों का इससे अधिक निकट का सांत्वनादायक स्मरण नहीं मिलता।

लेकिन मसीह ने हमें अतीत के प्रति लगाव बढ़ाने या अपनी जवानी के “जोश” की लालसा करने के लिए नहीं बुलाया है। आज बहुत-से लोग दुख के साथ विलाप करते हैं कि उनका “उठकर चल पड़ने का दम” उठकर चला गया है। उन्हें ऊँची बातों की कोई दृष्टि नहीं, और वे युवावस्था की ओस की अपेक्षा माउंटेन ड्यू के डिब्बे से अधिक ऊर्जा पाते हैं। आगे की आशा से अधिक वे स्मृतियों की गलियों में घूमने और बीते दिनों की घटनाएँ याद करने से प्रेरित होते हैं।

युवावस्था की ओस पाने में उम्र कोई बाधा नहीं है। सनातन परमेश्वर अब भी सोने की दीवटों के बीच चलते हैं। यूहन्ना ने उनके बाल… ऊन के समान श्वेत, वरन् हिम के समान उज्ज्वल…—प्रकाशितवाक्य 1:14 देखे, फिर भी सुलैमान कहता है …उसके घुँघराले बाल घने और कौवे के समान काले हैं—श्रेष्ठगीत 5:11। यद्यपि उम्र हमारी शक्ति और सुनने की क्षमता छीन सकती है, …यहोवा का हाथ ऐसा छोटा नहीं हो गया कि उद्धार न कर सके, और न उसका कान ऐसा भारी हो गया है कि सुन न सके—यशायाह 59:1। उसने युवावस्था की ओस सुरक्षित रखी है और हमें उसमें भाग लेने का निमंत्रण देता है। समस्या हमारे क्षीण होते शरीर में नहीं, बल्कि आत्मिक रूप से गिरते मन में है। वृद्धावस्था का अभिशाप मुख्यतः तब आरंभ होता है जब मन शरीर का अनुसरण करता है।

ऐसा नहीं है कि जीवन आगे बढ़ने पर दरिद्र हो जाता है या युवावस्था का आकर्षण मिटने पर उदात्त रहना छोड़ देता है। यदि हमें यहाँ केवल आनंद अनुभव करने के लिए रखा गया होता, तो युवावस्था के प्रेमभाव का बुझ जाना भयानक होता। परमेश्वर ने अपने बच्चों के लिए केवल जोश से “काम करने” से कहीं बड़ा उद्देश्य रखा था। हमें यहाँ सीखने के लिए भेजा गया है। पृथ्वी पर हमें मिले वर्ष सब सीखने के लिए हैं, और हम सबसे अच्छे तथा सबसे स्थायी पाठ युवावस्था के उज्ज्वल प्रेमभाव में नहीं सीखते। हम उन्हें अपने कर्तव्य को अडिग होकर निभाने, अपनी सीमाओं को शांतिपूर्वक स्वीकार करने, रोज़ का बोझ धैर्य से उठाने और अपने भाई की सहायता के लिए हाथ बढ़ाने में सीखते हैं। ये हमें मसीही चरित्र-निर्माण के सच्चे अवसर देते हैं और नैतिक उदात्तता की जड़ें हैं। मसीह ने उस भोजन के लिये परिश्रम न किया जो नाश होता है, परन्तु उस भोजन के लिये जो अनन्त जीवन तक ठहरता है…—यूहन्ना 6:27, और उन्होंने अपना पार्थिव कार्य 33 वर्षों में पूरा किया। परन्तु जब वे अपने पिता के दाहिने हाथ बैठे, तब युवावस्था की ओस मिट नहीं गई।

इस प्रकार, हम निष्कर्ष निकालते हैं कि यह यौवन शक्ति से नहीं, बल्कि…

...आशा

परन्तु यह व्यक्ति पापों के लिये सदा के लिये एक ही बलिदान चढ़ाकर परमेश्वर के दाहिने जा बैठा; और उसी समय से इसकी बाट जोह रहा है कि उसके बैरी उसके पाँवों की पीढ़ी बनें।—इब्रानियों 10:12-13।

अब हमें इस मसीह का चित्र किस रूप में देखना चाहिए? क्या वे आरामकुर्सी पर पड़े हैं, इस पृथ्वी के हठी लोगों के साथ अपने अनुभव से पूरी तरह थक चुके हैं? क्या वे अनमोल स्मृतियों की कोई यादगार पुस्तक बना रहे हैं? वृद्ध लोगों की स्थिति अक्सर ऐसी ही होती है, और इसलिए उनका मन उनके शरीर के साथ ही मर जाता है।

केवल यही नहीं, वरन् हम क्लेशों में भी घमण्ड करें, यह जानकर कि क्लेश से धीरज, और धीरज से खरा निकलना, और खरे निकलने से आशा उत्पन्न होती है—रोमियों 5:3-4। कभी-कभी हम सोचते हैं कि क्या यह वचन सच हो सकता है। जिसकी हड्डियों में उम्र आ चुकी है, वह खराब अनुभव और उसके बाद आने वाली निराशा की भावनाओं की गवाही दे सकता है। मनुष्य होने के नाते, हम सबने जीवनसाथी, बच्चे या कलीसिया के किसी संबंध के साथ निराशाजनक अनुभवों का सामना किया है, जिसके बाद निराशा का एक सताने वाला बादल छा जाता है। मसीह से बाहर, कड़वा अनुभव हमेशा निराशावाद की ओर ले जाता है। जब यीशु आए, तब संसार में ऐसा ही था। आज भी ऐसा ही है।

लेकिन युवावस्था की ओस में आशा की ऐसी शक्ति है जिसे मिटाया नहीं जा सकता। युवावस्था में स्वाभाविक रूप से और अद्भुत ढंग से एक उत्साहपूर्ण अपेक्षा जन्म लेती है और मसीह में बनी रहती है। हर सर्दी में, जब खेत सूने होते हैं और ठंडी हवा पेड़ों के बीच सीटी बजाती हुई निकलती है, तब यह आशा रहती है कि फूल फिर खिलेंगे। हर वसंत में ग्रीष्म की आशा होती है। हर ग्रीष्म में कटनी की आशा होती है। यह प्रकृति में भी जीवित है और युवावस्था में भी। जो इसके प्रति अंधे हैं, वे अधिक-से-अधिक एक नीरस, एकसुरी जीवन काटेंगे। जीना संसार की सबसे दुर्लभ बात है। अधिकतर लोग बस अस्तित्व में रहते हैं, और कुछ नहीं।—ऑस्कर वाइल्ड।

बाकी लोग आशा से उज्ज्वल रूप से प्रभावित होंगे, जो…

…हमारी दुर्बलताओं को चंगा करती है

हमारे शरीर कब्र के लिए नियत हैं और इस जीवन में उनके नए किए जाने की कोई आशा नहीं। हमारी सबसे बड़ी दुर्बलताएँ हमारे मन में हैं। बेथेस्दा का अड़तीस वर्ष से लाचार मनुष्य, जब मसीह ने उससे पूछा, …क्या तू चंगा होना चाहता है?—यूहन्ना 5:6। तो केवल निराशा से भरी शिकायत ही कर सका। उसके नए दिन के आरंभ पर उसे एक नया उपाय दिया गया—…देख, तू चंगा हो गया है; फिर पाप मत करना, ऐसा न हो कि इससे भी बुरी दशा तेरी हो जाए—यूहन्ना 5:14। वर्षों तक अपंग रहने से भी बुरा क्या हो सकता है? ऐसा मन जो इस संसार के दुखों में उदासीपूर्वक डूबा हुआ हो। उम्र तब हावी होती है जब कल की आशा की अपेक्षा अतीत की यादें अधिक हों। जब लोग बूढ़े हो जाते हैं और कल के लिए कोई दृष्टि नहीं रखते, तो यह निराशाजनक है; लेकिन युवाओं को उसके अपंग कर देने वाले प्रभावों से पीड़ित देखना एक विपत्ति है। बहुत-से लोग जीवन की विभिन्न परीक्षाओं से बिना दिशा के भटकते रहते हैं, और आशीष के अभाव से स्तब्ध होते हैं। दोपहर के सूर्य ने उनकी युवावस्था की ओस को सुखा दिया है, और वे जितनी प्रशंसा कर पाते हैं, वह बीते कल की मुट्ठी-भर सुखद बातों से ही आती है। नई सुबह की ओस से एक नया मनोभाव जन्म लेना चाहिए।

…हमारी आकांक्षाओं को नम्र करती है

मैं तुझ से सच सच कहता हूँ, जब तू जवान था, तो अपनी कमर बाँधकर जहाँ चाहता था वहाँ फिरता था; परन्तु जब तू बूढ़ा होगा, तो अपने हाथ फैलाएगा, और दूसरा तेरी कमर बाँधकर जहाँ तू न चाहेगा वहाँ तुझे ले जाएगा।—यूहन्ना 21:18। जब हम जवान होते हैं, तो अपनी जवानी की शक्ति से विजय पा सकते हैं। जैसे-जैसे उम्र अपना असर दिखाती है, हम एक अलग विकल्प पाएँगे: समर्पण के द्वारा विजय।

…मैं ने तुम्हें, हे जवानों, इसलिये लिखा है, कि तुम बलवन्त हो, और परमेश्वर का वचन तुम में बना रहता है, और तुम ने उस दुष्ट पर जय पाई है।—1 यूहन्ना 2:14। संसार हमें स्वार्थपूर्ण जीवन बिताने के लिए लुभाता है। युवाओं को अक्सर ऐसी शिक्षा-संस्थाओं में पढ़ना पड़ता है जो उन्हें सिखाती हैं कि “तुम जो कुछ बन सकते हो, वह सब बनो।” खुद को बेहतर बनाने और भविष्य की तैयारी पर बहुत अधिक ध्यान दिया जाता है। यह उन्हें “योग्यतम की उत्तरजीविता” वाले संसार के लिए तैयार कर सकता है, लेकिन जब युवावस्था की शक्ति और सामर्थ्य चली जाएगी, तो उन्हें बेसहारा छोड़ देगा।

क्योंकि जो कुछ संसार में है, अर्थात् शरीर की अभिलाषा, और आँखों की अभिलाषा, और जीविका का घमण्ड, वह पिता की ओर से नहीं, परन्तु संसार ही की ओर से है। और संसार और उसकी अभिलाषाएँ दोनों मिटते जाते हैं, पर जो परमेश्वर की इच्छा पर चलता है वह सर्वदा बना रहेगा।—1 यूहन्ना 2:16-17। भलाई से बुराई पर विजय पाना युवावस्था की ऊर्जा को सही दिशा देने का बाइबिलीय उपाय है। चाहे अभिलाषा भीतर हो या लालसा बाहर, किसी दूसरे के जीवन में दयालुता का बीज बोने से आशा जन्म लेती है। सुख और आराम की खोज अपने पानेवाले को हमेशा निराश करेगी और उसे उस घाटी से भी गहरे निराशा के गड्ढे में छोड़ देगी जहाँ से उसने शुरुआत की थी। मनुष्य के लिये अपनी जवानी में जूआ उठाना भला है… वह धूल में मुँह रखे, कदाचित् कुछ आशा हो।—विलापगीत 3:27-29। हमें परमेश्वर की दाख की बारी में काम करने के लिए बनाया गया है, और जिनमें इसके लिए लालसा है वे इसके युवावस्था के प्रतिफल की आशा में फल पाएँगे।

…हमारी परीक्षाओं को पवित्र करती है

क्योंकि आशा से हमारा उद्धार हुआ है; परन्तु जिस वस्तु की आशा की जाती है, जब वह देखने में आए तो फिर आशा कहाँ रही…—रोमियों 8:24। हम कितनी बार अपने दुःख में अय्यूब से जुड़ाव महसूस कर सकते हैं। परन्तु उसके दुःख का एक अंश भी प्रतिफलित होने से पहले ही, जब अय्यूब ने अपने सृष्टिकर्ता का आदर किया, तो चंगाई की धाराएँ बहने लगीं। जब हम यह स्वीकार कर पाते हैं कि परमेश्वर जिन परीक्षाओं की अनुमति देते हैं, उन सब में वे सिद्ध हैं, तब हम हाथों से न बने मन्दिर में आराधना करना सीखते हैं और शरीर की दुर्बलताओं की परवाह छोड़ देते हैं। मसीह के चरणों में बैठना युवावस्था की एक चिंगारी प्रज्वलित करता है, जो भीतर की आत्मा को आलोकित करती और आशा को जन्म देती है। तब युवावस्था की ओस हमारा भाग बन जाती है, क्योंकि मसीह हमें अनन्त जीवन और अनन्त यौवन देते हैं। कब्र की घड़ी से लेकर अनन्तकाल तक हम जवान रहेंगे और थकान तथा मृत्यु को चुनौती देंगे, यदि हम यीशु मसीह के भोर के प्रकाश में जी रहे हों। स्वर्ग निरंतर यौवन का स्थान है; और जैसे सूर्य का प्रकाश चंद्रमा पर प्रतिबिम्बित होता है, वैसे ही मसीह का प्रकाश उनकी दुल्हिन पर प्रतिबिम्बित होता है। वह शुद्ध और जवान है, …एक महिमामयी कलीसिया, जिसमें न कलंक, न झुर्री, न कोई ऐसी वस्तु हो…—इफिसियों 5:27। धन्य है वह आदरणीय संत जो ऐसी दशा में स्वर्ग के द्वार तक पहुँचता है।
