I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.

Virei-me na cama, ouvindo o som do meu pager a tocar. Não podiam ter passado mais de 15 minutos desde que me deitara depois da minha última admissão. Olhei para o número no pager. Sim, era o Serviço de Urgência outra vez.

Tentei esfregar o sono dos olhos e despertar o meu cérebro, ainda sonolento. Peguei no telefone e liguei para o serviço de urgência. «Olá», disse o médico do serviço de urgência. «Tenho duas admissões para si.»

«Ah», respondi, sonolento.

«Parece cansado», disse ele, em tom de brincadeira.

Eu estava cansado. Depois de se formarem em Medicina, os médicos passam por um período de formação intensiva chamado residência. Os primeiros dois anos dessa formação incluíam turnos noturnos no hospital. Não era invulgar trabalhar cem horas no hospital numa semana.

Mesmo quando não estávamos de prevenção, os dias começavam cedo e acabavam tarde. Muitas vezes lutava contra o sono enquanto conduzia para casa, vindo do hospital. Certamente aprendi muito durante esse período, mas também fico feliz por esses dias já terem ficado para trás.

A fadiga faz parte da condição humana. Todos já passaram por momentos em que tiveram dificuldade com o cansaço. Talvez fosse devido a um trabalho que precisava de ser feito, a uma viagem longa ou a noites sem dormir por causa de um bebé recém-nascido na família — fosse qual fosse a dificuldade, esforçamo-nos com determinação para atravessar esses períodos desafiantes.

Desde a infância, ensinam-nos que o trabalho é importante. Precisamos de ser responsáveis e de cuidar das tarefas que nos são atribuídas.

O trabalho foi ordenado por Deus. Em Génesis, capítulo 2, Deus deu a Adão a tarefa de cuidar do Jardim do Éden. Mais tarde, em Deuteronómio 5:13, os israelitas receberam a ordem de fazer todo o seu trabalho em seis dias e depois descansar no sétimo.

O Novo Testamento apresenta mais algumas razões para trabalharmos. Devemos trabalhar para poder sustentar as nossas famílias (ver II Tessalonicenses 3:10). Além disso, devemos trabalhar para poder ajudar os que têm necessidade (ver Efésios 4:28).

Deus espera que trabalhemos e que o façamos de uma forma que O glorifique. No entanto, também precisamos de descansar, e Deus providenciou isso.

Deus deu o exemplo do descanso na Criação

E, havendo Deus acabado no dia sétimo a obra que fizera, descansou no sétimo dia de toda a sua obra que tinha feito. E abençoou Deus o dia sétimo, e o santificou; porque nele descansou de toda a sua obra que Deus criara e fizera –Génesis 2:2-3.

Quando Deus criou o universo, incluindo a terra e tudo o que ela contém, levou apenas seis dias. Sendo Deus, podemos ter a certeza de que não estava cansado no fim desse trabalho. Ainda assim, apesar disso, tirou um dia de descanso e separou-o dos outros. Fê-lo como exemplo para nós.

Embora a lei do sábado só fosse instituída pelo menos dois mil anos mais tarde, o precedente foi estabelecido na Criação… Descansar um dia por semana.

Deus ordenou o descanso na Lei

Talvez a primeira coisa que nos venha à mente sejam as leis relativas ao dia de sábado, dadas em Êxodo 20:8-11. Foi ordenado especificamente que o povo não trabalhasse no sábado. Além disso, não devia fazer com que outras pessoas trabalhassem.

Outra lei que parecia centrar-se bastante na necessidade de descanso era a do Ano do Jubileu. Em Levítico 25, essa lei determinava que, de sete em sete anos, a terra ficasse em pousio durante todo o ano, os escravos fossem libertados, as terras voltassem a pertencer à família a que originalmente pertenciam e as dívidas fossem canceladas.

As ordens relativas ao Jubileu incluíam certas promessas. Havia a promessa de liberdade — por pior que tivessem sido as coisas nos seis anos anteriores, haveria um recomeço. Havia a promessa de herança — as coisas que tinham sido perdidas e vendidas seriam recuperadas. Havia a promessa de abundância — E, se disserdes: Que comeremos no sétimo ano? Eis que não havemos de semear, nem colher o nosso produto. Então eu mandarei a minha bênção sobre vós no sexto ano, e ela dará fruto por três anos –Levítico 25:20-21. Acima de tudo, havia a promessa de descanso do trabalho — para o povo e para a terra.

Essas ordens não foram impostas ao povo para o afligir. Pelo contrário, Deus deu-as sabendo que, sem elas, o Seu povo não descansaria o suficiente nem dedicaria tempo bastante a concentrar-se n’Ele, o seu Criador.

Todos precisamos de períodos de descanso, mas temos de compreender que guardar o sábado não se resume a abster-se do trabalho. Os nossos esforços para guardar o sábado devem incluir tanto o descanso como a adoração, e devem ser marcados pela presença de Deus na nossa vida, sem distrações.

O Novo Testamento não alterou a necessidade de descanso

Um dos versículos que me vem à mente quando penso no descanso é uma promessa feita por Jesus. Vinde a mim, todos os que estais cansados e oprimidos, e eu vos aliviarei. Tomai sobre vós o meu jugo, e aprendei de mim, que sou manso e humilde de coração; e encontrareis descanso para a vossa alma. Porque o meu jugo é suave e o meu fardo é leve –Mateus 11:28-30.

O livro bíblico de Hebreus também fala da importância do descanso e de entrarmos no descanso de Deus. Portanto, resta ainda um repouso para o povo de Deus. Porque aquele que entrou no seu repouso, ele próprio repousou das suas obras, como Deus das suas. Procuremos, pois, entrar naquele repouso, para que ninguém caia no mesmo exemplo de desobediência –Hebreus 4:9-11.

É importante perceber que o conceito de descanso no Novo Testamento é mais do que simplesmente ter tempo livre do trabalho. A verdadeira paz bíblica está intrinsecamente ligada ao conceito de paz, mesmo no meio de um mundo caótico. Deixo-vos a paz, a minha paz vos dou; não vo-la dou como o mundo a dá. Não se turbe o vosso coração, nem se atemorize –João 14:27. Jesus deu aos Seus seguidores uma paz que lhes permitia descansar, mesmo quando enfrentavam níveis elevados de stress.

Isto é uma bênção, pois não basta simplesmente tirar tempo livre do nosso trabalho habitual. Precisamos de ter a paz e a tranquilidade que a ligação com Jesus oferece. Sem …a paz de Deus, que excede todo o entendimento… –Filipenses 4:7, o nosso tempo livre será tão inquieto como o tempo que passamos a trabalhar.

É evidente que Deus quer que descansemos. Ele sabe que precisamos disso, não apenas por razões espirituais, mas também para a nossa saúde física.

******************************

Os responsáveis pela Revolução Francesa tentaram eliminar todas as instituições do passado. Foi uma iniciativa particularmente ímpia e, entre outras coisas, o novo governo decidiu «reformar» o calendário.

Em 1793, instituíram uma semana de trabalho de dez dias. Cada mês teria três semanas, com um dia de descanso em cada uma dessas semanas de dez dias. Entre outros objetivos, queriam eliminar todos os feriados religiosos e a celebração do domingo como dia de descanso. Acreditavam que se trabalharia mais tendo menos dias de descanso por mês.

Isso criou uma enorme dor de cabeça para os relojoeiros. Precisavam de encontrar uma forma de fabricar relógios que correspondessem aos pormenores desses novos decretos — cada dia teria dez horas, cada hora teria cem minutos e cada minuto teria 100 segundos.

Acabou por ser um desastre. O povo detestou as mudanças e a produtividade caiu consideravelmente em toda a França. Por fim, em 1806, Napoleão aboliu o sistema e voltou ao calendário antigo e ao sistema de descanso aos domingos. Essa «experiência» científica chegou ao fim. Acontece que as pessoas precisam de períodos de descanso e recuperação, e que uma semana de sete dias com um dia de folga para descansar não é apenas um conceito cristão: é algo necessário para a saúde e o bem-estar.

A União Soviética, sob o governo de Josef Stalin, também tentou uma experiência semelhante, eliminando o descanso ao domingo, com resultados semelhantes.

******************************

A semana, tal como Deus a criou (com um dia de descanso em cada sete), é necessária para continuarmos produtivos.

O descanso reduz a inflamação

Parte do problema que as pessoas enfrentam hoje é terem níveis elevados de hormonas do stress, como a adrenalina e o cortisol. Essas hormonas aumentam a pressão arterial e a frequência cardíaca. Também aumentam os níveis de inflamação no nosso corpo.

A inflamação crónica não é saudável, mas, felizmente, o descanso parece ajudar bastante a baixar esses níveis hormonais. Uma boa noite de sono é essencial para a recuperação, precisamente porque reduz essas hormonas e permite a recuperação dos nervos e tecidos sobrecarregados.

As doenças autoimunes e os níveis de dor melhoram quando as pessoas dormem o suficiente. A pressão arterial e as doenças cardíacas também beneficiam quando uma pessoa dorme o suficiente para recuperar.

O descanso permite a recuperação

O exercício é algo bom. Os médicos recomendam a prática regular de exercício cardiovascular porque faz bem ao coração, à mente e ao bem-estar geral.

Não é sensato fazer exercício todos os dias. O exercício também aumenta os níveis das hormonas do stress e não dá ao nosso corpo tempo suficiente para recuperar. As pessoas que se exercitam com demasiada frequência e intensidade têm muito mais probabilidades de acabar com lesões persistentes, dores articulares e musculares e fadiga. Um estudo concluiu que os músculos levam 72 horas a recuperar totalmente depois de um treino com pesos.

Idealmente, as pessoas que fazem exercício precisam de um ou dois dias de descanso por semana para permitir que o corpo recupere da atividade. Quanto mais intensamente treinar, mais precisará desses períodos de descanso. Mesmo alguém que esteja a treinar intensivamente para algo como uma maratona precisa de tirar dias sem correr de vez em quando, ou irá lesionar-se.

O descanso reduz os níveis de dor

Foram realizados muitos estudos que analisaram os relatos das pessoas sobre o sono e aspetos como a dor crónica e as dores de cabeça tensionais. Pelo menos 50 por cento das pessoas com insónia também sofrem de dor crónica. É claro que pode simplesmente acontecer que as pessoas com dor crónica não durmam tão bem como as que não têm esse problema.

Vários estudos analisaram a tolerância à dor das pessoas depois de serem privadas de sono. Concluíram que até mesmo uma única noite sem dormir era suficiente para que as pessoas sentissem a dor de forma mais intensa.

O descanso melhora o nosso sistema imunitário

Vários estudos analisaram o funcionamento de diferentes partes do nosso sistema imunitário e concluíram que funcionam melhor quando os participantes dormem o suficiente. É provável que o facto de os níveis de inflamação serem mais elevados quando não descansamos aumente o risco de infeção.

Quando nos esforçamos demasiado sem descansar, isso sobrecarrega o nosso sistema imunitário. Por outro lado, a melhor forma de recuperar é garantir que descansamos o suficiente.

O descanso faz muitas outras coisas. Ajuda a melhorar o humor. Pode ajudar no desempenho académico e em tarefas que dependem da memória.

Como em tudo, a moderação é fundamental. Alguém que não faça outra coisa senão descansar e dormir não terá um funcionamento melhor do que alguém que dorme bem sete horas por noite, nem será muito produtivo.

Há algumas regras básicas que nos podem ajudar a reservar períodos de descanso.

Descanse regularmente

A mensagem do sábado é que precisamos de reservar regularmente períodos curtos para descansar. Os Anos do Jubileu ensinam-nos que também precisamos de períodos mais longos e menos frequentes para recuperar. É preciso esforço e planeamento para garantir que esses períodos sejam verdadeiramente repousantes.

Talvez seja um pouco como um carro. Só é possível percorrer determinada distância com um depósito de combustível. Se esperar sempre que a luz de aviso acenda para encher o depósito, acabará por acontecer que esteja demasiado longe de uma estação de serviço para o encher antes de ficar sem combustível. Nunca é uma boa altura para ficar sem combustível. Da mesma forma, precisamos de recarregar periodicamente as nossas baterias espirituais, emocionais e físicas. Não há motivo para esperar que apareçam sinais de alerta de que precisamos urgentemente de fazer uma pausa.

O descanso exige preparação

A história do dom do maná em Êxodo 16 ensina-nos que havia maná todos os dias. O povo não podia guardá-lo para o dia seguinte, porque se estragava. No entanto, às sextas-feiras, deviam recolher uma quantidade extra, pois o dia seguinte era de descanso e não havia maná no sábado. Os que não tinham recolhido uma quantidade extra no dia anterior passavam fome.

Da mesma forma, é preciso preparação para ter períodos deste tipo. Não será fácil, mas é importante.

Faça coisas saudáveis durante o descanso

As pessoas tendem a comer coisas pouco saudáveis quando estão sob stress. Quando estão exaustas, normalmente não lhes apetece fazer exercício nem dar passeios. No entanto, são precisamente esse tipo de coisas que podem ajudar-nos a recuperar, tanto física como emocionalmente.

Mais uma vez, isto exige algum esforço, mas escolher opções saudáveis é importante para o nosso bem-estar.

Concentre-se em Deus

Deixei este ponto para o fim, mas é o aspeto mais importante do descanso. O verdadeiro descanso nasce não da medicação, nem mesmo de várias férias, mas de um coração cheio de paz. A paz que excede o entendimento vem de um coração concentrado em Deus.

Os nossos momentos de oração e leitura da Bíblia devem ser momentos de descanso. Se conseguirmos eliminar as distrações e os desafios do trabalho e da vida em casa, e fixar o olhar n’Aquele que mais importa, receberemos uma verdadeira bênção e a renovação de que o nosso espírito precisa.

Receio que muitas pessoas tenham dificuldade em encontrar descanso por não estarem verdadeiramente em paz. Procuremos, pois, entrar naquele repouso, para que ninguém caia no mesmo exemplo de desobediência –Hebreus 4:11. O descanso aqui é aquele que está prometido aos que perseveram e recebem a paz de Deus.

Conclusão

A vida depende do equilíbrio. Há momentos em que precisamos de trabalhar e também há momentos em que devemos descansar. Encontrar esse equilíbrio é o desafio que cada um de nós enfrenta. Uma coisa é certa: cada período de 24 horas estará completamente preenchido quando chegarmos ao seu fim.

Deus vê-nos, vê as nossas limitações e deseja que alcancemos esse equilíbrio entre o trabalho e os períodos de descanso. Se conseguirmos concentrar-nos n’Ele, receberemos orientação para encontrar esse equilíbrio.

Acima de tudo, receberemos uma paz sem preço, que nos permitirá encontrar descanso — mesmo durante uma tempestade.

I’ll walk with God—Today—
Tomorrow may not be.
I’ll make the best of TIME—right now—
That God has granted me.

I’ll plan not for a life
That I might live in ease,
But only for today to live
My God alone to please.

Nor dare I think in years
Or move from leaps to bounds;
With God shut out, and self shut in
And selfish aims surround.

There are those who plan their lives,
Who give God little thought;
Who weigh themselves, not with God’s truth,
As every day they ought!

“Boast not thyself,” I’m warned,
“Of what tomorrow brings;
Thy health and wealth—e’en life itself—
May all at once take wings!”

“This night, that soul of thine
May be required of thee:
And dost thou plan the New Year full
There, ‘neath some Christmas tree?”

“Wake up! Take stock, are you prepared?
Your lessons learned alright?
If God, in yet three hours, THIS DAY,
Should close your course TONIGHT?”

","section":"Poem","subtitle":null,"title":"Today"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"name":"Marvin L. Fieldhouse"}],"raw":"by Marvin L. Fieldhouse"}},"target_language":"German","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Ich geh mit Gott – heute –
Morgen vielleicht nicht mehr.
Ich nutze DIE ZEIT – jetzt gleich –
Die Gott mir geschenkt hat.

Ich plane nicht für ein Leben,
In dem ich sorglos leben könnt,
Sondern nur für diesen Tag,
Um allein meinem Gott zu gefallen.

Auch wage ich nicht, in Jahren zu denken
Oder weite Sprünge zu machen;
Gott ausgeschlossen, das eigene Ich eingeschlossen,
Umgeben von selbstsüchtigen Zielen.

Es gibt Menschen, die ihr Leben planen
Und kaum an Gott denken;
Die sich nicht an Gottes Wahrheit messen,
wie sie es jeden Tag tun sollten!

„Rühme dich nicht“, wird mir gesagt,
„dessen, was der Morgen bringt;
deine Gesundheit und dein Wohlstand – ja, selbst dein Leben –
können plötzlich davongeflogen sein!“

„Noch diese Nacht kann deine Seele
von dir gefordert werden:
Und planst du dort, unter einem Weihnachtsbaum,
schon das ganze neue Jahr?“

„Wach auf! Zieh Bilanz: Bist du bereit?
Hast du deine Lektionen gut gelernt?
Wenn Gott in nur drei Stunden, noch an DIESEM TAG,
heute Nacht deinen Lauf beenden sollte?“

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (revised edition Servant Publications 1981) epilogue pg 147
  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19

Έχεις προσπαθήσει ποτέ να αλλάξεις τον κόσμο; Εγώ έχω. Ως έφηβη ονειρευόμουν τα τολμηρά κατορθώματα που θα έκανα για τον Θεό. Καθώς έστρωνα το τραπέζι στο πατρικό μου σπίτι, περίμενα τη μέρα που θα μπορούσα να κάνω μεγαλύτερα πράγματα—όπως να εγκατασταθώ στην Αφρική, να μιλώ παράξενες γλώσσες και να οδηγώ ανθρώπους στον Ιησού. Η σκέψη ότι θα ζούσα σε μια καλύβα από λάσπη και θα απέφευγα δηλητηριώδη φίδια μού φαινόταν συναρπαστική.

Και τότε, ένα μέρος των ονείρων μου έγινε πραγματικότητα! Άφησα πίσω μου όλα όσα γνώριζα και προσγειώθηκα σε μια αφρικανική χώρα γεμάτη αδρεναλίνη. Προσπάθησα να αλλάξω τον μικρό κόσμο στον οποίο βρέθηκα—εκείνο το χωριό, εγκαταλειμμένο από τον Θεό, γεμάτο μέθη, διαλυμένους γάμους, καβγάδες και παραμελημένα παιδιά. Κάθε μέρα ένιωθα την αγωνία του να είμαι τόσο απασχολημένη με «ασήμαντες», επίγειες δουλειές και αναρωτιόμουν πώς θα μπορούσα να κάνω τη διαφορά. Ύστερα, ξαφνικά, οι κόποι μας έλαβαν απότομα τέλος λόγω εξουθένωσης και μιας σειράς υποψιών από την κυβέρνηση. Τίποτα από αυτά δεν υπήρχε στα όνειρά μου.

Εξακολουθώ να κάνω την ίδια ερώτηση: «Θεέ μου, πώς μπορώ να κάνω τη διαφορά;» Η γειτόνισσα χτυπά την πόρτα. Η γυναίκα που πλένει τα ρούχα χρειάζεται τα χρήματά της. Το μεσημεριανό πρέπει να είναι στο τραπέζι σε 15 λεπτά. Το παιδί μας που πηγαίνει στην πέμπτη τάξη χρειάζεται βοήθεια με τον πολλαπλασιασμό κλασμάτων. Ο ουρανός γεμίζει με μαύρα σύννεφα και το σκοινί είναι γεμάτο απλωμένα ρούχα. Σκουπίζω τη μύτη του μωρού για πολλοστή φορά, καθώς κάθεται πάνω στο τραπέζι και ανακατεύει τα βιβλία και τα χαρτιά του αδελφού της. Ψήνω ψωμί, φτιάχνω γιαούρτι, χτυπώ βούτυρο και μαγειρεύω 21 γεύματα την εβδομάδα. Διπλώνω βουνά από ρούχα και την επόμενη εβδομάδα τα ξανακάνω όλα από την αρχή. Σκουπίζω το πάτωμα, που μέσα σε μόλις δύο ώρες έχει μαζέψει απίστευτη ποσότητα βρομιάς. Από πολλές απόψεις, η ζωή είναι πιο μονότονη από ποτέ.

Δεν μπορούσα να αλλάξω τον κόσμο όταν ήμουν μια έφηβη με το κεφάλι στα σύννεφα, και ούτε τώρα μπορώ. Ο Θεός δεν μου ζητά κάτι τέτοιο. Μου ζητά μόνο να περπατώ μαζί Του και να υπακούω στη φωνή Του. Σιγά σιγά μαθαίνω ότι το πνευματικό και το σωματικό είναι αχώριστα—ακόμη και ο Ιησούς δίδασκε το ευαγγέλιο της βασιλείας ενώ ξεκουραζόταν, κοιμόταν και έτρωγε. Το τρίψιμο του πατώματος και το κόψιμο του ψωμιού μπορούν να γίνουν πράξεις λατρείας προς τον Δημιουργό μου, αν εγώ τις θεωρήσω έτσι. Εκείνος σχεδίασε ώστε η πνευματική μου πορεία και η διάδοσή της να πραγματοποιούνται καθώς τα χέρια μου αγγίζουν τα γήινα. Έτσι εξευγενίζεται το πνεύμα μου. Είναι ο μόνος τρόπος με τον οποίο μπορώ να εκφράσω την πίστη μου ως ζωντανή πίστη. Είναι ο μόνος τρόπος να αγγίξω τις καρδιές των παιδιών μου και να ζήσω μπροστά τους ένα πρακτικό ευαγγέλιο, που μπορούν να μιμηθούν. Έτσι η πίστη μου αποδεικνύεται αληθινή στον άπιστο, καθώς με βλέπει να παλεύω με τα ίδια πράγματα που αντιμετωπίζει κι εκείνος, αλλά και να βλέπει τις αντιδράσεις μου ως αποτέλεσμα.

Σιγά σιγά μαθαίνω ότι η υπηρεσία προς τον Θεό δεν έχει να κάνει με την αποφασιστικότητα ή με την αλλαγή του κόσμου. Έχει να κάνει με το να επιτρέπω στο Πνεύμα του Θεού να κατοικεί μέσα μου, να με καθοδηγεί και να μου μιλά. Μαθαίνω ότι ο Θεός ενδιαφέρεται περισσότερο για το πρόσωπο που γίνομαι, παρά για όλα όσα θέλω να κάνω για Εκείνον. Ίσως τελικά να είμαι απλώς ένα φυτίλι που καπνίζει, κι όχι εκείνη που θα αλλάξει τον κόσμο. Νομίζω πως ο Παύλος θα μπορούσε να καταλάβει αυτό το συναίσθημα, όταν έγραψε: Ο Θεός διάλεξε τα ανόητα του κόσμου για να καταισχύνει τους σοφούς· και τα αδύναμα του κόσμου διάλεξε ο Θεός για να καταισχύνει τα ισχυρά· και τα ευτελή του κόσμου και τα περιφρονημένα διάλεξε ο Θεός, και όσα δεν υπάρχουν, για να καταργήσει όσα υπάρχουν· ώστε κανένας άνθρωπος να μην καυχηθεί μπροστά Του –Α΄ Κορινθίους 1:27-29.

Η Ελίζαμπεθ Έλιοτ είπε: «Μερικές φορές το φως ανατέλλει οδυνηρά αργά. Η Βασιλεία του Θεού μοιάζει με προζύμι και σπόρο, πράγματα που ενεργούν σιωπηλά, κρυφά, αργά, αλλά μέσα τους υπάρχει μια δύναμη μεταμόρφωσης που δεν μπορεί να μετρηθεί. Ακόμη και στο απλό χώμα, ακόμη και στην άνοστη ζύμη, υπάρχει η δυνατότητα της μεταμόρφωσης.»1

Το να έχω προσηλωμένη την καρδιά μου στα επιτεύγματα και στην επιτυχία είναι ένας εγωιστικός τρόπος ζωής. Όταν εκείνο το χωριό και εκείνοι οι άνθρωποι απομακρύνθηκαν από κοντά μας μέσα στη δίνη κυβερνητικών ζητημάτων και παρεξηγήσεων, ένιωσα πως ήταν αδύνατο ο Θεός να το χρησιμοποιήσει αυτό για το καλό οποιουδήποτε. Εξακολουθούσε να μας χρειάζεται εκεί, έτσι δεν είναι; Η αλήθεια είναι ότι δεν μας χρειαζόταν πια εκεί. Δεν ήμασταν αναντικατάστατοι. Ίσως ο Θεός να το επέτρεψε όλο αυτό για να μάθω ότι η αποδοχή Του δεν βασίζεται στα επιτεύγματά μου.

Γιατί ποιος καταφρόνησε την ημέρα των μικρών πραγμάτων… –Ζαχαρίας 4:10.

Ποια είμαι εγώ για να κρίνω αν ένα έργο είναι μικρό ή όχι; Ανυπομονώ για τα καθήκοντά μου, πιστεύοντας ότι ο Θεός θα ευαρεστούνταν περισσότερο αν έκανα εκείνα που εγώ θεωρώ «μεγάλα» καθήκοντα, τα οποία μοιάζουν πάντα απρόσιτα; Μήπως ξεχνώ ότι η υπηρεσία στον Χριστό δεν αφορά εμένα και το αίσθημα πληρότητάς μου, αλλά τον Θεό και το έργο που θέλει να κάνει μέσω εμού;! Η Έιμι Κάρμιχαελ είπε: «Δεν έχει σημασία ο τόπος όπου βρισκόμαστε ούτε το έργο που κάνουμε ή δεν μπορούμε να κάνουμε· σημασία έχει κάτι άλλο. Είναι η φωτιά μέσα μας που καίει και λάμπει, όποιες κι αν είναι οι περιστάσεις μας.»2

Η φωτιά που καίει και λάμπει μέσα μας είναι το μυστικό μας. Αυτή η φωτιά μπορεί να καίει ενώ τρίβουμε πατώματα, μαγειρεύουμε ατέλειωτα γεύματα και εκπαιδεύουμε τα παιδιά μας στο σπίτι. Θα αγγίξει τη γυναίκα που πλένει τα ρούχα, την οικιακή βοηθό, την κοπέλα που δυσκολεύεται στην εκκλησία και τους γείτονες. Μερικές φορές αυτό θα συμβεί υποσυνείδητα· άλλες, όταν αποφασίσουμε να απλώσουμε το χέρι μας αντί να πάρουμε έναν υπνάκο ή να κάνουμε κάτι άλλο ευχάριστο. Πάντα, όμως, απαιτεί να ξεχνάμε τον εαυτό μας, να αγαπάμε τους άλλους και να προσέχουμε τις μικρές ευκαιρίες.

Προσέξτε, όμως… δεν πρέπει να συγχέουμε την αποδοχή της μικρότητας στη ζωή μας με την αδράνεια. Πάρα πολλοί Χριστιανοί δεν περιμένουν ότι ο Θεός θα τους χρησιμοποιήσει, κι έτσι βολεύονται σε μια πνευματική κατάσταση αδράνειας. Θα πρέπει να περιμένουμε ότι ο Θεός θα ενεργήσει με θαυμαστούς τρόπους. Ο Θεός μπορεί να μας χρησιμοποιήσει για να πραγματοποιήσει αυτά τα πράγματα, αλλά συχνά αυτό συμβαίνει με τρόπους που ούτε φανταζόμαστε ούτε περιμένουμε.

Η χήρα της Σαρεπτά συμφώνησε να δώσει την τελευταία χούφτα αλεύρι και τις τελευταίες σταγόνες λαδιού που της είχαν απομείνει σε έναν ξένο. Θα μπορούσε να αντιταχθεί στον προφήτη και να απαιτήσει να φύγει αμέσως, αφού άλλωστε ήταν υπεύθυνη για τον γιο της κι εκείνη η ελάχιστη ποσότητα αλευριού ήταν ό,τι είχε για να του δώσει. Όμως όχι, επέλεξε να τα δώσει όλα. Ο Θεός ευλόγησε την πρόθυμη υπακοή της, αναπληρώνοντας θαυματουργικά το αλεύρι και το λάδι της για όσο διάστημα τα χρειαζόταν.3

Ο Θεός συνέχισε να μειώνει τον στρατό του Γεδεών, ώσπου τελικά εκείνος πολέμησε και νίκησε στη μάχη με λίγες μόνο εκατοντάδες άντρες. Συνήθως ο Γεδεών ήταν συνηθισμένος σε στρατούς χιλιάδων αντρών, και τώρα ο Θεός τού ζητούσε να δώσει μια αποφασιστική μάχη με λίγες μόνο εκατοντάδες. Στο τέλος, αυτή η ανθρωπίνως αδύνατη αποστολή έγινε ευκαιρία για τον Θεό να φανερώσει τη δύναμή Του.4

Στην αρχή της διακονίας Του, ο Ιησούς επέλεξε να μαθητεύσει μόνο δώδεκα άντρες, αντί για τα πλήθη. Τελικά, εκείνη η μικρή ομάδα αντρών Τον εγκατέλειψε. Τον χλεύασαν και Τον σκότωσαν. Σε όσους παρακολουθούσαν, το έργο του Ιησού φαινόταν να έχει πεθάνει μαζί Του, κι όμως το κοσμικό σχέδιο της λύτρωσης έμπαινε σε εφαρμογή—εκείνοι οι απλοί ψαράδες έφεραν τον κόσμο άνω κάτω με το ευαγγέλιο.5

Από αυτά τα παραδείγματα βλέπουμε ότι ο Θεός δεν αναζητά τους πιο μεγάλους, τους πιο δυνατούς ή τους καλύτερους. Δεν χρησιμοποιεί μόνο ανθρώπους με εξειδικευμένες δεξιότητες ή εντυπωσιακά χαρίσματα. Η δύναμη και οι πόροι μας συχνά μοιάζουν με τους λίγους εκατοντάδες στρατιώτες του στρατού του Γεδεών—απλώς δεν επαρκούν για την ανάγκη. Όταν όμως προσφέρουμε ό,τι έχουμε με πρόθυμη καρδιά, ο Θεός πολλαπλασιάζει τις μικρές προσπάθειές μας και τις κάνει επίδειξη της χάρης Του—μια επίδειξη που προορίζεται για Εκείνον και συχνά δεν είναι ορατή στους άλλους. Η απλή πράξη του να στρώνουμε ένα τραπέζι είναι πράξη πίστης, προσφοράς και υπηρεσίας, όπου κι αν βρισκόμαστε. Ο Θεός επέλεξε αυτά τα αδύναμα πράγματα για να έχουν σημασία στη βασιλεία Του.

Το μυστικό μιας επιτυχημένης ζωής είναι ο Ιησούς μέσα μας, όχι οι προκατασκευασμένες ιδέες μας για την επιτυχία. Καθώς εργάζεται μέσα μας και μέσω ημών, η δύναμή Του θα καίει στα σπίτια και στις γειτονιές μας. Όταν Εκείνος είναι ο λόγος για τον οποίο ζούμε, μπορούμε να Τον εμπιστευτούμε για την έκβαση. Ακούγοντας τη φωνή του Ιησού, μπορούμε να κάνουμε τη διαφορά—έναν άνθρωπο, μια συνάντηση, ένα μικρό πράγμα κάθε φορά.

  2. Έιμι Κάρμιχαελ, Edges of His Ways, σ. 218
  3. Α΄ Βασιλέων 17: 11-16
  4. Κριτές 7
  5. Λουκάς 6:13-16, Ιωάννης 19

I’ll walk with God—Today—
Tomorrow may not be.
I’ll make the best of TIME—right now—
That God has granted me.

I’ll plan not for a life
That I might live in ease,
But only for today to live
My God alone to please.

Nor dare I think in years
Or move from leaps to bounds;
With God shut out, and self shut in
And selfish aims surround.

There are those who plan their lives,
Who give God little thought;
Who weigh themselves, not with God’s truth,
As every day they ought!

“Boast not thyself,” I’m warned,
“Of what tomorrow brings;
Thy health and wealth—e’en life itself—
May all at once take wings!”

“This night, that soul of thine
May be required of thee:
And dost thou plan the New Year full
There, ‘neath some Christmas tree?”

“Wake up! Take stock, are you prepared?
Your lessons learned alright?
If God, in yet three hours, THIS DAY,
Should close your course TONIGHT?”

Jag vandrar med Gud — i dag —
I morgon kanske inte finns.
Jag gör det bästa av TIDEN — just nu —
som Gud har skänkt mig.

Jag planerar inte för ett liv
där jag kan leva bekvämt,
utan bara för att i dag leva
så att endast min Gud blir nöjd.

Jag vågar inte heller tänka i år
eller ta språng efter språng;
när Gud stängs ute och jag stänger in mig
och själviska mål omger mig.

Det finns de som planerar sina liv
och knappt tänker på Gud;
som inte prövar sig själva mot Guds sanning,
fast de borde göra det varje dag!

”Skryt inte”, blir jag varnad,
”om vad morgondagen för med sig;
din hälsa och rikedom — ja, själva livet —
kan plötsligt fara sin kos!”

”I natt kan din själ
krävas tillbaka av dig:
Och planerar du ett helt nytt år
där, under någon julgran?”

”Vakna! Se över läget: är du redo?
Har du verkligen lärt dig läxorna?
Om Gud om bara tre timmar, JUST I DAG,
skulle sätta punkt för ditt liv I NATT?”

{"correction_findings":[{"location":"Poem, stanza 6","severity":"major","source_quote":"“My chosen one, I alone can fulfill, that for which your heart yearns.”","suggested_fix":"Keep the existing tags and translate the line as, for example: «Min utvalda, endast jag kan uppfylla det som ditt hjärta längtar efter.»","translation_quote":"”Min utvalda, Endast jag kan uppfylla det som ditt hjärta längtar efter."},{"location":"Poem, stanza 8","severity":"major","source_quote":"“Yet the promise remains, all works out well, For him that in God does delight.”","suggested_fix":"Translate the promise without adding the specific idea of things ‘working together’: for example, «Ändå står löftet fast: allt blir väl för den som har sin glädje i Gud.»","translation_quote":"Ändå består löftet: allt samverkar till det bästa för den som har sin glädje i Gud."},{"location":"Poem, stanza 10","severity":"minor","source_quote":"“While others lives go on so free.”","suggested_fix":"Use a Swedish expression that conveys others’ lives going on freely, such as «medan andra kan leva så fritt vidare».","translation_quote":"medan andras liv går vidare så obehindrat."}],"language_guidance":"Use standard contemporary Swedish.","language_tag":"sv","source":{"html":"

Sometimes my heart is heavy,
Weighted with fears and care.
It’s then my Lord calls out to me,
“Come My child, your burden I’ll bear.”

Sometimes questions flood my mind,
The answers seem evasive and trying.
That’s when I lift these eyes to my God,
Claiming His love on me overlying.

Sometimes I feel like quitting,
The way before me seems long and hard.
But I think of the path of my Shepherd,
It was for me He was scarred.

Sometimes my mind is clouded,
I stumble with each step that I take.
Yet out of the fog, I hear a whisper,
“You are Mine, trust Me, a way I will make.”

Sometimes I find my circumstances,
Seemingly harsh, and unfair.
But then my Father whispers,
“Dear one, do not despair.”

Sometimes I feel all alone,
The ache within chokes and burns.
The Master speaks, “My chosen one,
I alone can fulfill, that for which your heart yearns.

Sometimes my eyes are full of tears
My heart feels near to burst.
And then my Savior reminds me,
This path, before me, He traversed.

Sometimes I worry and wonder,
How things will ever turn out right.
Yet the promise remains, all works out well,
For him that in God does delight.

Sometimes the future seems scary,
Not at all like what I had hoped.
Still, I set my eyes on His ultimate goal,
Knowing it’s better than for what I had groped.

Sometimes I feel left behind,
While others lives go on so free.
But, in my Father’s plans I will trust,
And look forward to His eternal jubilee!

Sometimes I find myself dreaming,
Of the future in heaven to come.
Oh what bliss will be the feeling,
To hear those words, “Well done.”

","section":"Poem","subtitle":null,"title":"Sometimes"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"name":"Adrianna Fanton"}],"raw":"~by Adrianna Fanton"}},"target_language":"Swedish","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Ibland är mitt hjärta tungt,
Tyngt av oro och bekymmer.
Då ropar min Herre till mig,
”Kom, mitt barn, jag bär din börda.”

Ibland väller frågor fram i mitt sinne,
Svaren tycks undflyende och svårfångade.
Då lyfter jag blicken mot min Gud,
Och gör anspråk på hans kärlek, som vilar över mig.

Ibland känner jag för att ge upp,
Vägen framför mig tycks lång och svår.
Men jag tänker på min herdes väg,
Det var för mig han blev sårad.

Ibland är mitt sinne omtöcknat,
Jag snubblar för varje steg jag tar.
Men ur dimman hör jag en viskning,
”Du är min, lita på mig, jag ska bana en väg.”

Ibland tycks mina omständigheter
hårda och orättvisa.
Men då viskar min Fader,
”Kära barn, misströsta inte.”

Ibland känner jag mig helt ensam,
Värken inom mig kväver och bränner.
Mästaren säger: ”Min utvalda,
Endast jag kan uppfylla det som ditt hjärta längtar efter.

Ibland är mina ögon fulla av tårar,
Mitt hjärta känns nära att brista.
Då påminner min Frälsare mig:
Den väg som ligger framför mig har han vandrat.

Ibland oroar jag mig och undrar
hur allt någonsin ska ordna sig.
Ändå består löftet: allt samverkar till det bästa
för den som har sin glädje i Gud.

Ibland känns framtiden skrämmande,
Inte alls som jag hade hoppats.
Ändå fäster jag blicken på hans slutgiltiga mål,
för jag vet att det är bättre än det jag famlade efter.

Ibland känner jag mig lämnad bakom,
medan andras liv går vidare så obehindrat.
Men jag ska lita på min Faders planer
och se fram emot hans eviga jubel!

Ibland finner jag mig själv drömma
om den kommande framtiden i himlen.
Å, vilken salighet det ska vara
att höra orden: ”Bra gjort.”

","section":"Dikt","subtitle":null,"title":"Ibland"}}

After living in Haiti for several months, I finally had the opportunity to go visit the local witch doctor. As I walked up his long drive, I passed many statues and satanic symbols. It was eerie for sure. As I approached the voodoo temple that was connected to his house, I saw him standing there watching me approach. My heart began to race; I knew he was a powerful man. Then he began to laugh. The closer I got, the louder he laughed. I was a bit puzzled until I realized that many people from the village were following me up the lane. They were very interested in what was about to transpire. I approached the man, not knowing what would happen next.

“Are you a pastor?” he asked.

“Yes, I am,” was my reply. Again, he began to laugh loudly.

“You pastors are all the same,” he proclaimed. “You want everyone to come to your churches, but your churches have no power! When one of your people gets sick, they come to me. No power, you Christians!”

A heavy burden overtook me, and I explained to him how I agreed with him, but that the real church of Jesus Christ would always have power. The Bible actually says that the very gates of Hell shall not prevail against it.

This was the beginning of a very interesting relationship, but I will never forget those words—most certainly from the devil himself—“You Christians have no power!”

I have since traveled to hundreds of churches and need to agree with that voodoo priest. The Christian churches are lacking power. But why? We know that God is power. We have many things figured out, we look good and sound good, but do we still have the power of God in our churches?

In the Old Testament we have many examples of power and the lack of power. We can also learn how we receive power, and why we lose it.

In Joshua, chapter 6, we have the familiar account of the children of Israel and the city of Jericho. God tells Joshua and all the men of war to compass the city, and walk around it once every day, for six days. Then on the seventh day they were to march around the city not just once, but seven times. After they had completed the seven trips around the city, the priests were to blow their trumpets.

We know what happened when Joshua obeyed each command—those thick, impenetrable walls came tumbling down. God also gave Joshua a strict command about what the men should and should not do. They were to keep themselves from everything that God had pronounced was accursed; all the silver, gold, and vessels were to be consecrated into the treasury of the Lord; no man was to take any of the spoil.

However, Achan saw some nice things that he desired. He slipped them into his armor, then later hid them under his tent, and no one saw a thing.

After this great victory, Joshua sent spies to the next city, Ai, to discover how well the city was fortified. The men returned and told Joshua not to send all the men to Ai, for there were only a few defenders protecting the city.

However, the men of Ai smote the children of Israel and chased them away. Moreover, Joshua rent his clothes and cried out to God. Then God replied that there was sin in the camp of Israel.

In the Old Testament, the children of Israel are normally representative of the church of Jesus Christ today. Can we not glean much from this account? When there was no sin in the camp (or in the church) God’s people had complete victory; they lost not one. They did many wonderful things, they destroyed all their enemies around them, and they lived in COMPLETE victory. However, as soon as sin entered into their midst, even a small sin done by one man, they lost their power. They no longer had victory over their enemies.

What follows is a graphic description of how the children of Israel dealt with the sin that had entered the camp. It was totally destroyed.

And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor … And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire… –Joshua 7:24-26.

In this account it is clear why God’s people had lost their power—they had sin in the camp. It is also clear what it took for them to regain that power which they had lost—get rid of the sin.

In chapter 8 we read of the power being restored to Israel instantly after the sin was dealt with. Again, they lived in victory!

Another passage in the Old Testament that speaks of this topic is in Leviticus chapters 13 and 14. Leprosy was a strange disease. If one were to get leprosy, it was easily spread. Thus, there needed to be some strict guidelines regarding how to deal with the disease. The priest was to examine very closely to see if the person in question indeed had leprosy or not. If the priest was unsure, he would shut the person up in a room for seven days then examine him again. If it was determined that the person had leprosy, then they were sent outside of the city.

As Paul addresses the church in Corinth, he tells them that he has heard there is sin in the church. He seems surprised that the church is taking it so casually, …Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump? Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened… –1 Corinthians 5:6-7. Later he tells the church …Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person –1 Corinthians 5:13.

Let’s say that you heard the news that leprosy was again a problem in your village. This flesh-destroying disease had made a comeback and many from your village were now infected. Then you’re sitting in church on Sunday morning, when the doors open, and a man enters with skin and flesh hanging from his extremities. He is badly infected, but he does not seem to know it. What would you do? What if he wanted to come sit by you? What if he wanted to talk to your children? I think we all know what we would do; we would not allow him into our midst. We love our people, our families too much for that.

What about sin? Do we allow sin to come and join us? Do we take it seriously? What is worse, being infected with a flesh-destroying disease, or being infected by a soul-destroying sin? Remember, the wages of sin is death—spiritual death; eternal death. If we would treat sin in the same way as we would the disease (and we should) then our churches would once again have Holy Spirit power.

The Bible says …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

We have already seen how sin separates us from the power of God, and we have also seen how God wants to give us power. He wants us to have victory over the enemy—the devil, the world, and flesh. However, something seems to be happening in our churches—we are allowing sin to enter. It is common to hear a preacher say, “No one is perfect.” Or, “We all sin.” Oh, that we would realize the damage these statements can make. Jesus came to save us from ALL sin; ALL unrighteousness. If we are left to continue in our sin, what has Jesus done for us?

I hear about churches drifting into the world. They gradually let go of convictions and allow some new fashion and pomp of the world to enter. Something that I hear little of is churches falling apart because of gross sin, such as fornication or drunkenness. The enemy of our souls, desires for us to become lukewarm. He wants the church to lose its power, to start living like everyone else. Here in Haiti, there are churches everywhere. On Sunday mornings starting at five o’clock in the morning, I start hearing the churches singing and worshipping. However, where are all those people on Monday morning? They are mixing right back into the world from whence they have come.

I was recently talking to a very wealthy Haitian man who owned resorts and properties all over Haiti. I asked him if he was a Christian. (I wanted to start a conversation.) I could tell that he wanted to say yes; instead, he became frustrated and said no. I asked him why not. He said exactly what I thought he would say. “I have desired to become a Christian, I’ve gone to all the churches around here, but I don’t feel they have anything to offer me. I have money; I have physical blessings; but that seems to be all that they are seeking for.”

If our churches today would refuse to settle for anything less than the infilling, empowering, and leading of the Holy Spirit, a full dose of heavenly power, then we would be able to offer something that would appeal to the lost around us. I believe this is exactly what the world is looking for; they are seeking for something better, something supernatural. What if we would settle for nothing less? What if we would stay on our knees until the power of God came back? What if we would again weep for our souls, and the souls of others?

I was working closely with a vicious gang leader who lived in the neighboring village. He was hard, but God had led him to me. For seven long months we met and communicated, I wanted him to catch a glimpse of the power of God; I wanted God to save him. He would often get drunk and threaten to kill me; I would continue to point him to the Savior. He and his gang came over one day to stop a work project, saying that they now owned the land. They brandished their guns and threatened all that were there. I explained to him that God owned the land. He said, “That is fine; tell God to come down here, and I’ll cut off His head.” I was troubled by this remark and asked him if he understood the power of the God he just threatened. One afternoon I drove to his house, and we sat outside and talked. God led me to preach a bold message to him that day. “You need to give up this gang life. God wants to save you, and change your heart!” He seemed very sober as I continued, “You never know when someone will come here and kill you! You can’t control that, but my friend you can control where you go after you are dead!” I then reminded him of the terrible thing he had said days before.

While we were still talking, two men from a neighboring gang approached on motorbikes. They were heavily armed; they had come at that very moment to kill him, but they saw me talking to him and waited for me to leave. “You have a wife and children, are you not tired of this life? God has something so much better for you!” I was pleading, pleading for his soul. It was his very last opportunity, death waited at the door. As I left I told him that I would be back.

After the shooting I rushed back, but it was over… all over.

When we live in the power of the resurrection, the power of the Almighty God, it is then that He works! I feel there is so much work to be done before the Lord returns, but God’s people are too busy, we do not have time.

Do we fear talking about the power of God and the Holy Ghost simply because the Pentecostal movement has twisted what the Bible teaches? God help us.

When we call out to God for salvation, we are doing so because we know we need to be saved; converted. We also know that we cannot save ourselves, so we ask God to help us. Then when God helps us, we are able to do things that we could not do before! Angry people are angry no more. People that could not control their lust now have control. Selfish people begin to put others first. Shy people begin to preach with boldness. Greedy people begin to give to others. God does a work that counselors and doctors cannot do, He changes the very core of a person, and then all things become new. We now live for something far better than what this world has to give; we rise above by the power of God and show this sin-sick world there is a better way!

All through the Bible, God’s people did supernatural things; they did not settle for just a nice life. They sought something bigger, something better. There is power in the blood of Jesus, but it took the cross to make that a possibility. It also takes a cross for us to find that power. And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24. Yes, it seems foolish to those that perish, but to those that believe, it is the Power of God.

אחרי שחייתי בהאיטי כמה חודשים, סוף־סוף ניתנה לי ההזדמנות לבקר את מכשף הכפר המקומי. כשעליתי בשביל הגישה הארוך לביתו, חלפתי על פני פסלים רבים וסמלים שטניים. זה בהחלט היה מצמרר. כשהתקרבתי למקדש הוודו שהיה מחובר לביתו, ראיתי אותו עומד שם ומתבונן בי מתקרב. לבי החל להלום; ידעתי שהוא אדם רב־עוצמה. ואז הוא התחיל לצחוק. ככל שהתקרבתי, צחוקו נעשה רם יותר. הייתי מעט מבולבל עד שהבנתי שאנשים רבים מהכפר הולכים בעקבותיי בשביל. הם התעניינו מאוד במה שעומד להתרחש. ניגשתי אל האיש, בלי לדעת מה יקרה עכשיו.

״אתה כומר?״ הוא שאל.

״כן, אני כומר,״ השבתי. שוב הוא התחיל לצחוק בקול רם.

״אתם הכמרים כולכם אותו דבר,״ הכריז. ״אתם רוצים שכולם יבואו לכנסיות שלכם, אבל אין בכנסיות שלכם שום כוח! כשמישהו משלכם חולה, הוא בא אליי. אין לכם כוח, אתם הנוצרים!״

כובד רב נפל עליי, והסברתי לו שאני מסכים איתו, אבל שלכנסייה האמיתית של ישוע המשיח תמיד יהיה כוח. למעשה, המקרא אומר ששערי שאול לא יגברו עליה.

כך התחילה מערכת יחסים מעניינת מאוד, אבל לעולם לא אשכח את המילים האלה — שבאו בוודאי מהשטן עצמו: ״אין לכם כוח, אתם הנוצרים!״

מאז ביקרתי במאות כנסיות, ועליי להסכים עם כוהן הוודו ההוא. בכנסיות הנוצריות חסר כוח. אבל מדוע? אנחנו יודעים שאלוהים הוא כוח. אנחנו מבינים דברים רבים, אנחנו נראים טוב ונשמעים טוב, אבל האם עדיין יש בכנסיות שלנו את כוחו של אלוהים?

בתנ״ך יש לנו דוגמאות רבות לכוח ולהיעדר כוח. אנו יכולים ללמוד גם כיצד מקבלים כוח, ומדוע מאבדים אותו.

בספר יהושע, פרק ו׳, מופיע הסיפור המוכר על בני ישראל ועל העיר יריחו. אלוהים אומר ליהושע ולכל אנשי המלחמה להקיף את העיר ולצעוד סביבה פעם אחת בכל יום, במשך שישה ימים. ביום השביעי היה עליהם לצעוד סביב העיר לא פעם אחת בלבד, אלא שבע פעמים. אחרי שישלימו את שבע ההקפות סביב העיר, על הכוהנים היה לתקוע בשופרותיהם.

אנו יודעים מה קרה כאשר יהושע ציית לכל ציווי — החומות העבות והבלתי־חדירות התמוטטו. אלוהים גם ציווה את יהושע ציווי קפדני בדבר הדברים שהאנשים היו צריכים לעשות ושאסור היה להם לעשות. היה עליהם להימנע מכל מה שאלוהים הכריז שהוא חרם; כל הכסף, הזהב והכלים היו צריכים להיות מוקדשים לאוצר ה׳; איש לא היה רשאי לקחת מן השלל.

אולם עכן ראה כמה דברים יפים שרצה בהם. הוא החביא אותם בבגדיו, ואחר כך הסתיר אותם מתחת לאוהלו, ואיש לא ראה דבר.

אחרי הניצחון הגדול הזה שלח יהושע מרגלים אל העיר הבאה, העי, כדי לברר עד כמה העיר מבוצרת. האנשים חזרו ואמרו ליהושע שלא ישלח את כל הלוחמים אל העי, מפני שרק מגינים מעטים הגנו על העיר.

אולם אנשי העי הכו את בני ישראל והבריחו אותם. יתרה מזו, יהושע קרע את בגדיו וזעק אל אלוהים. אז השיב לו אלוהים שיש חטא במחנה ישראל.

בתנ״ך בני ישראל מייצגים בדרך כלל את כנסיית ישוע המשיח של ימינו. האם איננו יכולים ללמוד רבות מהסיפור הזה? כשלא היה חטא במחנה (או בכנסייה), זכו אנשי אלוהים לניצחון מוחלט; איש מהם לא אבד. הם עשו דברים נפלאים רבים, השמידו את כל אויביהם מסביבם וחיו בניצחון מלא. אולם ברגע שהחטא נכנס לתוכם, אפילו חטא קטן שעשה אדם אחד, הם איבדו את כוחם. הם כבר לא ניצחו את אויביהם.

בהמשך מובא תיאור מוחשי של האופן שבו בני ישראל טיפלו בחטא שנכנס למחנה. הוא הושמד כליל.

וַיִּקַּח יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל עִמּוֹ אֶת עָכָן בֶּן־זֶרַח, וְאֶת־הַכֶּסֶף, וְאֶת־האַדֶּרֶת, וְאֶת לְשׁוֹן הַזָּהָב, וְאֶת־בָּנָיו וְאֶת־בְּנֹתָיו, וְאֶת־שׁוֹרוֹ וְאֶת־חֲמֹרוֹ וְאֶת־צֹאנוֹ, וְאֶת־אָהֳלוֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; וַיַּעֲלוּ אֹתָם עֵמֶק עָכוֹר… וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל רָגְמוּ אֹתוֹ אֶבֶן, וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ אֹתָם בָּאֵשׁ… – יהושע ז׳:כ״ד–כ״ו.

בסיפור הזה ברור מדוע איבדו אנשי אלוהים את כוחם — היה חטא במחנה. ברור גם מה היה עליהם לעשות כדי להשיב לעצמם את הכוח שאיבדו — לסלק את החטא.

בפרק ח׳ אנו קוראים שכוחם של בני ישראל הושב להם מיד לאחר שהחטא טופל. שוב הם חיו בניצחון!

קטע נוסף בתנ״ך שעוסק בנושא הזה נמצא בויקרא, פרקים י״ג וי״ד. הצרעת הייתה מחלה מוזרה. אם אדם נדבק בצרעת, היא התפשטה בקלות. לכן היה צורך בהנחיות קפדניות כיצד לטפל במחלה. הכוהן היה צריך לבדוק היטב אם האדם הנדון אכן חולה בצרעת או לא. אם הכוהן לא היה בטוח, הוא היה סוגר את האדם בחדר לשבעה ימים ואז בודק אותו שוב. אם נקבע שהאדם חולה בצרעת, היו שולחים אותו אל מחוץ לעיר.

כשפאולוס פונה אל הכנסייה בקורינתוס, הוא מספר להם ששמע שיש חטא בכנסייה. נראה שהוא מופתע מכך שהכנסייה מתייחסת לכך בקלות ראש כזאת: …הַאִם אֵינְכֶם יוֹדְעִים שֶׁמְּעַט שְׂאוֹר מַחְמִיץ אֶת כָּל הָעִסָּה? לָכֵן בַּעֲרוּ אֶת הַשְּׂאוֹר הַיָּשָׁן, לְמַעַן תִּהְיוּ עִסָּה חֲדָשָׁה, הֲרֵי אַתֶּם מַצּוֹת… – הראשונה אל הקורינתים ה׳:ו׳–ז׳. בהמשך הוא אומר לכנסייה: …לָכֵן הוֹצִיאוּ מִקִּרְבְּכֶם אֶת הָאָדָם הָרָע הַזֶּה – הראשונה אל הקורינתים ה׳:י״ג.

נניח ששמעתם שהצרעת שוב נעשתה לבעיה בכפר שלכם. המחלה הזאת, שמשחיתה את הבשר, חזרה והתפרצה, ורבים מבני כפרכם נדבקו בה. ואז, ביום ראשון בבוקר, אתם יושבים בכנסייה, הדלתות נפתחות, ואדם נכנס כשעורו ובשרו תלויים מאיבריו. הוא נגוע קשות, אך נראה שאינו יודע זאת. מה הייתם עושים? מה אם הוא היה רוצה לשבת לידכם? מה אם היה רוצה לדבר עם ילדיכם? אני חושב שכולנו יודעים מה היינו עושים; לא היינו נותנים לו להיות בתוכנו. אנחנו אוהבים את בני עמנו ואת משפחותינו יותר מדי מכדי לעשות זאת.

ומה לגבי החטא? האם אנחנו מאפשרים לחטא לבוא ולהצטרף אלינו? האם אנחנו מתייחסים אליו ברצינות? מה גרוע יותר, להידבק במחלה שמשחיתה את הבשר או להידבק בחטא שמשחית את הנשמה? זכרו, שכר החטא הוא מוות — מוות רוחני; מוות נצחי. אילו היינו מטפלים בחטא כפי שהיינו מטפלים במחלה (וכך עלינו לעשות), היה שוב בכנסיות שלנו כוח רוח הקודש.

המקרא אומר: …תְּקַבְּלוּ גְּבוּרָה בְּבוֹא עֲלֵיכֶם רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְהִתְקַיֵּם בִּי עֵדִים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וּבְכָל יְהוּדָה וְשֹׁמְרוֹן וְעַד קְצֵה הָאָרֶץ – מעשי השליחים א׳:ח׳.

כבר ראינו שהחטא מפריד אותנו מכוחו של אלוהים, וראינו גם שאלוהים רוצה לתת לנו כוח. הוא רוצה שננצח את האויב — את השטן, את העולם ואת הבשר. אולם נדמה שמשהו מתרחש בכנסיות שלנו — אנחנו מאפשרים לחטא להיכנס. מקובל לשמוע מטיף אומר: ״אף אחד אינו מושלם.״ או: ״כולנו חוטאים.״ הלוואי שנבין את הנזק שהאמירות האלה עלולות לגרום. ישוע בא להציל אותנו מכל חטא; מכל עוולה. אם אנחנו נותרים בחטאנו, מה ישוע עשה למעננו?

אני שומע על כנסיות שנסחפות אל תוך העולם. בהדרגה הן מוותרות על עקרונותיהן ומאפשרות לאופנות חדשות ולראוותנות העולם להיכנס. דבר שאינני שומע עליו הרבה הוא כנסיות שמתפרקות בגלל חטאים חמורים, כגון זנות או שכרות. אויב נפשותינו רוצה שנהיה פושרים. הוא רוצה שהכנסייה תאבד את כוחה ותתחיל לחיות כמו כולם. כאן בהאיטי יש כנסיות בכל מקום. בימי ראשון, החל מחמש בבוקר, אני מתחיל לשמוע את הכנסיות שרות ועובדות את אלוהים. אבל איפה כל האנשים האלה ביום שני בבוקר? הם חוזרים ומתערבבים בעולם שממנו באו.

לאחרונה שוחחתי עם איש האיטי עשיר מאוד, שהיה בעל אתרי נופש ונכסים בכל רחבי האיטי. שאלתי אותו אם הוא נוצרי. (רציתי לפתוח בשיחה.) יכולתי לראות שהוא רצה לומר כן; במקום זאת הוא נעשה מתוסכל ואמר שלא. שאלתי אותו מדוע לא. הוא אמר בדיוק את מה שחשבתי שיאמר. ״רציתי להיות נוצרי, הלכתי לכל הכנסיות בסביבה, אבל אני לא מרגיש שיש להן מה להציע לי. יש לי כסף; יש לי ברכות גשמיות; אבל נראה שזה כל מה שהן שואפות אליו.״

אילו הכנסיות שלנו כיום היו מסרבות להסתפק בפחות ממילוי רוח הקודש, בהעצמה שהוא מעניק ובהדרכתו — במידה מלאה של כוח שמימי — היינו יכולים להציע משהו שימשוך את האובדים שסביבנו. אני מאמין שזה בדיוק מה שהעולם מחפש; הם מחפשים משהו טוב יותר, משהו על־טבעי. מה אם לא היינו מסתפקים בפחות מכך? מה אם היינו נשארים על ברכינו עד שכוחו של אלוהים יחזור? מה אם היינו שוב בוכים על נפשותינו ועל נפשות אחרים?

עבדתי בשיתוף פעולה הדוק עם מנהיג כנופיה אכזרי שחי בכפר השכן. הוא היה אדם קשה, אבל אלוהים הוביל אותו אליי. במשך שבעה חודשים ארוכים נפגשנו ושמרנו על קשר. רציתי שיזכה להצצה בכוחו של אלוהים; רציתי שאלוהים יושיע אותו. לעיתים קרובות הוא היה משתכר ומאיים להרוג אותי; ואני המשכתי להפנות אותו אל המושיע. יום אחד הוא ואנשי הכנופיה שלו באו לעצור מיזם בנייה ואמרו שהקרקע שייכת להם כעת. הם הניפו את נשקיהם ואיימו על כל הנוכחים. הסברתי לו שהקרקע שייכת לאלוהים. הוא אמר: ״בסדר; תגיד לאלוהים שירד לכאן, ואני אכרות את ראשו.״ דבריו הטרידו אותי, ושאלתי אותו אם הוא מבין את כוחו של האל שאיים עליו זה עתה. אחר צהריים אחד נסעתי לביתו, וישבנו בחוץ ושוחחנו. באותו יום אלוהים הוביל אותי לשאת לו מסר נועז: ״אתה צריך לנטוש את חיי הכנופיה האלה. אלוהים רוצה להושיע אותך ולשנות את לבך!״ הוא נראה פיכח מאוד כשאמרתי עוד: ״לעולם אינך יודע מתי מישהו יבוא לכאן ויהרוג אותך! את זה אינך יכול לשלוט, אבל ידידי, אתה יכול לשלוט במקום שאליו תלך אחרי מותך!״ ואז הזכרתי לו את הדבר הנורא שאמר כמה ימים קודם לכן.

בעודנו משוחחים, התקרבו שני אנשים מכנופיה שכנה על אופנועים. הם היו חמושים היטב; הם באו באותו רגע ממש להרוג אותו, אבל ראו אותי משוחח איתו והמתינו שאעזוב. ״יש לך אישה וילדים, לא נמאס לך מהחיים האלה? לאלוהים יש משהו הרבה יותר טוב בשבילך!״ התחננתי, התחננתי על נפשו. זו הייתה ההזדמנות האחרונה שלו; המוות עמד בפתח. כשעזבתי אמרתי לו שאחזור.

אחרי הירי מיהרתי לחזור, אבל זה נגמר… נגמר לגמרי.

כשאנחנו חיים בכוח תחיית המתים, בכוחו של האל הכול יכול, אז הוא פועל! אני מרגיש שיש כל כך הרבה עבודה לעשות לפני שובו של האדון, אבל אנשי אלוהים עסוקים מדי; אין לנו זמן.

האם אנחנו חוששים לדבר על כוחו של אלוהים ועל רוח הקודש רק מפני שהתנועה הפנטקוסטלית עיוותה את מה שהמקרא מלמד? אלוהים, עזור לנו.

כשאנחנו זועקים אל אלוהים לישועה, אנחנו עושים זאת מפני שאנחנו יודעים שעלינו להיוושע; לעבור שינוי. אנחנו גם יודעים שאיננו יכולים להושיע את עצמנו, ולכן אנו מבקשים מאלוהים שיעזור לנו. ואז, כשאלוהים עוזר לנו, אנחנו מסוגלים לעשות דברים שלא יכולנו לעשות קודם! אנשים כעסנים אינם כועסים עוד. אנשים שלא הצליחו לשלוט בתאוותיהם מצליחים כעת לשלוט בהן. אנשים אנוכיים מתחילים להקדים אחרים לעצמם. אנשים ביישנים מתחילים להטיף באומץ. אנשים חמדנים מתחילים לתת לאחרים. אלוהים עושה את מה שיועצים ורופאים אינם יכולים לעשות: הוא משנה את האדם ממש מעיקרו, ואז הכול נעשה חדש. כעת אנחנו חיים למען דבר טוב הרבה יותר מכל מה שהעולם הזה יכול לתת; בכוחו של אלוהים אנחנו מתעלים ומראים לעולם החולה בחטא שיש דרך טובה יותר!

לאורך כל המקרא עשו אנשי אלוהים דברים על־טבעיים; הם לא הסתפקו בחיים נעימים ותו לא. הם חיפשו משהו גדול יותר, משהו טוב יותר. יש כוח בדמו של ישוע, אבל הצלב הוא שאפשר זאת. גם אנחנו זקוקים לצלב כדי למצוא את הכוח הזה. וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל כֻּלָּם: ״אִישׁ כִּי יַחְפֹּץ לָבוֹא אַחֲרַי, יִתְכַּחֵשׁ לְעַצְמוֹ וְיִשָּׂא אֶת צְלָבוֹ יוֹם יוֹם וְיֵלֵךְ אַחֲרַי. כִּי הֶחָפֵץ לְהַצִּיל אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ יְאַבְּדֶנָּה, וְהַמְאַבֵּד אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ לְמַעֲנִי הוּא יַצִּילֶנָּה״ – לוקס ט׳:כ״ג–כ״ד. כן, הדבר נראה טיפשי בעיני האובדים, אך למאמינים הוא כוח אלוהים.
