Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.

आप सभी को मसीही प्रेम सहित नमस्कार। एक और साल बीत गया, और आगे का एक और साल हमारे सामने है, जिसमें हमें अपना रास्ता तय करना है। हमारा दृष्टिकोण क्या है? क्या हमारे हृदय में आशा और आनंद उमड़ रहे हैं, या भविष्य हमें निराशा और विनाश से भरा दिखाई देता है? अपने आसपास की परिस्थितियों और हालात में क्या हम परमेश्वर के प्रभुत्वशाली हाथ को कार्य करते देखते हैं, या हमारे दृष्टिकोण से संसार नियंत्रण से बाहर लगता है?

जब मैं देश भर के लोगों से बात करता हूँ, तो लगता है कि बहुत-से लोग एक आम समस्या से जूझ रहे हैं—थकान। आदेशों से थक चुके हैं। बंदिशों से थक चुके हैं। कोविड के मुद्दे को लेकर चारों ओर चल रही बहस और लड़ाई से थक चुके हैं। …से थक चुके हैं।

ऐसा लगता है कि बहुत-से लोग बस “इसके बारे में सोचना नहीं चाहते।” क्यों? सच कहूँ तो मुझे ठीक-ठीक नहीं मालूम कि इसके पीछे सभी कारण क्या हैं, लेकिन मुझे यक़ीन है कि हर व्यक्ति के पास कोई न कोई कारण है। याद रखें कि परमेश्वर चाहता है कि हम …इसलिये साँपों की नाईं चतुर और कबूतरों की नाईं भोले बनो –मत्ती 10:16।

यहाँ संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में, द्वितीय विश्व युद्ध के बाद से, मसीहियों ने सापेक्ष शांति और सुकून के 60 से अधिक वर्ष बिताए हैं। अधिकांशतः हमें अपने परिवारों का पालन-पोषण करने और अपने विवेक के अनुसार अपने पूर्वजों के परमेश्वर की आराधना करने की स्वतंत्रता मिली है। हमने अपने देश की स्थापना के आरंभ में लागू किए गए चर्च और राज्य के पृथक्करण का आनंद लिया है। हम अपने हाथों से काम करके जीविका कमा सके हैं। हममें से बहुतों ने इस देश की प्रचुरता का लाभ उठाया है।

शायद हम एक कृत्रिम बुलबुले में जी रहे थे। शायद हम सुरक्षा के झूठे एहसास में बहला दिए गए हैं। दुनिया भर के देशों में हमारे समकक्षों का क्या हाल है—अपने संसार में सच्चे मसीहियों के रूप में जीना उनकी वास्तविकता कैसी है? निस्संदेह, हम अपनी संपत्ति और आने-जाने की स्वतंत्रता का उपयोग करके उन लोगों के लिए बहुत कुछ भला कर पाए हैं, जिन्होंने मसीह का अनुसरण करने के कारण बहुत कठिनाइयाँ सही हैं। लेकिन इसकी कीमत क्या रही? हमारे बच्चों ने क्या सीखा है?

कभी-कभी हम पहली पीढ़ी के मसीहियों के बारे में सुनते हैं कि वे अपने प्रभु के लिए “जोश से भरे” होते हैं। कभी-कभी तो दूसरी और तीसरी पीढ़ी के मसीहियों को लगता है कि पहली पीढ़ी के मसीही अपने आसपास के लोगों को सुसमाचार सुनाने में शायद कुछ ज़्यादा ही उत्साही हैं।

अगली पीढ़ी का क्या? वे किसी से तो सीख रहे हैं—परमेश्वर, अपने बारे में और जीवन के बारे में। वे क्या सीख रहे हैं? और किससे सीख रहे हैं? हमें इसका जायज़ा लेना चाहिए, ताकि यह सुनिश्चित हो कि हमारे बच्चे जीवन के सबक इस तरह सीखें कि आने वाली बातों की वास्तविकता का सामना करने के लिए तैयार हों।

जब वह जैतून पहाड़ पर बैठा था, तो चेले एकांत में उसके पास आकर कहने लगे, “हमें बता, ये बातें कब होंगी? और तेरे आने और जगत के अन्त का क्या चिन्ह होगा?” यीशु ने उन्हें उत्तर दिया, “सावधान रहो कि कोई तुम्हें न बहकाए। क्योंकि बहुत से मेरे नाम से आकर कहेंगे, ‘मैं मसीह हूँ,’ और बहुतों को बहकाएँगे –मत्ती 24:3-5।

याद रखें कि संसार के अंत के विषय में अपने अनुयायियों से स्वयं यीशु बात कर रहे हैं। उनकी सबसे पहली चिंता यह है कि हम धोखे में न पड़ें। वे कहते हैं कि समय के अंत के आसपास धोखा ही सबसे बड़ा मुद्दा होगा। वे कहते हैं कि बहुत-से लोग मसीह होने का [या उनका प्रत्यक्ष प्रवक्ता होने का] दावा करते हुए आएँगे, ताकि लोग उनकी बात सुनें—यह सब सुनने वालों को धोखा देने और अपने अनुयायी बनाने के प्रयास में होगा।

यदि हमने अब तक ऐसा नहीं किया है, तो अब हमें निश्चय ही अपने बच्चों को वचन और आचरण दोनों से कुछ विशेष बातें सिखानी चाहिए। कि इस जीवन की यात्रा में हमें परदेशी और तीर्थयात्री होना है। कि यदि हम इस संसार के मित्र हैं, तो परमेश्वर हमारा शत्रु होगा। और यह कि यीशु का राज्य इस संसार का नहीं है; इसलिए, उसकी संतानों को पराए देश में राजदूतों की तरह जीना सीखना चाहिए। हमारे बच्चों को यह जानना चाहिए कि जो कोई मसीह यीशु में भक्तिपूर्वक जीवन बिताना चाहेगा, वह सताव सहेंगे ही।

हमारे चर्चों और चर्च-संबद्ध कार्यक्रमों में सिखाए गए कई सिद्धांतों ने कलीसिया की अगली पीढ़ी को बुरी तरह पंगु बना दिया है। हमें सिखाया गया है कि हम “उसके पुनरुत्थान की सामर्थ्य” पा सकते हैं, बिना “उसके दुखों की सहभागिता” में सहभागी हुए। दुख उठाने वाले मसीह और दुख सहने वाले उनके अनुयायियों को हटाकर ऐसे यीशु का अनुसरण करने पर ज़ोर दिया गया है, जो तुम्हारे साथ कुछ भी बुरा नहीं होने देगा। यद्यपि इस बात पर बहुत ज़ोर दिया जाता है कि यीशु ने तुम्हारे लिए दुख उठाया और प्राण दिए, लेकिन “प्रतिदिन अपना क्रूस उठाने” और उसके पीछे चलने की आवश्यकता के बारे में बहुत कम, बल्कि कोई शिक्षा ही नहीं दी जाती।

मानसिक स्वास्थ्य और भावनात्मक स्थिरता

कुछ साल पहले मुझे एक सैनिक की कहानी मिली, जो इराक में अपनी सेवा की अवधि पूरी करने के बाद, अभिघातोत्तर तनाव विकार (PTSD) से जूझ रहा था। निस्संदेह, मेरा विश्वास है कि PTSD वास्तविक है और उससे जूझना भी वास्तविक है; लेकिन जब मैंने इस व्यक्ति की कहानी पढ़ी, तो एक गंभीर संघर्ष कर रहे युवक को दिए जा रहे उत्तरों की कमी से मेरी झुँझलाहट बढ़ती गई। उसके कुछ सबसे गहरे संघर्ष उन घटनाओं की अचानक लौट आने वाली यादों से उपजे थे, जब उसने स्वयं शत्रु पक्ष के कई लोगों को मार डाला था। वह कितने ही परामर्श-सत्रों में गया, फिर भी उसे मन की शांति और विश्राम नहीं मिल पा रहा था। उसका मन व्याकुल था। उसे सोने में कठिनाई होती थी। उसे दूसरों के साथ निभाने में परेशानी होती थी।

मैंने सोचा, “काश कोई इस युवक के साथ खड़ा होकर उसे यीशु मसीह का सुसमाचार सुनाता। काश उसे परमेश्वर के वचन का यह सत्य दिखाया जाता कि किसी दूसरे मनुष्य का जीवन लेना परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में पाप है (भले ही वह शत्रु हो), और जब तक इस बात का समाधान नहीं होता, परमेश्वर उसे अपने हृदय में शांति नहीं पाने देगा। और यह भी कि असली रोमांच की बात यह है कि यदि वह बाइबल की शर्तों के अनुसार परमेश्वर के पास आए और अपने पाप से मन फिराए, तो वह परमेश्वर के साथ चलना शुरू कर सकता है और परमेश्वर उसकी व्याकुल आत्मा को शांति देना शुरू कर सकता है।”

पिछले कई वर्षों में यहाँ संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में कई सामूहिक गोलीबारी की घटनाएँ हुई हैं। हर बार सरकारी अधिकारी समाचार सम्मेलन करते हैं और अपने विचार साझा करते हैं, इस कोशिश में कि एक और ऐसी दुखद घटना का अर्थ समझ सकें, जो मानो समझ से परे हो। आम तौर पर, देर नहीं लगती कि कोई मानसिक स्वास्थ्य और सुरक्षा-जाल, जाँच-पड़ताल तथा ऐसी निरर्थक हिंसा रोकने के लिए बेहतर और अधिक उपचार उपलब्ध कराने के सार्वजनिक प्रयासों को बढ़ाने की आवश्यकता की बात करने लगे।

कुछ हफ्ते पहले, जिस राज्य में मैं रहता हूँ उससे अलग एक राज्य में एक भयानक और दुखद घटना हुई। एक बड़े शहर में, एक व्यक्ति ने एक महिला को प्लेटफ़ॉर्म से धक्का देकर आती हुई सबवे ट्रेन के रास्ते में गिरा दिया। वह बच नहीं पाई। ऐसी भयावह घटना के बाद सरकारी अधिकारियों ने जनता के संभावित भय को कम करने की कोशिश में बयान दिए। उन्होंने निष्कर्ष निकाला कि वह व्यक्ति भावनात्मक रूप से परेशान रहा होगा और वे मानसिक स्वास्थ्य संबंधी समस्याओं वाले लोगों के लिए सुरक्षा-जाल उपलब्ध कराने के प्रयास बढ़ाएँगे, ताकि ऐसी घटनाएँ फिर न हों।

निस्संदेह, जब हम इस मुद्दे को संसार की नज़र से देखते हैं, तो यह बात तर्कसंगत लगती है। लेकिन क्या मामला बस इतना ही है? क्या हम मसीही संसार के तौर-तरीकों के इतने अभ्यस्त हो गए हैं कि भूल गए हैं कि वे परमेश्वर के वचन के सत्य से कितनी दूर भटक गए हैं?

आइए, संसार और चुने हुए सरकारी अधिकारियों पर उँगली न उठाएँ। क्या कलीसिया के रूप में हम उनसे बेहतर हैं? हम अपनी बाइबल को कितना अच्छी तरह जानते हैं? अपने उद्धारकर्ता को कितना अच्छी तरह जानते हैं? जब कोई भीतर शांति और विश्राम खोजते हुए हमारे पास आता है, तो क्या हम जानते हैं कि उसे पवित्रशास्त्र तक कैसे ले जाएँ और यीशु की ओर कैसे मार्गदर्शन करें, जो फिर उसे पिता का मार्ग दिखा सकते हैं?

मैं यह सब क्यों कह रहा हूँ? यदि हम कलीसिया की अगली पीढ़ी को जीवन की समस्याओं के लिए कृत्रिम उत्तर और अस्थायी समाधान देते रहेंगे, तो वे …अन्त तक धीरज धरने… –मत्ती 24:13। के लिए तैयार नहीं होंगे।

फिर उसने सब से कहा, “यदि कोई मेरे पीछे आना चाहे, तो अपने आप से इनकार करे और प्रति दिन अपना क्रूस उठाए हुए मेरे पीछे हो ले। क्योंकि जो कोई अपना प्राण बचाना चाहेगा, वह उसे खोएगा; परन्तु जो कोई मेरे लिये अपना प्राण खोएगा, वही उसे बचाएगा –लूका 9:23-24।

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.

向每一位读者致以基督徒的爱与问候。又一年过去了，新的一年也已在我们面前展开，等待我们走过。我们抱持怎样的眼光？我们的心中是否涌动着盼望与喜乐，还是觉得未来一片阴暗、凶险？从我们的视角来看，我们是否看见上帝主权的手在周遭的处境和环境中运行，还是觉得这个世界已经失控？

我与全国各地的人们交流时，发现许多人似乎都在面对同一个问题——疲惫。厌倦了各种指令。厌倦了封控。厌倦了围绕新冠问题而起的种种争吵和斗争。厌倦了……

看来许多人只是“不想去想这件事”。为什么？我实在不确定原因究竟有哪些，但我确定每个人都有自己的原因。让我们记住，上帝要我们：……所以要灵巧像蛇，驯良像鸽子。——马太福音10:16。

在美利坚合众国，自第二次世界大战以来的六十多年里，基督徒相对享有和平与安宁。在大多数情况下，我们不受干扰，可以按照自己的良心养育家人，敬拜我们列祖的上帝。我们享受着建国之初确立的政教分离。我们能够亲手劳作，维持生计。我们许多人一直享受着这片土地的丰饶。

也许我们一直生活在一个人为的泡沫里。也许我们被哄入了一种虚假的安全感。世界各地与我们处境相似的人，他们作为真正的基督徒，在自己的世界里过着怎样的生活？当然，我们能够利用自己的财富和行动自由，为世界上那些因跟随基督而承受诸多苦难的人做许多好事。但代价是什么？我们的孩子学到了什么？

有时，我们听说第一代基督徒对他们的主“热火般火热”。有时甚至如此，以至于第二代和第三代基督徒认为，第一代基督徒在向身边的人传福音时或许有些过于热心。

下一代又如何呢？他们总会从某些人那里学习有关上帝、自己和人生的事。他们学到什么？又是向谁学习？我们必须认真审视，确保孩子们以一种能使他们预备好面对未来现实的方式学习人生功课。

耶稣在橄榄山上坐着，门徒暗暗地来，说：“请告诉我们，什么时候会有这些事？你降临和世界末了有什么预兆呢？”耶稣回答说：“你们要谨慎，免得有人迷惑你们。因为将来有好些人冒我的名来，说：‘我是基督’，并且要迷惑许多人。”——马太福音24:3-5。

要记住，这是耶稣亲自对跟随祂的人谈到世界的末了。祂最先关心的，就是我们不要受迷惑。祂说，迷惑将是末世围绕着我们的主要问题。祂说，许多人会来，声称自己是基督【或是祂直接的发言人】，借此博取听众的注意，一心要迷惑听见的人并招揽跟随者。

即使从前没有这样做过，现在我们也确实必须通过言语和行动教导孩子一些具体的事：我们在人生旅途中应当作客旅和寄居者；如果我们是这世界的朋友，上帝就会成为我们的仇敌；耶稣的国不属于这世界，因此祂的儿女必须学会像身在异乡的使者那样生活。我们的孩子需要知道，凡在基督耶稣里敬虔度日的人，都必定遭受逼迫。

我们教会以及教会附属事工中所教导的许多教义，严重削弱了教会的下一代。我们被教导说，不必有分于“祂所受的苦”，也可以得着“祂复活的大能”。一位受苦的基督和受苦的跟随者已被抛弃，取而代之的是跟随一位绝不会让坏事临到你的耶稣。虽然人们大力强调耶稣为你受苦并死去，却几乎没有——甚至完全没有——教导我们需要“天天背起自己的十字架”来跟从祂。

心理健康与情绪稳定

几年前，我读到一个士兵的故事。他在伊拉克服役一段时间后，正努力应对创伤后应激障碍。当然，我相信创伤后应激障碍是真实的，那些挣扎也是真实的；但读着这个人的故事，我发现自己对一个深陷困境的年轻人得不到什么解答，越来越感到沮丧。他最深的挣扎，有些源于那些闪回记忆：他曾亲手杀死了几名敌人。不管参加多少次辅导，他就是无法获得内心的平安与安歇。他心神不宁，难以入睡，也难以与他人相处。

我不禁想：“要是有人能来到这位年轻人身边，把耶稣基督的福音分享给他就好了。要是有人能向他显明上帝话语的真理，告诉他在上帝眼中，夺取另一个人的性命就是罪（即使那人是敌人）；在这件事得到处理之前，上帝不会让他心中有平安，那该多好。还有，真正令人振奋的是：如果他愿意按照圣经的要求归向上帝，并为自己的罪悔改，他就可以开始与上帝同行，而上帝也能开始赐平安给他那受困扰的灵魂。”

过去这些年，美国发生了许多起大规模枪击事件。每次，政府官员都会召开新闻发布会，分享他们的看法，试图理解又一起看似无法解释的悲剧。通常不久就会有人谈论心理健康，以及有必要加大公共层面的努力，提供安全网、筛查和更多、更好的治疗，以遏止这种毫无意义的暴力。

几周前，我居住的州以外的另一个州发生了一起可怕的悲剧。在一座大城市里，一名男子把一名女子从站台推下，推到了迎面驶来的地铁列车前。她没能活下来。如此骇人的事件发生后，政府官员向公众发表声明，试图平息民众可能产生的恐惧。他们认定那名男子必定情绪有问题，并表示将加大力度，为有心理健康问题的人提供安全网，以免类似事件再次发生。

当然，从世俗的眼光看这个问题，似乎说得通。但事情仅仅如此吗？我们基督徒是否已经如此习惯世俗的做法，以致忘记了他们偏离上帝话语的真理有多远？

让我们不要指责世人和民选官员。我们作为教会，真的更好吗？我们对圣经了解多少？我们对救主了解多少？有人来到我们面前寻求内心的平安与安歇时，我们知道如何带他们查考圣经，并引领他们到耶稣那里，让祂向他们指明通往父上帝的道路吗？

我为什么要说这些？如果我们继续用人为的答案和暂时的办法来应对人生的问题，供教会的下一代依靠，他们就无法预备好……忍耐到底……——马太福音24:13。

耶稣又对众人说：“若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，天天背起自己的十字架来跟从我。因为凡想救自己生命的，必丧掉生命；凡为我丧掉生命的，必救了生命。”——路加福音9:23-24。

After living in Haiti for several months, I finally had the opportunity to go visit the local witch doctor. As I walked up his long drive, I passed many statues and satanic symbols. It was eerie for sure. As I approached the voodoo temple that was connected to his house, I saw him standing there watching me approach. My heart began to race; I knew he was a powerful man. Then he began to laugh. The closer I got, the louder he laughed. I was a bit puzzled until I realized that many people from the village were following me up the lane. They were very interested in what was about to transpire. I approached the man, not knowing what would happen next.

“Are you a pastor?” he asked.

“Yes, I am,” was my reply. Again, he began to laugh loudly.

“You pastors are all the same,” he proclaimed. “You want everyone to come to your churches, but your churches have no power! When one of your people gets sick, they come to me. No power, you Christians!”

A heavy burden overtook me, and I explained to him how I agreed with him, but that the real church of Jesus Christ would always have power. The Bible actually says that the very gates of Hell shall not prevail against it.

This was the beginning of a very interesting relationship, but I will never forget those words—most certainly from the devil himself—“You Christians have no power!”

I have since traveled to hundreds of churches and need to agree with that voodoo priest. The Christian churches are lacking power. But why? We know that God is power. We have many things figured out, we look good and sound good, but do we still have the power of God in our churches?

In the Old Testament we have many examples of power and the lack of power. We can also learn how we receive power, and why we lose it.

In Joshua, chapter 6, we have the familiar account of the children of Israel and the city of Jericho. God tells Joshua and all the men of war to compass the city, and walk around it once every day, for six days. Then on the seventh day they were to march around the city not just once, but seven times. After they had completed the seven trips around the city, the priests were to blow their trumpets.

We know what happened when Joshua obeyed each command—those thick, impenetrable walls came tumbling down. God also gave Joshua a strict command about what the men should and should not do. They were to keep themselves from everything that God had pronounced was accursed; all the silver, gold, and vessels were to be consecrated into the treasury of the Lord; no man was to take any of the spoil.

However, Achan saw some nice things that he desired. He slipped them into his armor, then later hid them under his tent, and no one saw a thing.

After this great victory, Joshua sent spies to the next city, Ai, to discover how well the city was fortified. The men returned and told Joshua not to send all the men to Ai, for there were only a few defenders protecting the city.

However, the men of Ai smote the children of Israel and chased them away. Moreover, Joshua rent his clothes and cried out to God. Then God replied that there was sin in the camp of Israel.

In the Old Testament, the children of Israel are normally representative of the church of Jesus Christ today. Can we not glean much from this account? When there was no sin in the camp (or in the church) God’s people had complete victory; they lost not one. They did many wonderful things, they destroyed all their enemies around them, and they lived in COMPLETE victory. However, as soon as sin entered into their midst, even a small sin done by one man, they lost their power. They no longer had victory over their enemies.

What follows is a graphic description of how the children of Israel dealt with the sin that had entered the camp. It was totally destroyed.

And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor … And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire… –Joshua 7:24-26.

In this account it is clear why God’s people had lost their power—they had sin in the camp. It is also clear what it took for them to regain that power which they had lost—get rid of the sin.

In chapter 8 we read of the power being restored to Israel instantly after the sin was dealt with. Again, they lived in victory!

Another passage in the Old Testament that speaks of this topic is in Leviticus chapters 13 and 14. Leprosy was a strange disease. If one were to get leprosy, it was easily spread. Thus, there needed to be some strict guidelines regarding how to deal with the disease. The priest was to examine very closely to see if the person in question indeed had leprosy or not. If the priest was unsure, he would shut the person up in a room for seven days then examine him again. If it was determined that the person had leprosy, then they were sent outside of the city.

As Paul addresses the church in Corinth, he tells them that he has heard there is sin in the church. He seems surprised that the church is taking it so casually, …Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump? Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened… –1 Corinthians 5:6-7. Later he tells the church …Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person –1 Corinthians 5:13.

Let’s say that you heard the news that leprosy was again a problem in your village. This flesh-destroying disease had made a comeback and many from your village were now infected. Then you’re sitting in church on Sunday morning, when the doors open, and a man enters with skin and flesh hanging from his extremities. He is badly infected, but he does not seem to know it. What would you do? What if he wanted to come sit by you? What if he wanted to talk to your children? I think we all know what we would do; we would not allow him into our midst. We love our people, our families too much for that.

What about sin? Do we allow sin to come and join us? Do we take it seriously? What is worse, being infected with a flesh-destroying disease, or being infected by a soul-destroying sin? Remember, the wages of sin is death—spiritual death; eternal death. If we would treat sin in the same way as we would the disease (and we should) then our churches would once again have Holy Spirit power.

The Bible says …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

We have already seen how sin separates us from the power of God, and we have also seen how God wants to give us power. He wants us to have victory over the enemy—the devil, the world, and flesh. However, something seems to be happening in our churches—we are allowing sin to enter. It is common to hear a preacher say, “No one is perfect.” Or, “We all sin.” Oh, that we would realize the damage these statements can make. Jesus came to save us from ALL sin; ALL unrighteousness. If we are left to continue in our sin, what has Jesus done for us?

I hear about churches drifting into the world. They gradually let go of convictions and allow some new fashion and pomp of the world to enter. Something that I hear little of is churches falling apart because of gross sin, such as fornication or drunkenness. The enemy of our souls, desires for us to become lukewarm. He wants the church to lose its power, to start living like everyone else. Here in Haiti, there are churches everywhere. On Sunday mornings starting at five o’clock in the morning, I start hearing the churches singing and worshipping. However, where are all those people on Monday morning? They are mixing right back into the world from whence they have come.

I was recently talking to a very wealthy Haitian man who owned resorts and properties all over Haiti. I asked him if he was a Christian. (I wanted to start a conversation.) I could tell that he wanted to say yes; instead, he became frustrated and said no. I asked him why not. He said exactly what I thought he would say. “I have desired to become a Christian, I’ve gone to all the churches around here, but I don’t feel they have anything to offer me. I have money; I have physical blessings; but that seems to be all that they are seeking for.”

If our churches today would refuse to settle for anything less than the infilling, empowering, and leading of the Holy Spirit, a full dose of heavenly power, then we would be able to offer something that would appeal to the lost around us. I believe this is exactly what the world is looking for; they are seeking for something better, something supernatural. What if we would settle for nothing less? What if we would stay on our knees until the power of God came back? What if we would again weep for our souls, and the souls of others?

I was working closely with a vicious gang leader who lived in the neighboring village. He was hard, but God had led him to me. For seven long months we met and communicated, I wanted him to catch a glimpse of the power of God; I wanted God to save him. He would often get drunk and threaten to kill me; I would continue to point him to the Savior. He and his gang came over one day to stop a work project, saying that they now owned the land. They brandished their guns and threatened all that were there. I explained to him that God owned the land. He said, “That is fine; tell God to come down here, and I’ll cut off His head.” I was troubled by this remark and asked him if he understood the power of the God he just threatened. One afternoon I drove to his house, and we sat outside and talked. God led me to preach a bold message to him that day. “You need to give up this gang life. God wants to save you, and change your heart!” He seemed very sober as I continued, “You never know when someone will come here and kill you! You can’t control that, but my friend you can control where you go after you are dead!” I then reminded him of the terrible thing he had said days before.

While we were still talking, two men from a neighboring gang approached on motorbikes. They were heavily armed; they had come at that very moment to kill him, but they saw me talking to him and waited for me to leave. “You have a wife and children, are you not tired of this life? God has something so much better for you!” I was pleading, pleading for his soul. It was his very last opportunity, death waited at the door. As I left I told him that I would be back.

After the shooting I rushed back, but it was over… all over.

When we live in the power of the resurrection, the power of the Almighty God, it is then that He works! I feel there is so much work to be done before the Lord returns, but God’s people are too busy, we do not have time.

Do we fear talking about the power of God and the Holy Ghost simply because the Pentecostal movement has twisted what the Bible teaches? God help us.

When we call out to God for salvation, we are doing so because we know we need to be saved; converted. We also know that we cannot save ourselves, so we ask God to help us. Then when God helps us, we are able to do things that we could not do before! Angry people are angry no more. People that could not control their lust now have control. Selfish people begin to put others first. Shy people begin to preach with boldness. Greedy people begin to give to others. God does a work that counselors and doctors cannot do, He changes the very core of a person, and then all things become new. We now live for something far better than what this world has to give; we rise above by the power of God and show this sin-sick world there is a better way!

All through the Bible, God’s people did supernatural things; they did not settle for just a nice life. They sought something bigger, something better. There is power in the blood of Jesus, but it took the cross to make that a possibility. It also takes a cross for us to find that power. And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24. Yes, it seems foolish to those that perish, but to those that believe, it is the Power of God.

Efter att ha bott i Haiti i flera månader fick jag till slut möjlighet att besöka den lokale häxdoktorn. När jag gick uppför hans långa infart passerade jag många statyer och sataniska symboler. Det var onekligen kusligt. När jag närmade mig voodootemplet som låg i anslutning till hans hus såg jag honom stå där och betrakta mig när jag kom. Mitt hjärta började slå snabbare; jag visste att han var en mäktig man. Sedan började han skratta. Ju närmare jag kom, desto högre skrattade han. Jag var lite förbryllad tills jag insåg att många från byn följde efter mig längs vägen. De var mycket nyfikna på vad som skulle hända. Jag gick fram till mannen utan att veta vad som skulle ske härnäst.

”Är du pastor?” frågade han.

”Ja, det är jag”, svarade jag. Återigen började han skratta högt.

”Ni pastorer är alla likadana”, förklarade han. ”Ni vill att alla ska komma till era kyrkor, men era kyrkor har ingen kraft! När någon av era församlingsmedlemmar blir sjuk kommer de till mig. Ingen kraft, ni kristna!”

En tung börda föll över mig, och jag förklarade för honom att jag höll med honom, men att Jesu Kristi sanna kyrka alltid skulle ha kraft. Bibeln säger faktiskt att själva helvetets portar inte ska få makt över den.

Detta blev början på en mycket intressant relation, men jag kommer aldrig att glömma de orden – helt säkert från djävulen själv: ”Ni kristna har ingen kraft!”

Sedan dess har jag besökt hundratals kyrkor, och jag måste hålla med den där voodooprästen. De kristna kyrkorna saknar kraft. Men varför? Vi vet att Gud är kraft. Vi har mycket på plats, vi ser bra ut och låter bra, men har vi fortfarande Guds kraft i våra kyrkor?

I Gamla testamentet finns många exempel på kraft och på avsaknad av kraft. Vi kan också lära oss hur vi får kraft och varför vi förlorar den.

I Josua, kapitel 6, finns den välbekanta berättelsen om Israels barn och staden Jeriko. Gud säger åt Josua och alla krigsmännen att tåga runt staden och gå ett varv runt den varje dag i sex dagar. På den sjunde dagen skulle de sedan tåga runt staden inte bara en gång, utan sju gånger. När de hade gått de sju varven runt staden skulle prästerna blåsa i sina trumpeter.

Vi vet vad som hände när Josua lydde varje befallning – de tjocka, ointagliga murarna rasade samman. Gud gav också Josua en sträng befallning om vad männen skulle och inte skulle göra. De skulle hålla sig borta från allt som Gud hade förklarat vara bannlyst; allt silver, guld och alla kärl skulle avskiljas till Herrens skattkammare; ingen fick ta något av bytet.

Men Akan såg några fina saker som han ville ha. Han smög ner dem i sin rustning och gömde dem sedan under sitt tält, och ingen såg någonting.

Efter denna stora seger skickade Josua spejare till nästa stad, Ai, för att ta reda på hur väl staden var befäst. Männen kom tillbaka och sa till Josua att inte skicka alla männen till Ai, eftersom det bara fanns några få försvarare som skyddade staden.

Men männen från Ai slog Israels barn och jagade bort dem. Josua rev dessutom sönder sina kläder och ropade till Gud. Då svarade Gud att det fanns synd i Israels läger.

I Gamla testamentet är Israels barn vanligtvis en förebild för Jesu Kristi kyrka i dag. Kan vi inte lära oss mycket av den här berättelsen? När det inte fanns någon synd i lägret (eller i kyrkan) hade Guds folk fullständig seger; de förlorade inte en enda man. De gjorde många underbara ting, besegrade alla sina fiender runt omkring sig och levde i FULLSTÄNDIG seger. Men så snart synd kom in ibland dem, även en liten synd som begicks av en enda man, förlorade de sin kraft. De hade inte längre seger över sina fiender.

Det som följer är en grafisk beskrivning av hur Israels barn hanterade synden som hade kommit in i lägret. Den utplånades fullständigt.

Och Josua och hela Israel med honom tog Akan, Seras son, och silvret, manteln och guldtackan, hans söner och döttrar, hans oxar, åsnor och får, hans tält och allt han ägde, och de förde dem till Akors dal … Och hela Israel stenade honom, och de brände dem i eld … – Josua 7:24–26.

I den här berättelsen framgår det tydligt varför Guds folk hade förlorat sin kraft – det fanns synd i lägret. Det framgår också tydligt vad som krävdes för att återfå den kraft de hade förlorat – att göra sig av med synden.

I kapitel 8 läser vi att kraften genast återställdes åt Israel efter att synden hade hanterats. Återigen levde de i seger!

Ett annat ställe i Gamla testamentet som behandlar detta ämne finns i Tredje Moseboken, kapitel 13 och 14. Spetälska var en märklig sjukdom. Om någon drabbades av spetälska spreds den lätt. Därför behövdes strikta riktlinjer för hur sjukdomen skulle hanteras. Prästen skulle undersöka personen mycket noggrant för att se om han verkligen hade spetälska eller inte. Om prästen var osäker skulle han stänga in personen i ett rum i sju dagar och sedan undersöka honom igen. Om det fastställdes att personen hade spetälska skickades han utanför staden.

När Paulus vänder sig till församlingen i Korinth berättar han att han har hört att det finns synd i församlingen. Han verkar förvånad över att församlingen tar det så lättvindigt: …Vet ni inte att lite surdeg syrar hela degen? Rensa därför bort den gamla surdegen, så att ni blir en ny deg, eftersom ni är osyrade … – Första Korinthierbrevet 5:6–7. Senare säger han till församlingen: …Driv därför bort den onde från er … – Första Korinthierbrevet 5:13.

Anta att du fick höra att spetälska återigen var ett problem i din by. Denna sjukdom, som förstör kroppens vävnad, hade kommit tillbaka och många i din by var nu smittade. Sedan sitter du i kyrkan en söndagsmorgon när dörrarna öppnas och en man kommer in, med hud och kött hängande från sina lemmar. Han är svårt smittad, men verkar inte veta om det. Vad skulle du göra? Tänk om han ville sätta sig bredvid dig? Tänk om han ville prata med dina barn? Jag tror att vi alla vet vad vi skulle göra; vi skulle inte låta honom komma in bland oss. Vi älskar våra människor och våra familjer alltför mycket för det.

Hur är det med synden? Låter vi synden komma och slå följe med oss? Tar vi den på allvar? Vad är värre, att smittas av en sjukdom som förstör kroppen eller av en synd som förstör själen? Kom ihåg att syndens lön är döden – andlig död; evig död. Om vi behandlade synden på samma sätt som vi skulle behandla sjukdomen (och det borde vi), skulle våra kyrkor återigen ha den helige Andes kraft.

Bibeln säger: …ni ska få kraft när den helige Ande kommer över er, och ni ska bli mina vittnen i Jerusalem och i hela Judeen och Samarien och ända till jordens yttersta gräns – Apostlagärningarna 1:8.

Vi har redan sett hur synden skiljer oss från Guds kraft, och vi har också sett hur Gud vill ge oss kraft. Han vill att vi ska segra över fienden – djävulen, världen och köttet. Men något verkar hända i våra kyrkor – vi låter synden komma in. Det är vanligt att höra en predikant säga: ”Ingen är fullkomlig.” Eller: ”Vi syndar alla.” Tänk om vi ändå kunde inse vilken skada dessa uttalanden kan göra. Jesus kom för att rädda oss från ALL synd; ALL orättfärdighet. Om vi lämnas att fortsätta i vår synd, vad har då Jesus gjort för oss?

Jag hör talas om kyrkor som glider in i världen. De släpper gradvis sina övertygelser och låter något nytt mode och världens pompa och ståt komma in. Något jag sällan hör talas om är kyrkor som faller samman på grund av grov synd, såsom otukt eller fylleri. Vår själs fiende vill att vi ska bli ljumma. Han vill att kyrkan ska förlora sin kraft och börja leva som alla andra. Här i Haiti finns kyrkor överallt. På söndagsmorgnarna, med början klockan fem, börjar jag höra kyrkorna sjunga och tillbe. Men var är alla dessa människor måndag morgon? De blandar sig åter med den värld de kommit ifrån.

Jag talade nyligen med en mycket rik haitisk man som ägde semesteranläggningar och fastigheter över hela Haiti. Jag frågade honom om han var kristen. (Jag ville inleda ett samtal.) Jag kunde se att han ville svara ja; i stället blev han frustrerad och sa nej. Jag frågade honom varför inte. Han sa precis det jag trodde att han skulle säga. ”Jag har velat bli kristen, jag har gått till alla kyrkor här omkring, men jag tycker inte att de har något att erbjuda mig. Jag har pengar; jag har materiella välsignelser; men det verkar vara allt de strävar efter.”

Om våra kyrkor i dag vägrade nöja sig med något mindre än den helige Andes uppfyllande, kraftgivande och ledning – en full dos himmelsk kraft – då skulle vi kunna erbjuda något som tilltalar de förlorade omkring oss. Jag tror att det är precis detta världen söker; de letar efter något bättre, något övernaturligt. Tänk om vi inte nöjde oss med något mindre? Tänk om vi stannade på knä tills Guds kraft kom tillbaka? Tänk om vi återigen grät över våra egna själar och andras själar?

Jag arbetade nära en våldsam gängledare som bodde i grannbyn. Han var hård, men Gud hade lett honom till mig. Under sju långa månader träffades vi och hade kontakt. Jag ville att han skulle få en glimt av Guds kraft; jag ville att Gud skulle frälsa honom. Han blev ofta berusad och hotade att döda mig; jag fortsatte att visa honom på Frälsaren. En dag kom han och hans gäng dit för att stoppa ett arbetsprojekt och sa att marken nu tillhörde dem. De viftade med sina vapen och hotade alla som var där. Jag förklarade för honom att marken tillhörde Gud. Han sa: ”Det går bra; be Gud komma ner hit, så ska jag skära av honom huvudet.” Den här kommentaren bekymrade mig, och jag frågade honom om han förstod vilken kraft Gud hade, den Gud han just hade hotat. En eftermiddag körde jag hem till honom, och vi satt utomhus och pratade. Gud ledde mig den dagen till att predika ett djärvt budskap för honom. ”Du måste lämna det här gänglivet. Gud vill frälsa dig och förändra ditt hjärta!” Han verkade mycket nykter när jag fortsatte: ”Man vet aldrig när någon kommer hit och dödar dig! Det kan du inte styra över, men min vän, du kan styra över vart du kommer efter att du har dött!” Sedan påminde jag honom om det fruktansvärda han hade sagt några dagar tidigare.

Medan vi fortfarande pratade kom två män från ett gäng i grannskapet fram på motorcyklar. De var tungt beväpnade; de hade kommit just då för att döda honom, men när de såg mig prata med honom väntade de tills jag hade gått. ”Du har en hustru och barn, är du inte trött på det här livet? Gud har något så mycket bättre för dig!” Jag vädjade, vädjade för hans själ. Det var hans allra sista möjlighet; döden väntade vid dörren. När jag gick sa jag att jag skulle komma tillbaka.

Efter skottlossningen skyndade jag tillbaka, men det var över … helt över.

När vi lever i uppståndelsens kraft, den allsmäktige Gudens kraft, är det då han verkar! Jag känner att så mycket arbete återstår att göra innan Herren återvänder, men Guds folk är alltför upptagna; vi har inte tid.

Är vi rädda för att tala om Guds kraft och den helige Ande, bara för att pingströrelsen har förvrängt det Bibeln lär? Gud hjälpe oss.

När vi ropar till Gud om frälsning gör vi det därför att vi vet att vi behöver bli frälsta; omvända. Vi vet också att vi inte kan frälsa oss själva, så vi ber Gud om hjälp. När Gud sedan hjälper oss kan vi göra sådant som vi inte kunde göra tidigare! Arga människor är inte längre arga. Människor som inte kunde behärska sin lust får nu kontroll över den. Själviska människor börjar sätta andra först. Blyga människor börjar predika frimodigt. Giriga människor börjar ge åt andra. Gud utför ett verk som rådgivare och läkare inte kan utföra; han förändrar själva kärnan i en människa, och då blir allting nytt. Nu lever vi för något mycket bättre än det den här världen har att erbjuda; genom Guds kraft höjer vi oss över den och visar denna syndasjuka värld att det finns en bättre väg!

Genom hela Bibeln gjorde Guds folk övernaturliga ting; de nöjde sig inte med ett trevligt liv. De sökte något större, något bättre. Det finns kraft i Jesu blod, men det var korset som gjorde det möjligt. Det krävs också ett kors för att vi ska finna den kraften. Och han sade till alla: Om någon vill följa mig, ska han förneka sig själv och varje dag ta sitt kors och följa mig. Ty den som vill rädda sitt liv ska mista det, men den som mister sitt liv för min skull ska rädda det – Lukasevangeliet 9:23–24. Ja, det verkar dåraktigt för dem som går förlorade, men för dem som tror är det Guds kraft.

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

Du har din ungdoms dugg. Salme 110:3

Det er mange sider ved ungdommen som ikke er dydige. Mange unge i vår tid opplever en tidlig periode preget av ufølsom likegyldighet og uhell. Ofte legger avgjørelser som tas i ungdomsårene grunnlaget for resten av livet. Det var den yngre sønnen, den bortkomne, som ba om å få utbetalt arven sin på forskudd, og deretter sløste den bort i et utsvevende liv. Det var den unge Dina som gikk bort fra farens hus og …gikk ut for å se døtrene i landet –1. Mosebok 34:1. Der ble hun utsatt for landets hedenske unge menn og utløste en blodig massakre, slik at Jakob ble en stank i landet. Mange tåpelige unge har sådd i vinden og høstet ødeleggelsene som fulgte. De som mangler solide prinsipper og foreldrenes autoritet, løper stor risiko for å lide åndelig skipbrudd.

Det finnes bestemte lyster som rammer unge mer enn eldre, og de unge blir formant til å flykte fra dem. (–se 2. Timoteus 2:22) Salomo så ut gjennom vinduet sitt: Blant de uerfarne så jeg, blant de unge la jeg merke til en ung mann uten forstand –Ordspråkene 7:6-7. Den unge mannen søkte inderlig etter det som syntes vakkert … [In]ntil en pil [gjennomboret] leveren hans; som en fugl som haster mot snaren uten å vite at det gjelder livet –Ordspråkene 7:23. Vi kunne undersøke lastene i Rehabeams, Amnons, Nadabs og Abihus ungdomsliv, og hos utallige andre. Vi finner heller ingen mangel på moderne, dårskapsfylte eksempler rundt oss, levd ut av lettsindige unge.

Men unge skal ikke foraktes. La ingen forakte deg fordi du er ung, men vær et forbilde for de troende i ord, i ferd, i kjærlighet, i ånd, i tro, i renhet –1. Timoteus 4:12. Faktisk velger Gud som regel de unge som redskaper for å utbre sitt budskap. Josef, med sin plettfrie karakter, ble sendt av Gud til Egypt da han var 17 år, for å berge liv (–se 1. Mosebok 45:5). Mirjam, som var tolv år, holdt vakt over den framtidige befrieren av hele det jødiske folket og sørget for at sin egen mor, Jokebed, fikk være den lille Moses’ amme. David ble som ung sendt for å oppmuntre brødrene sine i hæren. Brødrene foraktet ham: …Jeg kjenner din overmot og ditt hjertes ondskap … –1. Samuelsbok 17:28. Saul avviste ham: …Du kan ikke gå mot denne filisteren og kjempe med ham, for du er bare en ung gutt … –1. Samuelsbok 17:33. Goliat hånte ham: …Er jeg en hund, siden du kommer mot meg med stokker … –1. Samuelsbok 17:43. Men forakten deres var forgjeves da Gud valgte ham til konge over hele Israel.

Disse edle ungdommelige ambisjonene ble videreført av Josjia, Jesaja, Jeremia, Daniel, Maria og Herrens disipler, som alle valgte å minnes sin Skaper i ungdommens dager. Men disse var ikke naive eksempler som prøvde å sikre seg sin plass i livet; de var levende eksempler på unge som søkte å etterligne sin Herres bilde.

Vi behøver ikke granske Kristi karakter lenge før vi finner …

...Du har din ungdoms dugg

Salme 110 er kanskje det skriftstedet det oftest henvises til i Det gamle testamentet. Dette retoriske portrettet av Messias åpenbarer en levende dyd som vi kan betrakte. Kristus, som den eldgamle, ble beskrevet i Åpenbaringen med hodet og håret … hvitt som ull, så hvitt som snø … –Åpenbaringen 1:14, men her framstilles han som evig ung, mens han sitter ved Guds høyre hånd (–se Salme 110:1). Alderdommens tretthet kan ikke komme dit, for Kristus er Morgenstjernen. Det er evig morgen rundt Guds trone. De hellige som følger nøye etter i hans bilde, vil også gjenspeile denne dyden, for Jesu lys er ungdommens lys.

Salmedikteren beskriver Messias ved å hente fram morgenens naturlige skjønnhet, duggen (–se Salme 110:3). Tanken på dugg fører blikket vårt ned fra himmelen og avdekker et portrett av jorden vi bor på. I himmelen finnes det ingen natt, ingen veksling mellom varme og kulde, og ikke behov for solen til å lyse opp dagen – og dermed heller ingen dugg. Duggen hører til det jordiske, der alle som bare vil bøye seg ned og se, kan betrakte en ensartet tropp av gress som funkler som om det var besatt med utallige diamanter. Etter en lang, mørk natt står duggdråpene i blomstene som tårer i øynene deres, mens de gråter av glede over den første morgenstrålens ankomst. De som går gjennom den lave vegetasjonen, får føttene sine vasket av tusen kjærtegnende hender, slik Gud har utformet det. Kristus framstilles ikke som morgenens dugg, men som ungdommens dugg, og bildet utvides videre.

Ungdommen er en tid med overstrømmende energi. Noen klarer ikke å sitte stille. De er vanligvis sosiale skapninger som elsker å være sammen med andre. Dette er verken en dyd eller en last. Det er ganske enkelt naturlig. Med årene kommer det en gradvis påkjenning som temmer og tøyler sjelen. Etter hvert som livet går sin gang, får vi et klarere syn og mer stødig tankegang, og vi stiger mot bedre ting. Men når midtlivets topp er passert og føttene går nedover bakken, blir den stormende strømmen av kroppslig energi som tidligere brøytet seg gjennom alt, bevart i minnene om fortiden. For mange er dette den nærmeste trøsten de finner for de svunne dagene da de var sterke.

Men Kristus har ikke kalt oss til å dyrke en forkjærlighet for fortiden eller lengte vemodig etter ungdommens «fres» («DO»). Så mange i dag beklager trist at drivkraften deres har tatt bena på nakken. De har ikke blikk for høyere ting og får mer energi av en boks Mountain Dew enn av ungdommens dugg. De blir mer inspirert av en tur ned minnenes allé og av å mimre om fortidens hendelser enn av håpet som ligger foran dem.

Alder er ingen hindring for å få del i ungdommens dugg. Den gamle av dager rir fremdeles blant de gylne lysestakene. Johannes så håret hans … hvitt som ull, så hvitt som snø … –Åpenbaringen 1:14, men Salomo sier likevel: …hans lokker er buskete og svarte som ravnen –Høysangen 5:11. Alderen kan ta fra oss styrke og hørsel, men …Herrens hånd er ikke for kort til å frelse, og hans øre er ikke for tungt til å høre –Jesaja 59:1. Han har sikret ungdommens dugg og innbyr oss til å ta del i den. Problemet ligger ikke i kroppen vår som forfaller, men i et sinn som åndelig sett går tilbake. Alderdommens plage setter i hovedsak inn når sinnet følger kroppen.

Det er ikke slik at livet blir fattigere etter hvert som det går framover, eller slutter å være edelt når ungdommens sjarm har falmet. Hvis vi bare var satt her for å oppleve glede, ville ungdomsforelskelsens ebbe ut være forferdelig. Gud hadde et langt større mål for barna sine enn at de bare skulle være livlige «gjørere». Vi er sendt hit for å lære. Årene vi har fått tildelt på jorden, skal alle være en skolegang, og det er ikke i ungdommens strålende romantikk vi lærer de beste og mest varige leksjonene. Vi lærer dem ved standhaftig å gjøre vår plikt, ved stille å godta våre begrensninger, ved tålmodig å bære vår daglige byrde og ved å rekke en hjelpende hånd til vår bror. Dette gir oss de virkelige mulighetene til kristen dannelse og er røttene til etisk edelhet. Kristus arbeidet …ikke for den mat som forgår, men for den mat som varer til evig liv … –Johannes 6:27, og han fullførte sin jordiske oppgave på 33 år. Men ungdommens dugg forsvant ikke da han satte seg ved sin Fars høyre hånd.

Derfor konkluderer vi med at denne ungdommeligheten ikke sikres ved styrke, men ved …

...Håp

Men denne mannen har båret fram ett offer for synder for alltid, og satte seg ved Guds høyre hånd. Fra nå av venter han på at fiendene skal legges som skammel for føttene hans. –Hebreerne 10:12-13.

Hvordan skal vi se for oss Kristus nå? Ligger han i en godstol, helt utslitt etter sin erfaring med denne jordens gjenstridige mennesker? Holder han på å lage en utklippsbok med dyrebare minner? Altfor ofte er dette de eldres situasjon, og slik dør sinnet deres sammen med kroppen.

Og ikke bare det, men vi roser oss også av trengslene, for vi vet at trengselen virker tålmodighet, tålmodigheten prøvethet, og prøvetheten håp –Romerne 5:3-4. Noen ganger lurer vi på om dette skriftstedet kan være sant. Alle som har noen år på baken, kan vitne om vonde erfaringer og følelsen av håpløshet som følger etter. Som mennesker har vi alle opplevd skuffende erfaringer med en ektefelle, et barn eller et forhold i menigheten, og etterpå senker en gnagende fortvilelse seg som en sky. Utenfor Kristus fører en vond erfaring alltid gjerne til pessimisme. Slik var det i verden da Jesus kom. Slik er det fremdeles i dag.

Men ungdommens dugg er håpefull på en måte som ikke lar seg kurere. En sprudlende forventning blir naturlig og storslått født i ungdommen og bevares i Kristus. Hver vinter, når markene ligger øde og den kalde vinden suser gjennom trærne, finnes håpet om at blomstene skal spire igjen. Hver vår rommer håpet om sommer. Hver sommer rommer håpet om høst. Dette lever i naturen og i ungdommen. De som er blinde for det, vil i beste fall høste en trist, monoton tilværelse. Å leve er det sjeldneste i verden. De fleste mennesker eksisterer, det er alt. –Oscar Wilde.

De andre vil bli sterkt preget av et håp som …

…Legen våre skrøpeligheter

Kroppene våre er bestemt for graven, og det finnes ikke noe håp om fornyelse for dem i dette livet. Det er sinnet vårt som bærer på våre største skrøpeligheter. Den lamme mannen ved Betesda, som hadde vært syk i 38 år, kunne bare komme med en håpløs klage da Kristus spurte ham: …Vil du bli frisk? –Johannes 5:6. Ved inngangen til sin nye dag fikk han et nytt råd: …Se, du er blitt frisk. Synd ikke mer, for at ikke noe verre skal hende deg –Johannes 5:14. Hva kunne være verre enn å være lam i årevis? Et sinn som er plaget av en sørgmodig hengivelse til denne verdens sorger. Alderdommen setter inn når vi har flere minner om fortiden enn håp for morgendagen. Det er skuffende når folk blir gamle uten å ha noen visjon for morgendagen, men det er en katastrofe å se unge mennesker plaget av dens lammende virkninger. Mange famler formålsløst gjennom livets mange prøvelser, omtåket av mangelen på velsignelse. Middagssolen har fordampet ungdommens dugg, og den eneste lovprisningen de klarer å mønstre, henter de fra en håndfull hyggelige minner fra i går. En ny holdning må bli født av duggen fra en ny morgen.

…Ydmyker våre mål

Sannelig, sannelig sier jeg deg: Da du var ung, bandt du beltet om deg selv og gikk dit du ville. Men når du blir gammel, skal du rekke ut hendene, og en annen skal binde beltet om deg og føre deg dit du ikke vil. –Johannes 21:18. Når vi er unge, kan vi seire i ungdommens styrke. Etter hvert som alderen gjør sitt, finner vi en annen vei: seier gjennom overgivelse.

…Jeg har skrevet til dere, unge menn, fordi dere er sterke, og Guds ord blir i dere, og dere har seiret over den onde. –1. Johannes 2:14. Verden lokker oss til å leve egoistisk. Unge blir ofte underlagt utdanningssystemer som lærer dem å «bli alt dere kan bli». Hovedfokuset er på selvutvikling og forberedelse til framtiden. Dette kan forberede dem på en verden der den best tilpassede overlever, men det vil etterlate dem fattige når ungdommens styrke og kraft har forlatt dem.

For alt som er i verden, kjødets lyst og øynenes lyst og hovmodig skryt av det en eier, er ikke av Faderen, men av verden. Og verden forgår med sin lyst, men den som gjør Guds vilje, blir til evig tid. –1. Johannes 2:16-17. Å overvinne det onde med det gode er Bibelens motgift og en måte å kanalisere ungdommens krefter på. Enten det gjelder lysten i oss eller lengselen etter det som er utenfor oss, blir håpet unnfanget ved å så et vennlighetsfrø i et annet menneskes liv. Jakten på nytelse og søken etter fritid vil alltid skuffe den som får del i den, og etterlate ham i en fortvilelsens dal som er dypere enn da han begynte. Det er godt for en mann å bære åket i sin ungdom … Han legger munnen i støvet, om det ennå kunne være håp. –Klagesangene 3:27-29. Vi er skapt til å arbeide i Guds vingård, og de som har lyst til det, vil høste i håp om dens ungdommelige lønn.

…Helliggjør våre prøvelser

For i håpet er vi frelst. Men et håp som en ser, er ikke noe håp … –Romerne 8:24. Hvor ofte kan vi ikke kjenne oss igjen i Jobs smerte. Men før smerten hans hadde fått et gram av gjengjeldelse, begynte helbredende strømmer å flyte da Job æret sin Skaper. Når vi kan erkjenne at Gud er fullkommen i alle prøvelsene han tillater, lærer vi å tilbe i tempelet som ikke er gjort med hender, og å se bort fra kroppens skrøpelighet. Å sette seg ved Kristi føtter tenner en ungdommelig gnist som stråler ut fra ånden i oss og avler håp. Da blir ungdommens dugg vår del, idet Kristus gir oss evig liv og evig ungdom. Fra gravens stund og gjennom evigheten skal vi være unge og trosse tretthet og død, hvis vi lever i morgenlyset fra Jesus Kristus. Himmelen er et sted med evig ungdom, og slik månelyset gjenspeiler solens lys, gjenspeiler også Kristi brud Kristi lys. Hun er ren og ung, …en herlig menighet uten flekk eller rynke eller noe slikt … –Efeserne 5:27. Velsignet er den ærverdige helgenen som kommer til himmelens porter i en slik tilstand.
